This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Iran Death toll from U.S. strike on wedding in Sirik rises to five: The death toll from a U.S. attack on a wedding party in Sirik rose to five, Iranian state broadcaster IRIB reported on Thursday, after a 22-year-old woman died from her injuries. Four of the victims, including a 4-year-old and a 16-year-old, were buried in Kuhestak on Thursday in a funeral attended by a large number of mourners, relatives, military, and civilian officials, according to state media. U.S. strikes on Sirik wounded at least 60 people; 11 remain hospitalized and six are in an intensive care unit, according to IRIB. Iranian authorities report intercepting stockpiled weapons on Pakistan border: Iranian officials claimed they seized a "significant weapons cache" after a clash with militants at the Pakistan border, Iran's Fars news agency reported on Thursday, alleging that the weapons were being smuggled into the country to "carry out acts of sabotage and create insecurity." The cache included RPG-7 launchers, antitank RPG projectiles, RPG propellant charges, 2,382 rounds for AK-47 rifles, and 796 rounds for M4 rifles, according to a commander in Iran's border guard. IRGC arrests suspected Kurdish militants carrying munitions near Iraqi border: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said on Thursday that it arrested seven people allegedly carrying ammunition in the country's northwestern Ilam province, claiming the detainees belonged to a Kurdish separatist group and that they sought "to carry out armed operations" against the government. EU to join U.S. economic pressure campaign against Iran, Bessent claims: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced in a Thursday evening X post that the European Union had officially joined "Operation Economic Outcast," the U.S.'s economic pressure campaign against Iran, noting that the U.S. "appreciated" the body's "strong and early stance." The EU, however, has yet to announce participation. Bessent called the campaign a "clear message" to the Iranian government, and said that the pressure would not cease until Iran's "every remaining financial lifeline" was severed. The EU stated earlier that it would "work closely with the United States and other G7 and international partners to maintain pressure on Iran and contribute to de-escalation and regional stability." Vance addresses Iran "conflict" in briefing: At a White House press briefing, U.S. Vice President JD Vance addressed the U.S.'s ongoing war on Iran, rejecting calls for a timetable, ruling out negotiations, and leaving open the possibility of U.S. covert action. Vance to call the conflict a "war," saying that, at present, "there is no active shooting," while acknowledging recent strikes as part of a "flare-up." When asked whether the war would end before the midterms, Vance said he didn't know, but would not "set an artificial timeline." He also said that the U.S. was not presently negotiating with Iran, and would not talk to them "unless they stop shooting at commercial shipping." Vance said that the U.S. remained open to every means of fighting Iran, including arming dissidents. "Everything that could happen is on the table," he said, including "economic pressure, military pressure, diplomatic pressure, covert pressure." Vance also said China was "willing to play ball" with the U.S.'s campaign to isolate Iran, though he noted Beijing was not doing everything Washington had asked of it, and named Turkey, Azerbaijan, the UAE, Saudi Arabia and Qatar as countries privately helping apply pressure. The campaign was intended, in part, to prevent Iran from rebuilding its nuclear program, Vance , but acknowledged: "So far, we haven't seen them try to do so." Asked about the U.S. strike on a wedding gathering in Kuhestak, southern Iran, that killed five people and wounded 67, Vance he was "extremely skeptical" of the reports that the U.S. had intentionally or knowingly killed civilians. "The United States never targets civilians in combat. We never will do that. We never have done that, and unfortunately, obviously, sometimes things happen," he said. Iranian VP threatens "asymmetrical response" to U.S. attacks: Mohammed Reza Aref, Iran's first vice president, said in a on X that the United States had changed Tehran's security and defense calculations, warning Iran's next response would be "asymmetrical" and "multi-layered." "The Americans should start thinking about stockpiling gasoline and fuel," Aref warned. "Dark months await the American economy." Netanyahu says Israel remains committed to overthrowing Iran 's government; Katz threatens energy infrastructure: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu reportedly told senior Israeli officials that overthrowing Iran's leadership is his "next main mission," according to the Israeli newspaper Israel Hayom. Separately, Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz said that his country would strike Iran's energy and civilian infrastructure if Iran were to attack Israel, saying that such an attack would "free Israel from any existing limitations on attacking Iran." "We will cripple all of Iran's national military and civilian infrastructure--including energy infrastructure--and return Iran deep into the Stone Age and darkness," Katz threatened in a Thursday speech. South Korea reviews possible military deployment to Strait of Hormuz: South Korea is a possible deployment of military assets to the Strait of Hormuz amid pressure from Trump for allies to support operations in the region, The Guardian reported. The assets reportedly under consideration include a P-8 Poseidon maritime patrol aircraft, a naval logistics support ship, and an explosive ordnance disposal team. The presidential office, however, said "nothing related to the matter has been decided." South Korea relies heavily on the Strait of Hormuz, with more than 90% of its primary energy imported and about 70% of its crude oil passing through the waterway. Trump calls reporters "treasonous SCUM" over reports of low munitions: In response to recent reporting on the U.S.'s diminishing munitions stockpiles, which some experts have characterized as "dangerously low," Trump outlets that reported on the topic "treasonous SCUM" and claimed the reports were inaccurate, saying the U.S. was producing munitions at "levels never seen before" and has "far more than we could ever use." Palestine Israeli attacks kill two Palestinians in Gaza on Friday: One Palestinian was and "several others" wounded when an Israeli drone struck a group of people west of Khan Younis, WAFA reported. Another Palestinian was killed and three others wounded by Israeli gunfire north of the city. Israeli forces kill Palestinian in East Jerusalem, shoot and wound children in Bethlehem: East Jerusalem: Israeli police Ibrahim Al-Hindi, 33, from Beit Hanina, near Damascus Gate early Friday,, according to WAFA. Police reportedly claimed he had attempted to stab an officer. His killing brings the number of Palestinians killed in the Jerusalem governorate this year to 17. Bethlehem : Two Palestinian children were shot and wounded with live ammunition during an Israeli raid on Beit Fajjar, south of Bethlehem in the occupied West Bank, on Thursday evening. Ramallah: Settlers a tent Friday near Palestinian homes in Umm Safa, northwest of Ramallah, after dozens attacked a resident's home and property under Israeli military protection, WAFA reported. Israeli forces closed the main entrance to Al-Mughayyir, northeast of Ramallah, where two Palestinian teens were killed by Israeli gunfire on Wednesday, preventing residents from entering or leaving, as settlers encroached on Palestinian land east of the village. The United Nations the teens' killings brings the number of Palestinians killed by Israeli forces and settlers in the village since December 2024 to nine, including five boys. The UN said Al-Mughayyir, surrounded by eight settlement outposts, has faced "incessant settler and state violence" aimed at forcing Palestinians from the area. Fourth person killed in Nazareth in 24 hours: A young Palestinian man was shot dead in Nazareth on Thursday, the fourth person killed in the city within 24 hours. His killing brought the number of Palestinian citizens of Israel killed in violent crime this year to 158, amid continued criticism of Israeli police and the government over their failure to investigate most killings and hold those responsible to account. Israeli police said they arrested 30 people in two overnight operations on Thursday and Friday, claiming dozens of officers "stormed several compounds belonging to gangs" and, "in several cases," chased and arrested suspects. Israeli prison guards beat Dr. Hussam Abu Safiya, injuring his head, face, and chest: Israeli prison guards repeatedly detained Palestinian doctor Hussam Abu Safiya with hands, feet and batons, the Palestinian Center for Prisoners' Defense said, citing a new message through his lawyer. Abu Safiya, director of Gaza's Kamal Adwan Hospital, said guards deprive him of sleep with noise and loudspeakers at night and threaten him against revealing his prison conditions. He also reported being assaulted after lawyers' visits, suggesting retaliation for speaking out. The center said he has injuries to his head, face, chest and left eye while being denied medical care and called for urgent UN, Red Cross, and WHO intervention. UN report: Israel violated international law when it expelled Palestinian refugees from three West Bank camps: A new UN Human Rights says Israeli security forces forcibly displaced the entire Palestinian populations of the Jenin, Nur Shams, and Tulkarm refugee camps in the occupied West Bank in January and February 2025 and are still preventing their return. "Operation Iron Wall" killed civilians, destroyed hundreds of homes, damaged roads and other infrastructure, cut off water and electricity and barred humanitarian access, the report said, as Israeli forces went door to door forcing residents to leave. "The way Operation Iron Wall has been conducted suggests its aim was to expel as many Palestinians as possible and to make way for more illegal Israeli settlements, in further violation of international law," said UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Turk. Amnesty: Israel escalates West Bank annexation with first civil land seizures in Area A: Israel is escalating its annexation of the occupied West Bank by confiscating land in Area A under Palestinian Authority control, according to a from Amnesty International. The rights group said the Israeli military issued at least 15 confiscation orders in July covering about 200 dunams (20 hectares) in the Jenin Governorate, across Areas A and C, to connect the planned settlements of Emek Dotan and Noa. According to Peace Now, this marks "the first time since the Oslo Accords that military seizure orders have been issued in Area A openly for civil purposes benefiting settlers rather than for ostensible security reasons." "These latest confiscation orders from Area A show how Israel is now brazenly expanding its annexation agenda to areas that have been under the control of the Palestinian authorities since the Oslo Accords," Amnesty said. Luxembourg declines to renew authorization for Israel bonds: Luxembourg's financial regulator did not renew its authorization for Israeli bonds after it expired on Monday, complicating Israel's ability to raise funds from investors across European markets, Anadolu Agency . Israel can still seek approval from another EU member state to continue marketing the bonds in Europe. DRC announces plans to move Israel embassy to Jerusalem: The Democratic Republic of the Congo plans to move its embassy in Israel from Tel Aviv to Jerusalem. Israel claims the entire city as its capital, while Palestinians seek occupied East Jerusalem as the capital of a future Palestinian state. The UN Security Council has rejected measures seeking to alter Jerusalem's status and called on countries not to establish diplomatic missions in the city. Yemen Al Jazeera: More than 100 killed in Yemen clashes in past 48 hours: At least 100 fighters have been killed in clashes between Yemen's Ansarallah and Saudi-backed government forces in the past 48 hours, according to Al Jazeera. A military official told AFP 24 government fighters were killed near the western coast, while another said 15 were killed in fighting around Taiz. Medical sources in areas controlled by Ansarallah reported at least 42 Ansarallah fighters killed. Yemen 's Saudi-backed forces claim they regained territory: Heavy clashes are ongoing between Yemeni's Saudi-backed government forces and Ansarallah fighters in Taiz governorate, with government forces claiming they repelled Ansarallah attacks in Maqbanah and Al-Kudhah and regained some territory that had briefly fallen to the group, Al Jazeera reported. Ansarallah has been pushing west of Taiz towards the road linking the city with the Red Sea port of Al-Makha, in an apparent attempt to cut supply routes to government forces there. Lebanon Israeli forces carry out explosions and shell southern Lebanon despite "ceasefire": Israeli forces explosions in Al-Mansouri in the Tyre (Sour) governorate on Friday, Lebanon's National News Agency reported, while Israeli artillery shelling in Zawtar Al-Sharqiyah, in the Nabatieh governorate. Israel claims control of Ali Taher Ridge as Katz vows to remain in southern Lebanon until Hezbollah disarms: The Israeli military it had taken control of the Ali Taher Ridge near Nabatieh and cleared two major tunnel routes it described as a Hezbollah "nerve center," The Times of Israel reported. Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz the operation marked "the completion of the phase of establishing control over the security zone in southern Lebanon," and vowed Israel "will not withdraw" until Hezbollah is disarmed. Hezbollah-affiliated MP Ihab Hamadeh Israel's account, saying there remained "ambiguity" over whether Israeli forces had actually taken control of the ridge. He said Israel had provided no images showing its forces inside the facility and argued that continued Israeli strikes on the area raised questions about its claim of full control. Israel releases five Lebanese detainees as ICRC calls for better access: Israel released five Lebanese detainees since Thursday, including four handed over at the Ras Al-Naqoura crossing on Friday. The ICRC transferred the four to a Lebanese army barracks in Tyre (Sour). Among those released was a man who had been detained for more than two months. Lebanese President Joseph Aoun the U.S., President Donald Trump, and international parties, particularly the ICRC, for efforts leading to what he called the release of the "first batch" of Lebanese detainees. Dozens of Lebanese citizens are reportedly being detained in Israeli jails. The ICRC it has been unable to access detainees in Israeli detention facilities since October 2023, including Lebanese nationals, and reiterated its demand for access to them. U.S. News House GOP cancels final two weeks of pre-election session : Republican leaders the House will cancel its final two pre-election weeks of legislative business, meaning members will leave Washington by September 17 and not return until mid-November. Speaker Mike Johnson attributed the shortened calendar to a Senate backlog of nearly 600 House-passed bills, and to pre-midterm political pressures, arguing "many [members] want and need to be in their districts, working with their constituents, and running their campaigns." GOP leaders indicated they would recall members to Washington only if the Senate advances a party-line budget reconciliation package, which is not currently expected. U.S. shifts to weekly deportation flights to Haiti as violence worsens : The U.S. government more than 100 people to Haiti on Thursday, landing in Cap-Haitien, the third such flight in three weeks. The U.S. has sent deportees from a Louisiana facility to Cap-Haitien rather than to the country's capital, Port-au-Prince, because of gang violence. Gangs control an estimated 70% of the city. Violence in the country displaced nearly 1.5 million people nationwide and killed more than 3,050 from January to June, according to the U.N. Missouri Supreme Court blocks congressional map in rare setback for GOP redistricting : The Missouri Supreme Court unanimously the state's new, Trump-backed congressional maps from being used in November and ordered a statewide referendum on redistricting, following a petition campaign which garnered 30,000 signatures. The map that the court jettisoned was used in the state's August primaries. Republicans hoped that map would help them net an additional House seat, with Democratic Rep. Emanuel Cleaver 's Kansas City-based district dramatically redrawn. Trump administration proposes IRS rules revoking tax-exempt status from schools with race-based support programs: The Treasury Department proposed regulations Thursday that would strip tax-exempt status from any school, including universities, found by the IRS to have admissions, scholarship, or other policies deemed racially "discriminatory" toward white or Asian American students. The policy, which could apply to as many as 18,000 schools, relies upon a 1983 Supreme Court case which allows the IRS to revoke tax-exempt status from organizations in opposition to "fundamental public policy." It also follows the Supreme Court's 2023 ruling in the Students for Fair Admissions case. American Association of University Professors President Todd Wolfson called the move "blatantly racist political coercion" and said the group is likely to sue. Florida bans undocumented students from state universities: Florida's Board of Governors unanimously to bar undocumented students from enrolling in state universities starting in the 2027-28 academic year, making Florida the largest state to enact such a ban and joining Alabama, Georgia, and South Carolina, the South Florida Sun-Sentinel reported. The vote follows a June decision by the State Board of Education banning undocumented immigrants from Florida's 28 state colleges and adult education programs, and comes after the state already ended in-state tuition waivers for these students. At least 4,672 undocumented students were enrolled in state colleges in 2024-25, with an estimated 2,000 more at state universities. U.S. House passes bill that would penalize universities for boycotting Israel: The House of Representatives passed a bill on Thursday that would bar federal funds from American universities that boycott Israel or its academic institutions, including those located in the occupied West Bank. The body approved the measure in a 237-169 vote on Thursday, with 33 Democrats, including Jake Auchincloss , Gil Cisneros , Jared Moskowitz , Jimmy Pannetta , Debbie Wasserman Schultz , and Juan Vargas , joining the Republican majority. Republicans Warren Davidson and Thomas Massie broke ranks with their party to reject the bill. The bill needs the approval of the Republican-controlled Senate and the signature of the president to become law. Trump names Adam Telle acting Army secretary after Driscoll 's resignation: President Donald Trump Thursday evening that Adam Telle , currently assistant secretary of the Army for Civil Works, would become acting Army secretary "effective immediately." The appointment follows the resignation of Dan Driscoll , whose departure this week capped months of internal clashes with War Secretary Pete Hegseth over his broader push to reshape Army leadership. Telle previously served as Sen. Bill Hagerty 's chief of staff and worked in the White House Office of Legislative Affairs during Trump's first term. Missouri GOP candidate charged with plotting to plant drugs on political opponent: The Justice Department charges against Thomas Ross , 37, a Republican candidate for Missouri state representative, alleging he instructed his former campaign manager to plant cocaine and Adderall on his primary opponent,Louise Secker , whom he defeated by just 33 votes last month. The head of the Missouri GOP has called for Ross to drop out of the race. 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com Other International News Global food prices hit four-year high, UN says: The UN Food and Agriculture Organization's Food Price Index for a third straight month to 133.3 points in August, its highest level since late 2022, with every tracked category--cereals, vegetable oils, sugar, meat, and dairy--rising over the month. FAO chief economist Maximo Torero said "climate shocks, geopolitical tensions and disrupted trade logistics are converging to tighten supply expectations," with sugar rising fastest, up nearly 12% to a one-year high. Cereal prices climbed more than 2% to a two-year high, a result of strikes in the Black Sea, a major route for Russian grain exporters. The risks are compounded by global warming and the return of El Niño, which contributed to reduced crop yields amid European heatwaves this summer. The weather pattern also threatens production across Asia, with the World Food Programme warning the phenomenon could push another 50 million people into acute hunger by the end of next year. U.S. sanctions Ra ul Castro's grandson, five Cuban companies amid economic pressure campaign: The U.S. State Department new sanctions on five Cuban companies and Fidel Ernesto Castro, the 31-year-old grandson of 95-year-old revolutionary leader Raul Castro. Washington sanctioned the state-owned Banco Exterior de Cuba, two nickel mining companies, and two energy-sector firms including an oil importer, with Secretary of State Marco Rubio accusing Cuban leaders of enriching themselves while seeking "to export subversive Marxist ideology to the United States." Cuban Foreign Minister Bruno Rodriguez countered that "Cuba does not threaten U.S. national security or the U.S. economy." "The accusation that Cuba allegedly sponsors terrorism actually reveals the U.S. government's lack of seriousness," he added. A U.S. oil blockade imposed earlier this year has worsened Cuba's power grid failures and prompted UN warnings of a humanitarian crisis on the island. Cuba unveils new market reforms to attract foreign investment amid U.S.-driven crisis: Cuba 34 pages of new regulations Thursday aimed at attracting foreign investment, trade, and tourism, part of ongoing free-market reforms adopted under pressure from Washington and a deepening economic crisis driven by punishing U.S. sanctions. The regulations follow a package of 176 reforms announced in June, widely considered the largest overhaul of Cuba's socialist economic model since the 1959 revolution. Ukrainian security service and military clash in Kyiv: Ukraine's security service and military intelligence agency gunfire in Kyiv on Wednesday, reportedly wounding three officers. The clash between the Security Service of Ukraine (SBU) and Defence Intelligence of the Ministry of Defence of Ukraine (GUR) broke out the night of September 2 over the detention of Stepan Kaplunov, deputy commander of the Russian Volunteer Corps, an anti-Kremlin Russian unit fighting for Ukraine under military intelligence. The SBU said its officers came under armed attack while investigating a Russian assassination plot. A GUR commander accused SBU personnel of opening fire on unarmed intelligence officers without warning. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy ordered an investigation and dismissed senior SBU official Oleh Khramov. "Here in Ukraine, shooting is only permissible at Russian occupiers," he said. Russian drone strikes Kyiv headquarters: A Russian drone the headquarters of Ukraine's security service, on Volodymyrska Street across from St. Sophia Cathedral, injuring at least five people, according to Ukrainian officials. Zelenskyy said the drone was aimed directly at the office of SBU chief Oleksandr Poklad, but did not disclose whether he was present. Zelenskyy ordered the SBU to prepare "an appropriate, tangible response" against Russia, saying the retaliation should, where possible, mirror the strike and would receive support from Ukraine's military. UAE pardons imprisoned dissident Abdulrahman Al-Qaradawi: The president of the United Arab Emirates has pardoned Egyptian-Turkish poet and political dissident Abdulrahman Yusuf Al-Qaradawi one week after he was sentenced to 10 years in prison and a fine of AED200,000 ($54,452), to The National. Qaradawi was first detained in Lebanon in December 2024 on charges related to a video he posted to social media while visiting Syria in which he criticized the governments of Egypt, Saudi Arabia and the UAE. Both Egypt and the UAE issued extradition requests for Qaradawi and he was deported to Abu Dhabi less than two weeks later and remained forcibly disappeared for over 200 days in what human rights groups called a flagrant violation of human rights and due process. Read Drop Site's coverage of Qaradawi's case . Haitian FM urges UN to renew international force mandate: Haiti's Foreign Minister Raina Forbin the UN Security Council Thursday to extend the 12-month mandate of an international force supporting Haitian police "as soon as possible" before it expires this month, saying stronger backing is essential for the country to hold its first election since 2016. Court orders arrest of Philippines VP Sara Duterte over alleged assassination threat: A Quezon City court a warrant Friday for the arrest of Philippines Vice President Sara Duterte over allegations she arranged to have President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., his wife, and former House Speaker Martin Romualdez killed. Duterte is facing an ongoing Senate impeachment trial over the same threats--a case that, if it results in a guilty verdict, would remove her from office and quash her 2028 presidential ambitions. Duterte's lawyer, Paul Lawrence Lim, said she has "no intention of evading the law," and officials expect her to post bail quickly rather than face detention. body:
That cemetery is where my father is buried, as well as men I trained and served alongside
#
Peter, they just told us when they’re beginning construction on the Arc de Trump:
[](https://act.votevets.org/go/2927?c0=vv-pac-em-sep26.f1bOKp&refcode=em260904-1-180&t=1&akid=35540%2E3013755%2EVoqeGm)
Two weeks. That's how long we have before they break ground.
Back in June, a federal commission packed with Trump appointees voted 8 to 1 to advance this thing, after hearing nearly three hours of public opposition first. That same commission still hasn’t voted on final approval, with their next meeting scheduled for October 1st.
Trump wants to put the graves of our honored dead at Arlington in his shadow. That cemetery is where my father is buried, as well as men I trained and served alongside. It is among the most sacred places in the country. It is not the backdrop for this draft-dodging coward’s vanity project.
So we're asking for $5. That's it.
$5 because they've given us two weeks, and that is not a lot of time.
$5 because we're up against a President who's made this one of the top priorities of his administration — and today, he got himself a start date.
But really, $5 or anything you can afford. Because whatever you can give, right now, matters more than the amount itself.

| Dear Peter,

[](https://click.everyaction.com/k/138572618/644487630/-1735968383?sourceid=1151571&utm_campaign=27emcge-0901-aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=dcf&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwODAwMTBiYi03OWE4LWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTkzM2IiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=Nme6NrZPavXLoicmR8AZmzQ8MqzO_cAELu0a-9DT5LI=&emci=c99befb5-23a7-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&emdi=080010bb-79a8-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&ceid=954237)

[The funding is extraordinary, and so was the chance to connect with thousands of people like you who care deeply about reproductive rights, and the Center's work.](https://click.everyaction.com/k/138572673/644487718/-1735968383?sourceid=1151571&utm_campaign=27emcge-0901-aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=dcf&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwODAwMTBiYi03OWE4LWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTkzM2IiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=Nme6NrZPavXLoicmR8AZmzQ8MqzO_cAELu0a-9DT5LI=&emci=c99befb5-23a7-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&emdi=080010bb-79a8-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&ceid=954237)

At our booth, festivalgoers customized bandanas, explored our interactive "Does Your State Love You or Love You Not?" map, and learned more about the state of reproductive rights across the country. [More than 600 people added stickers to their home states, sparking conversations about what reproductive freedom looks like where they live.](https://click.everyaction.com/k/138572689/644487811/-1735968383?sourceid=1151571&utm_campaign=27emcge-0901-aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=dcf&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwODAwMTBiYi03OWE4LWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTkzM2IiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=Nme6NrZPavXLoicmR8AZmzQ8MqzO_cAELu0a-9DT5LI=&emci=c99befb5-23a7-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&emdi=080010bb-79a8-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&ceid=954237)

This was a proud moment for the Center, and it wouldn't have been possible without Olivia Rodrigo's vision and the incredible community that showed up. We're grateful to be part of it — and energized to keep the momentum going.

Onward!

Nancy Northup

Republicans have a serious problem heading into November: Donald Trump.

This one gets me fired up. But there's an important warning here too: **none of this is guaranteed.**

[ stdin# ]Our Revolution Logo

Peter Willis,

The front page of the New York Times just sounded the alarm: at least $1
BILLION in anonymous dark money is flooding the midterms — touching nearly
EVERY SINGLE RACE.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/39588?source=email-20260904&t=1011&akid=11276%2E5885482%2EH1634a ]Headline: Millions of Dollars in Secret Spending Could Upend the 2026
Midterms. Subheadline: At least $1 billion from anonymous donors is
flowing into the midterm elections. Dark money is not new, but it now
permeates nearly every major contest.

To fight back, over the next *eight weeks* our organizers, volunteers, and
members like you are striving to reach FIVE MILLION voter contacts at the
doors and on the phones to out-organize Big Money at the ballot box.

But that’s not all.

We’re also leading the only inside strategy that can *fix* the rigged
system itself. The DNC is on the brink of banning dark and corporate money
from the 2028 presidential primaries, but it all comes down to what
happens in the next few weeks — and it’s going to take ALL of us to make
sure they do it.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/39588?source=email-20260904&t=1012&akid=11276%2E5885482%2EH1634a ]SIGN NOW: Demand that the DNC finally ban dark and corporate money from
Democratic primaries.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/39588?source=email-20260904&t=1013&akid=11276%2E5885482%2EH1634a ]ADD YOUR NAME

In Michigan and Minnesota, tens of millions in untraceable cash tried to
crush progressive Senate candidates. In Texas, our opponents used secret
funds to boost a candidate they knew couldn’t win. And now dark money is
covering the airwaves, threatening to drown out real grassroots
organizing.

Let’s be clear: the system is completely broken, and overturning Citizens
United is the long game, but it’s not happening soon. So in the meantime,
we have work to do.

Thousands of Our Revolution supporters already pushed the DNC to pass a
historic resolution last year to ban super PAC and corporate cash from
funding our presidential primaries. The DNC promised an implementation
plan, but August came and went. Now, we need to send a clear message to
the corporate-backed establishment — the power of democratic voters won’t
let you stop us.

Ken Martin has been championing this effort but needs to implement it in
the next few weeks, well before presidential primaries kick off in 2028.
And we can show the party that the grassroots will not let Big Money
choose our next nominee.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/39588?source=email-20260904&t=1014&akid=11276%2E5885482%2EH1634a ]This is a fight we can actually win if we flood the DNC with grassroots
demand. Add your name and send a message straight to the DNC calling for a
plan to ban dark money from the primaries.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/39588?source=email-20260904&t=1015&akid=11276%2E5885482%2EH1634a ]ADD YOUR NAME

If we want to protect future candidates from billionaire PACs, super PACs,
and cynical corporate front groups, we need your voice RIGHT NOW.

When we organize, we win.

| Dear Fairfax County Friends and Neighbors,
Thank you again for the encouragement, signatures, and support that helped put me on the ballot for Congressional District 8. I am grateful for everyone who has stepped forward, shared the news, and asked how they can help in this next phase of the campaign.
If you would like to learn more about my campaign and the issues I am raising in this race, ARLnow recently published an article outlining my priorities and why I am running: [Libertarian takes on Rep. Beyer, pledging to cut government waste, support civil liberties.](https://5f9eawebb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001HwmGx9oaXYkETjWNCOAP_klTmKU54OBU_k9cskLBCT0b9eIA7tQgSM8nmC4ap5mhJZABjfWz46q4lgJrqrwBZewZqs4hETMJ84cWGkLbmf3BWRkao2rXDuAd0qQZbm7BXhNB-tZt7lT93ZDgc1I22pRrmT5b4zqCp6erma49i3DnwOBeY8ZHnXU43Zt3KMYvESqUzG10Mr-LGkST6AoIZctUm_CWCYEyW3wcGl9hNwtLZmht99SegrJ6tLGjKyfLZqok87p2Tj1G1ilikIB8Xw==&c=TyN3YboSVvva_Z0jPjGhh3rHh54elNkh6cSh2Ya5UYahGFWxdsXyEg==&ch=Q03JpndkpREx9hGYrHeEshQB9gH73-413RyZwbIHU885XBlNfp-o-w==)
I also invite you to come see me live at the annual candidates forum on Tuesday, Sept. 8, during the [Arlington County Civic Federation General Meeting](https://5f9eawebb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001HwmGx9oaXYkETjWNCOAP_klTmKU54OBU_k9cskLBCT0b9eIA7tQgSM8nmC4ap5mhEHYVyfshQiGp8P9RiJGwuLt3QCrJqu53sea5vd0iK2DpzwPDfqRJJTZmF-2HCXqwbGA5NwKo0ijs6y1ikpUG2Q==&c=TyN3YboSVvva_Z0jPjGhh3rHh54elNkh6cSh2Ya5UYahGFWxdsXyEg==&ch=Q03JpndkpREx9hGYrHeEshQB9gH73-413RyZwbIHU885XBlNfp-o-w==). This will be an important opportunity to hear directly from the candidates and to ask questions about the future of our district.
Campaign signs are on order and should arrive soon. If you would like to put one in your yard, send me a DM or email, and I will find a way to get it to you.
You can also join my fight by volunteering your time, sharing my information on social media, and introducing me to friends and neighbors who want a different kind of representation. Peter, I went back and forth on if I should send you this or not. Not because I didn't know what to say, but because I knew how much it would hurt to say it. It’s difficult to admit that I can't do this alone. [**There's so much weighing on me right now, and finding the right words feels impossible. But I'm trusting these words will reach you the way they need to.**](https://links.iterable.com/s/c/zmi2iUcox11E34O7fkbFu1oI8BSG_mvnsZdcYG6_bUdwMr0LluhjGtGttw0cvD7IW7KY0tuInFFNYSREb3F8mkUSWYKErmuQvkgJaIbu1xJg2PT4ZITiLdr5RTGAT3u06g8dRIboKkJAiroSgkUYnIoULAGkBfkehX98P8k9eRCEkoopVNfthqL_Q1X5CbLQ__rVKOsoXCx3XYuul2okf1lJf6x-A25Sd8Viw4lqVzxxO8O1p67bbL0aVpnkpbQsqWqkJHQTH94qv_RGEH-hEVZKO69St9q1RqtgMWWC78TjkHi_mdRfptEl91UAD1Zy1IqGCI0v95EIl7aJDNi_qFnGMO-tI0EeqIWf0q8e2N-F0FVM-5xhWhVQpOn2PDS6CtUe0DSxjflMl6qu4N5DAyOQ7m8fY5QVZ5W3lXbKtSXwjS4Fr6tVEc9KhcwByLXUNtA9_sNIR3E_J-ucmDnkLDNntClWYXJyS-41S0t44M_l6K9192G9HKLfe4A96EIdv12i9fF-hLaN0HK0dlN3C978_FBcnhwdUGPjhXdO3FDXRuV1izxD0dGEi5eFTvD1lrGxrqDaySbkxr1Sw_meDptITI7VRi4gVnedpelxEOgBux0--i2qOftFnhvFywhCWV6eQeEGdud9XqXtgfBAjQDpucY7zo9tTXeoC3TTnDTvjlrCfqctgj7fiH1A3Tx7JIaXKKezYoQIaCyf6fiuFdpzR2dS9Y6WH5CwFEElpwDYyFN4tjFNHFh9ll2DAsjzzEnOiZccXvjjArKAwyUUo_YGTr0Wzd1-a-2Req9LX5g0uUY/bPsXRxTRGMJvfD4M5ZLviB7dfk4TFBfr/24) It’s Congressman Brandon Gill. Working cows and driving tractors growing up made me who I am today. It taught me the value of hard work, the importance of keeping your word, and what it means to sacrifice for something bigger than yourself. Trust me, I know all the constant emails and texts can weigh on you. It wears on me too. Some days I wonder if it's worth it. But then I remember why I'm here. I didn't come to Washington because I love asking true patriots like you for money. I didn't run for Congress at 29 years old to become the youngest House Republican so I could spend my nights begging for donations. I came because my kids deserve to grow up in a better America than I grew up in — and right now, that's not guaranteed. Being a husband and a father are the two most important things in my life. Sometimes, when I'm holding my kids, I feel like I'm holding the whole world in my arms. They're everything to me. They're the wind in my sails when it comes to the mission I've committed my life and career to. And at the end of my life, I want to sit before the Father Almighty and declare that I did all I could to leave this great country better off than it was when I grew up. I refuse to look my kids in the eye someday and tell them I gave up when it mattered most. [**That's why I'm still here. That's why I keep sending these messages.**](https://links.iterable.com/s/c/0UV4xL0GCfSwKqOpvciv11W72ut-BceMLuLMEpps3KXx2ebcfdfXqUREB6QIkxlRhUhF1wFxgpFXizG9bLMmQASoPI5pVw_jrFViBpedz7DyI5-5sYZMRaVusQAG-NsSEcb1T0aSpTOPTo3l0I02nrme8P95UyLMNWxEBRq2R93Hq7JpVLEtRyHfnp16RQqG08bU0ea9ZgCX3X4H39VNxz5bsgoxsh3Az8KvH8-jglU-9hXBcEEMvE_ct8w9VDhrA567wuWqsCjKmB4iseo19KxUtgITeqv0YVhFw3yEf7czFW3-qUKXbbW0GQnRw4TH57PhJMd1GRozmzQsVfSu50SLmc_jf5Kf9aw2A0i2-XPe3RRivQ3Cv2VzuibDrybjC1vYironYjzwWLaV-LFw2LiJZ2wOyRZ6U8eJIJHOA4Ia3pqX_U1M7Jv1dfKnX0GqjFZ9d81Jfx-acljxv1ydCneFXpnOW69y34ZiDPTIZStQgngSFyIEtXaiitaaVSjF4DeUlGGVbk8XcHysKDyOzb_6tyLr5so_tfqt2OM7Nl7Q44RYRFwRjhbCmPwHf9QLSbVNXrxWvFiKurvgdmOw0tstPOEW9932paYjby2bqZWbVFT4-7hl6EKWdoEkFnndDb4C_9w-ofxHIU3b2dG1hrOoyMmCVmYInc9AwrNoxteJEi2Uh2p3vuQM4i3IKAlYJWfyzIoMDbI6iFd-gC6vat5hXRqqgBwSPVOU7WBFUbzDd9heNaARlRR9CNyL_axTebyu2iwXfXrGA7ND1-94PW4yY8-suuJtc5d-BbeW-3U4y54/jjzUBNC9tR_posx8ViwgCkZRDVCnw09D/24) Because nothing — I repeat — nothing is more important to me than fighting off the vicious leftist attacks against the soul of our country. The left hates you. They hate your vote. They hate MAGA for putting America First. And they will do anything — lie, cheat, steal, destroy — to ensure your children inherit a country you won't even recognize. Peter, today I'll make the same promise to you that I've made to myself, to my wife, and to my children: As long as I live, I will continue to FIGHT to preserve the soul of our country. No force on Earth will push me to abandon my mission and calling. Not the attacks. Not the exhaustion. Not the constant pressure to give up and go home. Believe me, I'm not someone who finds it easy to ask for support. Texting and emailing you like this is the last thing I thought I'd have to do when I ran for Congress. But the country we love is on the brink of destruction, and God has put it on my heart to fight with all that I have — even when that means swallowing my pride and asking for help. The battle for the heart and soul of Texas is underway.
As we get closer and closer to election day, Democrats are going to flood your inbox, your phone, the airwaves, and your mailbox with manufactured lies to get you to turn your back on the Republican Party.
These ads, funded by dark money groups and out of state billionaires looking to sway Texans to vote for the most radical slate of Democrat candidates in the history of Texas, are blanketing our state.
In California and New York, Zohran Mamdani and Gavin Newscum are scheming with their coastal elite billionaire backers as they look down on Texas like buzzards ready to devour us.
**Texas is the crown jewel of the United States because of the** **Texas Miracle. That’s why Democrats nationwide are laser focused on winning our state.**
Mamdani, AOC, Newscum, Talarico, and Radical Rosenthal are all members of the same brood.
These snakes, if they have it their way, will shutter the Texas Oil and Gas industry and your life will get measurably worse in every single way.
The only well Radical Rosenthal wants to plug is the well from which Texas prosperity flows: our entire Oil and Gas industry.
**What happens if Democrats win this November?**
Prices will explode at the pump, shipping costs will skyrocket and groceries will get more expensive.
Democrats will immediately begin nonenforcement of immigration laws and will force Law Enforcement agencies to stop cooperating with ICE.
Illegals will flood Texas as Democrats marshal our state’s resources to bring and settle them in your neighborhood.
Mortgages, rent and insurance will increase overnight as migrants take over our state and crime increases dramatically.
**_In short, if Democrats win Texas, literally every aspect of your life will quickly be made worse._**
Since you are a Patriot, I know that I can trust you with anything.
As hundreds of millions in out-of-state Democrat dollars continue to pour into our state, I need your help getting my message out, because if Democrats win, it's game over for America.
Last week, my opponent Radical Rosenthal announced that his polls have our race tied.
I know I can count on you to keep Texas Red.
Every dollar you donate goes straight to reaching voters. Every $100 you give puts my message in front of another 3,220 Texans who need to hear the truth about Radical Rosenthal before November.
friend, I don't take your support for granted. If you are receiving this email, I already know you are one of my top patriots.
I will keep traveling this state, meeting Texans like you, and getting the message out to the millions of voters across Texas.
Now I need you to do your part.
**_If you believe Texas oil and gas should stay in Texan hands. . . and that the Texas Miracle belongs to YOU, not Radical Rosenthal's billionaire backers. . . then prove it with a donation today._**

In California and New York, Zohran Mamdani and Gavin Newscum are scheming with their coastal elite billionaire backers as they look down on Texas like buzzards ready to devour us. Texas is the crown jewel of the United States because of the Texas Miracle. That’s why Democrats nationwide are laser focused on winning our state. Mamdani, AOC, Newscum, Talarico, and Radical Rosenthal are all members of the same brood. These snakes, if they have it their way, will shutter the Texas Oil and Gas industry and your life will get measurably worse in every single way. The only well Radical Rosenthal wants to plug is the well from which Texas prosperity flows: our entire Oil and Gas industry. What happens if Democrats win this November? Prices will explode at the pump, shipping costs will skyrocket and groceries will get more expensive. Democrats will immediately begin nonenforcement of immigration laws and will force Law Enforcement agencies to stop cooperating with ICE. Illegals will flood Texas as Democrats marshal our state’s resources to bring and settle them in your neighborhood. Mortgages, rent and insurance will increase overnight as migrants take over our state and crime increases dramatically. In short, if Democrats win Texas, literally every aspect of your life will quickly be made worse. Since you are a Patriot, I know that I can trust you with anything. As hundreds of millions in out-of-state Democrat dollars continue to pour into our state, I need your help getting my message out, because if Democrats win, it's game over for America. Last week, my opponent Radical Rosenthal announced that his polls have our race tied. I know I can count on you to keep Texas Red. Every dollar you donate goes straight to reaching voters. Every $100 you give puts my message in front of another 3,220 Texans who need to hear the truth about Radical Rosenthal before November. friend, I don't take your support for granted. If you are receiving this email, I already know you are one of my top patriots. I will keep traveling this state, meeting Texans like you, and getting the message out to the millions of voters across Texas. Now I need you to do your part. If you believe Texas oil and gas should stay in Texan hands. . . and that the Texas Miracle belongs to YOU, not Radical Rosenthal's billionaire backers. . . then prove it with a donation today. I'm going to make a prediction...

When the votes are counted this November, the radical left is going to be in a state of total shock.

_The Democrats are at war with the American people -- open borders, defunding ICE, eliminating voter ID, putting men in women's sports._

You name it, they are on the wrong side of it.

And yet they are running the most radical, well-funded Senate candidates in states across this country who are counting on Republicans to stay home and let them walk right in.

I will not let that happen. And I don't think you will either.

name: JusticeDemocrats.com
subject: Where do you stand on AI and data centers?
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY JUSTICE DEMOCRATS
body:
[1]Justice Democrats

Peter,

The rise of artificial intelligence (AI) and the data centers that power
it have taken our country by storm over the last few years. Now, it’s
becoming a key issue in our elections:

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140957?c0=jd-em-20260904.CXWgtY&source=em20260904-38231&t=1002&akid=38231%2E1203867%2EGVn8LS ]Screenshot of multiple headlines regarding data centers. AP News
headline: "In a divided America, the left and right unite to oppose
artificial intelligence data centers" ; News of the United States
headline: "A Democratic Reckoning on Data Centers Is Coming" ; CNN
headline: "A uniquely bipartisan backlash against data centers shakes up
the midterms"

AI lobby groups and Silicon Valley super PACs are already vying to become
the biggest spender in politics: so far, they’ve raised $200 million and
spent $57 million in federal races this cycle alone.

As Big Tech companies roll out more AI-based tools that threaten job
security and public health, while building massive energy and
water-guzzling data centers that pollute neighborhoods, voters across the
political spectrum are decisively uniting against them.

At first, many Democrat and Republican leaders were competing in the AI
race, fast-tracking data center development and letting corporations get
away with buying up land, building with little regulation, and stealing
water and electricity from communities without paying for it.

Now, both parties are reevaluating their approach ahead of the midterms as
they witness the massive public pushback: A brand new YouGov poll shows
that nearly two-thirds of people in the U.S. oppose data center
construction in their community.

Rural areas, suburban towns, and cities of all shapes and sizes are
standing up and fighting to ban data centers from being built in their
backyards. Just look at Memphis, where Justice Democrat Justin J. Pearson
is leading the fight against Elon Musk’s Colossus data center cluster
that’s creating both air and noise pollution for the surrounding poor and
working-class residents.

Many localities and several states have already passed bans on new data
center development. Some Democratic leaders have been wary of this
technology and its public impacts since the beginning. Some are changing
their tune with the polls. And others are sticking by their Big Tech
megadonors and pushing for as little regulation as possible.

As this becomes a bigger issue not only in this election cycle but for the
2028 presidential election ahead of us, we want to know where you
stand, Peter.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140957?c0=jd-em-20260904.CXWgtY&source=em20260904-38231&t=1003&akid=38231%2E1203867%2EGVn8LS ]Will you take a few minutes to fill out our AI and data center survey
today?

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140957?c0=jd-em-20260904.CXWgtY&source=em20260904-38231&t=1004&akid=38231%2E1203867%2EGVn8LS ]TAKE THE SURVEY

We’d like to hear directly from the members of our progressive movement as
we keep up the fight to get corporate money out of our elections and elect
progressive leaders to prioritize the working class — not Big Tech
billionaires.

Thanks for sharing your input with us.

In solidarity,

Justice Democrats

This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Email is the most important way for us to reach you about opportunities to get involved. subject: Let's Spill The Tea On Mail Ballots

body:
<a clicktracking=off href="http://example.com">
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/EA/EA016/1/99735/images/NPP_Ed_logo_RGB_green1-01.jpg]
Hi Friend,
Welcome to the latest New PA Project Education Fund (NPPEF) newsletter!
Earlier this week, the PA [https://www.politicspa.com/could-changes-finally-be-coming-to-pa-election-laws/141393/] House State Government Committee [https://www.politicspa.com/could-changes-finally-be-coming-to-pa-election-laws/141393/] [https://www.politicspa.com/could-changes-finally-be-coming-to-pa-election-laws/141393/] voted on two bills that have the potential to impact our voting rights: State Rep Mehaffie's Voter ID bill (HB771) and State Rep. McClinton's omnibus bill (HB1396). Both passed out of committee this week and will now be voted on by the full house.
An omnibus bill is a legislative bill that combines multiple, sometimes unrelated, provisions or bills into one single bill. It's essentially a package deal of different legislative proposals, often used to facilitate the passage of legislation, particularly appropriations bills.
HB 771 is sponsored by State Rep. Thomas Mehaffie (Dauphin) and “would require all voters arriving at their election precincts to show identification or attest under penalty of law that they are legally able to vote in Pennsylvania.”
State Rep. Malcolm Kenyatta (Philadelphia) voiced his opposition to the bill. The bill doesn’t address [https://www.politicspa.com/state-government-committee-sends-voter-id-election-omnibus-bills-to-house-floor/141399] the real issues at stake. “We need to solve problems of voter irregularities and voter fraud,” he said. “We do not have demonstrable evidence that leads us to make the point that we need to address voter ID in this way. Let’s talk about the issues that do exist. This legislation doesn’t address those.”
HB 1396 has a more recognizable name behind it – Speaker of the State House Joanna McClinton (Delaware/Philadelphia). State Rep. Ben Waxman (Philadelphia) complemented the Speaker, saying that the legislation is a “comprehensive approach to election reform that tries to dramatically improve the process and makes administration of elections much smoother.”
Among other changes, [https://penncapital-star.com/campaigns-elections/voter-id-and-vote-by-mail-reform-bills-move-to-pa-house] House Bill 1396 would also give election workers up to a week before Election Day to prepare to count mail-in ballots, a process that has been a bottleneck for election results in parts of the state, providing fodder for election deniers.
The vote-by-mail provision has been the subject of numerous lawsuits, including one now before the U.S. Supreme Court, as candidates and parties have argued over how election officials should handle irregularities, such as errors on completed ballots, that are not explicitly addressed.
The bill would make clear that county election officials are required to notify voters if their mail-in ballots have been rejected for the lack of a signature and give the voter an opportunity to “cure” the error.
Upcoming events
As Allegheny County voters prepare for the pivotal 2025 local, municipal and judicial elections, the New PA Project Education Fund (NPPEF) is hosting two critical public candidate forums to give community members the chance to hear directly from the candidates shaping our schools and courts. These moderated discussions will allow voters to ask questions and learn more about each candidate’s priorities and qualifications before heading to the polls.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/EA/EA016/1/99735/images/Pittsburgh%20School%20board%20forum%208.5x11.png]
Meet the candidates running for the Pittsburgh School Board and hear how they plan to impact our schools and students.
Moderator: Dr. Kimeka Campbell is our Senior Director of Campaigns and Engagement. She is a recognized community activist, political strategist, and civic engagement leader.
With over 15 years of experience in community organizing, political consulting, and nonprofit leadership, Dr. Campbell has been instrumental in shaping voter engagement strategies and building coalitions for progressive change. She co-founded Young Professionals of Color–Greater Harrisburg (YPOC), an organization dedicated to fostering leadership, advocacy, and professional growth for communities of color.
When: Friday, May 9, 2025 | 6:00 PM – 7:30 PM

This past Friday, Courts delivered wins for Pennsylvania voters [https://www.democracydocket.com/news-alerts/a-double-win-for-voters-in-pennsylvania] . One ruling ensured that undated or wrongly dated mail-in ballots will be counted, while the other rejected a bid to purge more than 277,000 from the state’s voter rolls.
First, the 3rd U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals denied [https://www.democracydocket.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/445-2025-04-24-Order-denying-PA-Attorney-Generals-motion-to-intervene.pdf] a request by Pennsylvania Attorney General Dave Sunday (R), on behalf of the state, to halt a recent federal court ruling that Pennsylvania must count undated or wrongly dated mail-in ballots.
The ruling stemmed from a lawsuit originally filed [https://www.democracydocket.com/cases/pennsylvania-undated-and-wrongly-dated-mail-in-ballots-challenge-eakin/] in 2022, challenging the state’s instructions to county boards of elections that any mail-in ballot that’s timely cast but either missing a date or containing the wrong date on the outer return envelopes should not be counted.
After the federal judge’s ruling in March of this year, the plaintiffs appealed [https://www.democracydocket.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/441-2025-04-02-Notice-Of-Appeal-.pdf] the decision to the 3rd Circuit. The appeal remains ongoing, but today’s order ensures that counties will count wrongly dated and undated ballots during this month’s primary.
Second, a Pennsylvania district court judge dismissed a lawsuit by the 1789 Foundation to have hundreds of thousands of voters purged from Pennsylvania’s voter rolls.The 1789 Foundation, also known as Citizen_AG, filed [https://www.democracydocket.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/1-2024-10-29-Complaint.pdf] a lawsuit in October against Pennsylvania Secretary of State Al Schmidt (R) claiming Schmidt failed to maintain voter rolls in line with the National Voter Registration Act.
The group wanted the court to force Pennsylvania to remove 277,000 registrants who did not respond to confirmation notices in the 2020 general election cycle removed from the voter rolls.
District Court judge Robert Mariani dismissed [https://www.democracydocket.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/67-2025-05-02-Memorandum-.pdf] the 1789 Foundation’s lawsuit on the grounds that the organization lacked standing to bring the case in the first place.
In law, standing [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standing_(law)] is a condition that a party seeking a legal remedy must show they have, by demonstrating to the court, sufficient connection to and harm from the law or action challenged to support the party's participation in the case.
In other news, this year marks the 15th anniversary of a landmark U.S. Supreme Court ruling that fundamentally reshaped the world of campaign finance. For good-government supporters, it’s a somber milestone. Find out why in Spotlight PA’s full report. [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/05/citizens-united-supreme-court-ruling-campaign-finance-dark-money]
The 2010 decision in Citizens United v. Federal Election Commission , they say, vastly expanded the role of big money in politics and ushered in an era of unprecedented — and in some cases, untraceable — spending on elections by ultra-wealthy special interests.
In Pennsylvania, the court decision’s impact on races for state and local offices was muted — at least early on. That is because of Pennsylvania’s notoriously lax campaign finance laws. Some state lawmakers have sought to tighten rules around so-called “dark money” groups, but their legislation didn’t make it through the full legislature. Continue reading for more on Citizens United and its lasting impact [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/05/citizens-united-supreme-court-ruling-campaign-finance-dark-money] .

There are things every one of us can do [https://www.democracydocket.com/opinion/we-have-more-power-than-trump-wants-us-to-believe-heres-what-you-can-do/] in our daily lives to help ensure free and fair elections. Some actions are small — so small that you might dismiss them as unimportant. Don’t. Every important journey begins with a single step, and the first is no less important than the last.
1. Educate Yourself
Elections can be complicated. The rules vary from state to state — and sometimes even from county to county. These rules also change frequently due to new laws, policies or court rulings. My first recommendation: spend time each month learning what’s happening with voting laws in your state and nationally.
Spotlight PA has an 2025 Election Center [https://www.spotlightpa.org/elections] with all the information you need to be prepared to vote this year, including guides to the big races, key dates, and more.

* Everything you need to know about how to vote and where to vote [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/05/pennsylvania-primary-election-day-2025-voter-information-registration]

2. Stay Engaged
To protect democracy, we all must stay engaged day in and day out. We can’t just show up right before an election and tune out afterward. If we remain committed, democracy will win.
Check out a Montgomery County Commissioner’s effort to educate voters. It's now an emmy-nominated short film. “Running elections in Pennsylvania's third-most-populous county, Neil Makhija said he’s seen the slippery slope from election misinformation to political violence.” ( Philadelphia Inquirer [https://www.inquirer.com/politics/pennsylvania/montgomery-county-commissioner-neil-makhija-emmy-20250508.html] )
3. Share What You Learn
Once you’ve figured out what’s going on, share that information with your networks and community. It might feel awkward to bring up voter suppression or changes in election laws when we’re not in the middle of a major election — but local elections happen in off years, and special elections are more common than you think. Now is the perfect time to start conversations about voting.
Here, in Pennsylvania, we vote every year, twice a year!
4. Join or Support Pro-Democracy Organizations
Is partisan politics not for you? There are numerous nonprofits and grassroots organizations working every day to protect voting rights and ensure free and fair elections. Supporting these groups with your time or resources helps these groups do their work.
Check out the work New PA Project has been up to lately below. AND , check out our upcoming events listed above!
5. Become a Trained Poll Worker
Many counties face a shortage of poll workers, especially during election season. Being a poll worker requires dedication, attention to detail and a willingness to be trained. It’s a meaningful way to serve your community and help protect the integrity of the voting process.
Here are some resources that may be helpful:
Pennsylvania Capital-Star - Advocacy groups offer training for Pa. primary poll watchers [https://penncapital-star.com/briefs/advocacy-groups-offer-training-for-pa-primary-poll-watchers/]
Spotlight PA - Election 2025: How to become a poll worker for the PA primary [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/04/pennsylvania-primary-election-2025-how-to-be-poll-worker-guide/]
Franklin County Free Press - Poll Workers Needed for Pennsylvania’s 2025 Primary Election [https://fcfreepresspa.com/poll-workers-needed-for-pennsylvanias-2025-primary-election/]
6. Engage Your Elected Officials
Call and write your elected officials at the federal, state and local levels. Tell them that protecting voting rights and ensuring free and fair elections are your top priorities. Even better, show up at public meetings. Ask them directly what they’re doing to combat voter suppression. Be informed about pending legislation and urge them to support pro-democracy initiatives. This applies no matter where you live or who represents you — Democrat or Republican. Constituent pressure always matters. Don’t let anyone tell you otherwise.
7. Vote in Every Election
Yes — every election. That means local elections, primary elections and special elections. Become a super-voter. The more you vote, the more informed and engaged you become. You’ll also be better positioned to notice and report problems — like changes to polling locations or voting equipment — that could impact turnout or accessibility.
Make a plan to vote in the primary election, Tuesday, May 20th. When are you voting this year? Who are you going with? How are you voting this year -- by mail or on Election Day? As a reminder, the last day to request a mail ballot is Tuesday, May 13th!

Earlier this week, the PA [] House State Government Committee [] [] voted on two bills that have the potential to impact our voting rights: State Rep Mehaffie's Voter ID bill (HB771) and State Rep. McClinton's omnibus bill (HB1396). Both passed out of committee this week and will now be voted on by the full house. An omnibus bill is a legislative bill that combines multiple, sometimes unrelated, provisions or bills into one single bill. It's essentially a package deal of different legislative proposals, often used to facilitate the passage of legislation, particularly appropriations bills. HB 771 is sponsored by State Rep. Thomas Mehaffie (Dauphin) and “would require all voters arriving at their election precincts to show identification or attest under penalty of law that they are legally able to vote in Pennsylvania.” State Rep. Malcolm Kenyatta (Philadelphia) voiced his opposition to the bill. The bill doesn’t address [] the real issues at stake. “We need to solve problems of voter irregularities and voter fraud,” he said. “We do not have demonstrable evidence that leads us to make the point that we need to address voter ID in this way. Let’s talk about the issues that do exist. This legislation doesn’t address those.” HB 1396 has a more recognizable name behind it – Speaker of the State House Joanna McClinton (Delaware/Philadelphia). State Rep. Ben Waxman (Philadelphia) complemented the Speaker, saying that the legislation is a “comprehensive approach to election reform that tries to dramatically improve the process and makes administration of elections much smoother.” Among other changes, [] House Bill 1396 would also give election workers up to a week before Election Day to prepare to count mail-in ballots, a process that has been a bottleneck for election results in parts of the state, providing fodder for election deniers. Join our team and help us provide civic education in our communities and register folks to vote! Positions start at $20 an hour. Interested? Contact jobs@nppef.org [jobs@nppef.org] EMAIL US [jobs@nppef.org] News You Can Use There are things every one of us can do [] in our daily lives to help ensure free and fair elections. Some actions are small — so small that you might dismiss them as unimportant. Don’t. Every important journey begins with a single step, and the first is no less important than the last. 1. Educate Yourself Elections can be complicated. The rules vary from state to state — and sometimes even from county to county. These rules also change frequently due to new laws, policies or court rulings. My first recommendation: spend time each month learning what’s happening with voting laws in your state and nationally. Spotlight PA has an 2025 Election Center [] with all the information you need to be prepared to vote this year, including guides to the big races, key dates, and more. New: Which Pittsburgh mayoral candidate most aligns with you? Take our quiz [] Get answers to your questions with our AI-powered Election Assistant [] Everything you need to know about mail voting [] , becoming a poll worker [] Everything you need to know about how to vote and where to vote [] Guides to Commonwealth, Superior Courts [] , vetting judicial candidates [] Guides to State College school board [] , Reading City Council president [] Guides to voting as a college student [] En Español Guía para votar por correo [] , la presidencia del Concejo Municipal de Reading [] * Guía para quién está en la papeleta de las primarias [] , cómo convertirse en trabajador electoral el 20 de mayo [] 2. Stay Engaged To protect democracy, we all must stay engaged day in and day out. We can’t just show up right before an election and tune out afterward. If we remain committed, democracy will win. Check out a Montgomery County Commissioner’s effort to educate voters. It's now an emmy-nominated short film. “Running elections in Pennsylvania's third-most-populous county, Neil Makhija said he’s seen the slippery slope from election misinformation to political violence.” ( Philadelphia Inquirer [] ) 3. Share What You Learn Once you’ve figured out what’s going on, share that information with your networks and community. It might feel awkward to bring up voter suppression or changes in election laws when we’re not in the middle of a major election — but local elections happen in off years, and special elections are more common than you think. Now is the perfect time to start conversations about voting. Here, in Pennsylvania, we vote every year, twice a year! 4. Join or Support Pro-Democracy Organizations Is partisan politics not for you? There are numerous nonprofits and grassroots organizations working every day to protect voting rights and ensure free and fair elections. Supporting these groups with your time or resources helps these groups do their work. Check out the work New PA Project has been up to lately below. AND , check out our upcoming events listed above! 5. Become a Trained Poll Worker Many counties face a shortage of poll workers, especially during election season. Being a poll worker requires dedication, attention to detail and a willingness to be trained. It’s a meaningful way to serve your community and help protect the integrity of the voting process. Here are some resources that may be helpful: Pennsylvania Capital-Star - Advocacy groups offer training for Pa. primary poll watchers [] Spotlight PA - Election 2025: How to become a poll worker for the PA primary [] Franklin County Free Press - Poll Workers Needed for Pennsylvania’s 2025 Primary Election [] 6. Engage Your Elected Officials Call and write your elected officials at the federal, state and local levels. Tell them that protecting voting rights and ensuring free and fair elections are your top priorities. Even better, show up at public meetings. Ask them directly what they’re doing to combat voter suppression. Be informed about pending legislation and urge them to support pro-democracy initiatives. This applies no matter where you live or who represents you — Democrat or Republican. Constituent pressure always matters. Don’t let anyone tell you otherwise. 7. Vote in Every Election Yes — every election. That means local elections, primary elections and special elections. Become a super-voter. The more you vote, the more informed and engaged you become. You’ll also be better positioned to notice and report problems — like changes to polling locations or voting equipment — that could impact turnout or accessibility. Make a plan to vote in the primary election, Tuesday, May 20th. When are you voting this year? Who are you going with? How are you voting this year -- by mail or on Election Day? As a reminder, the last day to request a mail ballot is Tuesday, May 13th! Recent Events [] Solidarity for Immigrants On Monday, May 5th, also Cinco de Mayo, over 300 people, representing 18 community organizations from across Pennsylvania, gathered at the State Capitol in Harrisburg to rally for immigrant rights. We amplified voices that have been silenced, advocated against injustice, and showed that solidarity is not just a word—it is a force that creates change. This event was a declaration that Pennsylvania stands against injustice and division. [] [] [] NPPEF on the Ground [] Last Monday, May 5th was the last day to register to vote for the primary election! Our teams were out in their communities leading up to the voter registration deadline on Monday. We helped folks ensure they have the ability to exercise their right to vote in the primary on Tuesday, May 20th. Our teams are currently getting ready for GOTV - a time of year where we are on the ground connecting with our communities and mobilizing them to vote. It's our favorite time of year to build relationships with those we hope to uplift. Dauphin County [] [] Delaware County [] [] Luzerne County [] [] Super voters vote twice a year, every year ! Thank you for doing your part to stay informed and engaged! | | Welcome back to Fact Friday. **With Election Day approaching, every Texas voter should take one critical step today:**[**check your voter registration.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138581506/644508787/864965444?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDEvMS82MTY0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzNjYxNjk0MS04MmE4LWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTkzM2IiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=caZ-AAntWuhJjooFpg5XUh4RF6FBFeFTQSWky9XrFPk=&emci=67939c0a-6ea8-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&emdi=36616941-82a8-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&ceid=14565883#/login) More than 1.2 million registered voters across Texas are currently listed in "suspense" status — **including nearly 50,400 voters here in El Paso County.** Let's break down what "suspense" actually means — and what to do if you see it next to your name. Being placed on the suspense list **doesn't mean your registration has been canceled or that you've lost your right to vote**. Peter, **Election Day is two months away.** Voters paying close attention to this race often bring up just how stark the contrast is between me and my opponent, Dillan Vancil. This is one of the most competitive districts in the country, but that hasn't stopped Vancil from defending the same MAGA agenda that's hurting families here at home. He has said he will double down on Trump’s agenda, “100 percent”. When asked directly about how Donald Trump is handling things, from mass layoffs of federal workers to rising costs to an unauthorized war, Vancil's answer was that it's all been "fine." _It is not fine_ , and families across Illinois know it. I've spent my career, first as a meteorologist and now in Congress, showing up for this district before and after the storm, not just when it's convenient. I've fought to lower prescription drug costs, protect health care, and support the family farmers who keep our region running. These are basic conditions to represent our district, and as we head into the final months, we need to keep making our case, because we know it's a winning one. [**With control of the House hanging on just a handful of seats, now cannot be the time to slow down. Huge news, Peter: The Missouri Supreme Court just ruled unanimously to strike down Republicans’ mid-decade gerrymander and restore the state’s prior map for the 2026 midterms—while allowing citizens the opportunity to reject Republicans’ proposed map at the ballot box in November. As Attorney General Eric Holder put it: “We must never forget the power that we, the people, possess. This victory is a testament to the tenacity of Missourians, who have shown the nation the power the people have to fight back when politicians attempt to undermine their right to vote. “From calling legislators and peacefully protesting to express their overwhelming opposition to Republicans’ mid-decade gerrymander, to organizing a citizen veto ballot measure to fighting back against their so-called leaders in court, at every turn they pushed and persevered. It is because of those efforts that Missourians will not only elect their Members of Congress on the state’s preexisting congressional map—a map that keeps Kansas City together—but also have the opportunity to reject Republicans’ proposed mid-decade gerrymander at the ballot box in November.” If the U.S. Supreme Court does not go out of its way to intervene, this represents a victory for the people of Missouri. And it would mean that Donald Trump and Republicans will have failed to eliminate a Democratic member of the state’s congressional delegation. This is why we fight. The people want fair maps, and when all the dust settles, that’s exactly what we’ll achieve. In 2024, Mississippi declared a public health emergency after its infant mortality rate climbed to 9.7 deaths per 1,000 live births--the state's highest level in more than a decade and roughly 60% above the national average. The announcement rightfully alarmed the nation. Any reversal in infant survival demands urgent study. But as social media claims began linking the surge to COVID-19 mRNA vaccines through "transgenerational" harm, a closer look at the data reveals a different picture--one that points to longstanding systemic health failures, not vaccination.
**What CDC Data Actually Shows**
Nationally, the infant mortality rate increased by roughly 3% in 2022, rising from 5.44 to 5.6 deaths per 1,000 live births. It was the first statistically significant jump in about two decades. While any increase is concerning, the scale is far smaller than the ">50%" or "77%" excess rates claimed in viral posts.
The leading causes of death in 2022 remained consistent with pre-pandemic patterns: congenital malformations (accounting for nearly one in five infant deaths), disorders related to short gestation and low birth weight (about 14%), sudden infant death syndrome (SIDS), unintentional injuries, and maternal complications. Notably, deaths from maternal complications rose by 9% between 2021 and 2022.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/6590ad69-101a-42bd-83bf-182ae50484b2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Mississippi's rate of 9.7 per 1,000 stands apart even from other Southern states. Georgia, Iowa, Missouri, and Texas also saw statistically significant increases, but Mississippi's burden remains the worst in the nation. The state is home to some of the highest rates of poverty, limited access to prenatal care, and maternal health disparities in the country--all factors correlated with infant mortality long before COVID-19 vaccines existed.
**What Mississippi Officials Actually Said**
Mississippi State Health Officer Dr. Dan Edney did not attribute the crisis to vaccines. In declaring the emergency, the Mississippi Department of Health identified the drivers as*congenital malformations, preterm birth, low birth weight, and SIDS. The state's response plan centers on expanding access to prenatal and postpartum care, strengthening community support for mothers, and addressing maternal health.
"Improving maternal health is the best way to reduce infant mortality," Edney stated. The emergency declaration allows the department to redirect resources toward prenatal services and maternal support--not to investigate purported vaccine effects. This matters because Mississippi's health infrastructure has struggled for years. In 2023, Mississippi ranked last or near-last in maternal health outcomes, childhood poverty, and access to obstetric care, with several counties considered maternity care deserts.
**What the Scientific Literature Says About mRNA Vaccines in Pregnancy**
Prior to revelations in Anthony Fauci's texts, emails and dairy, Federal health officials, including Drs. Anthony Fauci and Rochelle Walensky, recommended COVID-19 vaccination during pregnancy based on data showing that COVID-19 infection itself posed severe risks--including preterm birth, stillbirth, and maternal ICU admission. mRNA vaccines do not fall under the clinical definition of "gene therapy." The mRNA instructs cells to temporarily produce a spike protein to trigger an immune response; it does not enter the cell nucleus and degrades within hours to days, they said.
Yet, multiple large-scale studies have evaluated pregnancy outcomes. Research published in JAMA Pediatrics and presented at the 2026 Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine Pregnancy Meeting found no association between maternal mRNA COVID-19 vaccination and adverse neurodevelopmental outcomes in children aged 18 to 30 months. Additionally, the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG), the CDC, and the World Health Organization have maintained that vaccination during pregnancy is safe based on extensive safety monitoring.
The claim that mRNA genetic material transfers to offspring and causes "transgenerational" harm lacks a biological mechanism and has not been demonstrated in peer-reviewed studies is a huge disconnect from what is happening in maternity wards around world.
**Why Social Media Claims Have Been Rated False**
Posts by epidemiologist Nicolas Hulscher claiming a ">50%" or "77%" excess infant mortality rate and linking it to "transgenerational mRNA vaccine fatal adverse events" have been independently fact-checked by AFP, Veridica.ro, and FactCheck.org. Fact-checkers found that the figures do not correspond to CDC-reported metrics and appear to rely on unconventional statistical baselines. The claim that infant death causes "mirror" adult vaccine adverse events was also found to be unsupported; infant deaths continued to reflect historic causes like birth defects and prematurity, not cardiac or inflammatory conditions seen in rare adult vaccine reactions. So who's right, the CDC and JAMA using Fauci era information or independant thinking scientists like Nicolas?
**Mississippi Is a Concerning Case for Study --Into the Real Causes**
Mississippi deserves national attention as a case study, but for the reasons its own health officials have identified: crumbling maternal care access, poverty, and chronic conditions that disproportionately affect mothers and infants including vaccinations. The state's emergency declaration is an admission that the healthcare system is failing its most vulnerable residents.
Attributing the crisis solely to mRNA vaccines risks diverting resources and political will away from the prenatal care, nutrition support, and obstetric infrastructure that could actually save lives. The tragedy is real. The solution, according to Mississippi's own data, lies in maternal health--not in undoing vaccinations totally.
Mississippi has done a lot right this generation. For example, Mississippi 4th graders lead the nation in gains for both reading and math over time, ranking No. 1 for score improvements in reading and math since 2013. Let's hope more newborn babies arriving in the Hospitality State survive to experience it.
