**I keep showing up in communities like these because of a simple reason: I’m a Senator for every Virginian, no matter your zip code or who you voted for.**

It’s why I’ve fought to save rural hospitals after Donald Trump and congressional Republicans made massive cuts to health care. It’s why I’ve worked to expand broadband to hard-to-get-to communities across Virginia relying on high-speed internet to compete in the 21st century economy. And it’s why I’m fighting to put some real checks and balances on data centers and make sure they don’t jack up your utility bills and hurt our communities.

I’m running for reelection because where you start out should never determine where you end up. But if we want to give _every_ Virginian a shot at success, no matter where you grew up, we have a lot more work to do to make that a reality.

## **Who Owns Our Ballots?**
[](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=KO8ZOB0mq2gq63DvFrKfewPklsCL1tzWdLLY7SQpgx4ym6EbHeLUFRJBevgM_ro5&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=2026_september_newsletter&n=2) We hope you all are all watching Chris Gambino's fight to stay on the ballot for PA State House. He's doing a great job sharing the story for himself on [Facebook](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=KO8ZOB0mq2gq63DvFrKfeyK1qZFx7bNIR-pYCJqTbAnSyW5-n5tbR1ArP5djEoGS3diQRCSpFMS_OKusmuHOCA&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=2026_september_newsletter&n=3) and [Instagram](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=HR9MoATtHgNjF_4kmlo5pHG8iumOna6n8U6hzrwDi8XdQpdmIKdFrAj-3QU3Ho8U&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=2026_september_newsletter&n=4). He is demonstrating once again the challenges Independent and 3rd party candidates face in our state. It precisely these reasons that we spend so much time not only focusing on election reforms that would enhance fairness and competition - but also building a community so candidates like Chris know they have support. So that running as an Independent doesn't mean running alone. [Open Letter asking Josh Shapiro to stand up for voters](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=s9-xbJ9sz3bHEgiwz34eSc6WIoYlHfxOZDFkxGzSdvW4yeuuL_lV-iA4PJYugsr75IlD_CHuVFpbgDB1f_9UZ-UpAoMzYFLX28ndN9R1zSRtBkQGc0S8co0ncugkpwCyhbYQHygrRIHeJINqNXFEhhf7QRcLgMuYkn4LqFeXPiU1AxqVKApcg0MQXCu2l3sPNprYeuvlkWlV7g0d75vq6psYbToK8vuTq6FCMIWcHpbEy16cYHyplP1jHgV8Lw6rdmvkNU1J9Lsvs_dnFR0AD-rqvCWJerNrJrczPIYd57paBc4X5ikbpr-NlbKowPcu3tvymaCWNT2jvV6EZtT5yg&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=2026_september_newsletter&n=5) [Pennsylvania Capital Star's reporting on Chris's challenge](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=QHKVItFn0MybuDjVkgRHGIpx90TW4P5V5pA04QCABieOon5yKhbHTWtFHEy_js8c_ZZbJglyUhnVxjuo73eUtduBHKrwsyTCqUHLYtDdXDupX9z4791a7XPH4Thpqw5CTIBonGimF21hF9oWJoGUkpwlewaSu4cFY_JPGzNhEA43kQE-tOc6vQewox2Nq9Od&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=2026_september_newsletter&n=6) Listed below are a lot of opportunities to attend events or calls this month and there will be more before November's election. **Lean in. Help build the community. Show support.**

Coming out of July's convention, there is a renewed sense of the serious challenges facing us and the opportunity we have to get this right. Our party has been building a foundation for the last four years. Now it's time to push to the next level. We plan to hold more events and get our message out to a wider audience. We want to define our goals clearly to that audience. We want to find new ways to support the candidates who affiliate with us and recruit more great candidates in the future. If you want to help, this is the time to get involved.

# [Trump just stuck China with Maduro's 65 billion barrel IOU in brutal dunk](https://substack.com/redirect/06425a78-0fbd-4bcc-bfb8-8a7225b5c7ee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Washington's takeover of Venezuelan oil denies China both crude and the repayment channel on **[billions of dollars Caracas owed Beijing](https://substack.com/redirect/a06dbdf3-8e88-4d18-8bc3-c1ab034862b8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** against more than 65 billion barrels of reserves.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/06425a78-0fbd-4bcc-bfb8-8a7225b5c7ee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Revenue claims are cut:** The Yahoo Finance report said Beijing will have no claim on revenue from Venezuelan oil production, severing the main way Caracas serviced oil-backed Chinese debt.
* **65 billion barrels is the prize:** The fields hold more than 65 billion barrels, the asset Washington is using to redraw who gets paid from Venezuelan crude.
* **Hemisphere framed as security:** The United States is treating parts of the region's economic ties with China as a security concern and using leverage to enforce those red lines.
* **Beijing says its rights stand:** China said its "legitimate rights and interests in Venezuela must be protected" and that China-Venezuela cooperation is "protected by international law" and "doesn't concern any third party."

### [China lost Iran's cheap barrels and is overpaying Russia](https://substack.com/redirect/06425a78-0fbd-4bcc-bfb8-8a7225b5c7ee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Chinese refiners paid more than $7 a barrel over Brent for November ESPO, with offers as high as $10,[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/ceb2badd-d5d1-4ec4-b5c2-6bd899ee1a9b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[as buyers scramble to replace Iranian barrels](https://substack.com/redirect/ceb2badd-d5d1-4ec4-b5c2-6bd899ee1a9b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** blocked by U.S. naval measures.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/06425a78-0fbd-4bcc-bfb8-8a7225b5c7ee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **China still takes 83% of ESPO:** Beijing remained the dominant buyer in the first seven months, though its share slipped from 88% a year earlier.
* **India 's slice rose to 16%:** Indian refiners lifted ESPO purchases as Chinese imports slumped in May and June and Middle East supplies stayed disrupted.
* **Kozmino loadings are up 6%:** Oil exports from Russia's Far Eastern port of Kozmino rose 6% over the first seven months.
* **Iranian crude is the hole being filled:** Independent Chinese refiners turned to ESPO after the U.S. naval blockade squeezed Iranian flows.

Employers **[added 162,000 jobs in August,](https://substack.com/redirect/0443e7ed-437d-448e-ab64-7d9702d6590e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** far above the **[53,000-to-56,000 forecasts,](https://substack.com/redirect/0c8383ff-07ac-47de-b4e4-cec773fa5332?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** as the jobless rate held at 4.1% and traders lifted[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/bb7e9313-b2f6-47ab-9bfb-0989066d61c9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[September Fed hike odds to about 60%.](https://substack.com/redirect/bb7e9313-b2f6-47ab-9bfb-0989066d61c9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/06425a78-0fbd-4bcc-bfb8-8a7225b5c7ee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **June and July get rewritten:** July flipped from a 23,000 loss to a 21,000 gain and June rose to 31,000, leaving those two months 55,000 jobs higher than first reported.
* **Restaurants and schools did the lifting:** Food services added 59,000 jobs and local-government education 42,000, while information lost 23,000 and wages rose 0.3% on the month, 3.1% over the year.
* **Stocks sold the hot print:** The Dow was down 0.6%, the S&P 500 0.3%, and the Nasdaq 0.1% as the 10-year yield sat near 4.77% to 4.80% and hike odds jumped from roughly even money.
* **Trump wants cuts, not a hike:** Trump called it a "great jobs number" and told the Fed to lower rates, while Morgan Stanley's Ellen Zentner said next week's inflation prints still decide the meeting.

# [600,000 NYC students can't touch classroom AI this year](https://substack.com/redirect/06425a78-0fbd-4bcc-bfb8-8a7225b5c7ee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Mayor Zohran Mamdani imposed[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/728aa9a0-7d51-45bf-846b-f68398e93699?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[a one-year generative-AI moratorium on elementary and middle schoolers](https://substack.com/redirect/728aa9a0-7d51-45bf-846b-f68398e93699?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** in the nation's largest district, while high schoolers get five AI programs.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/06425a78-0fbd-4bcc-bfb8-8a7225b5c7ee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Not a forever ban:** City Hall framed the K-8 halt as a one-year pause, not a permanent lockout, in a district the Fox Business report called the country's largest.
* **High school still gets five programs:** Teenagers will study AI's uses and risks across five separate programs because, Mamdani said, they are already growing up in an AI-saturated world.
* **He says no study backs early use:** Mamdani said he has "yet to see a study showing that AI is beneficial for students in elementary and middle school" and that ubiquity is not the same as necessity.
* **Teachers-pay fight is in court:** His office sued to block a teacher pay increase after City Hall approved it, arguing the bill violates state law; the United Federation of Teachers intervened.

# [VW doubles job cuts to 100,000 and kills half the lineup](https://substack.com/redirect/06425a78-0fbd-4bcc-bfb8-8a7225b5c7ee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Volkswagen's supervisory board approved **[another 50,000 job cuts](https://substack.com/redirect/dbaaa9aa-23a0-4c20-a0f9-0db4760699b1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** on top of about 50,000 already made since 2024, taking planned reductions to 100,000 as the company **[slashes its model range.](https://substack.com/redirect/23265d65-798c-48cc-99b8-f838b42da309?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/06425a78-0fbd-4bcc-bfb8-8a7225b5c7ee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Four German plants lose new models:** Emden, Zwickau, Hanover, and Neckarsulm get no new vehicles unless costs fall, with alternative uses under review.
* **Half the lineup goes in 9 years:** VW plans to discontinue half its models over nine years to cut complexity after the board's surprise restructuring vote.
* **Shares bid the bloodletting:** **[Volkswagen stock rose about 5.5% on the news,](https://substack.com/redirect/92ee343e-bb49-4fc8-a24a-68672c1b38d0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/92ee343e-bb49-4fc8-a24a-68672c1b38d0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)even after a year-to-date drop of more than 20%.
* **Workers face closure risk:** **[Barron's said](https://substack.com/redirect/23265d65-798c-48cc-99b8-f838b42da309?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** the deeper cuts open the door to factory closures and left staff reeling after the doubled target landed.

# [Waymo adds 3 cities as Zoox opens paid Vegas airport runs](https://substack.com/redirect/06425a78-0fbd-4bcc-bfb8-8a7225b5c7ee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Waymo opened public driverless rides **[in Denver, San Diego, and Tampa,](https://substack.com/redirect/63a41530-e5c9-4c4e-b3d1-03dcc1b88505?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** reaching 14 U.S. cities, while Amazon's Zoox started paid robotaxi shuttles **[between the Las Vegas Strip and Harry Reid International Airport.](https://substack.com/redirect/cfd1741e-c989-4d8d-9635-0397a12a8934?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/06425a78-0fbd-4bcc-bfb8-8a7225b5c7ee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Waymo claims a 94% safety gap:** The company said its driver was in 94% fewer crashes with serious injuries or worse than human drivers over the same distance, after tens of thousands signed up in each new city.
* **Zoox needed a federal waiver:** NHTSA granted a temporary FMVSS exemption on July 31 because the carriages have no steering wheel or pedals; paid airport service began Aug. 10.
* **Four-seat carriages, no driver controls:** Zoox vehicles seat 4 facing each other and run to the Convention Center, Sphere, T-Mobile Arena, and major Strip resorts.
* **Zoox maps 10 more paid cities:** After Vegas, Zoox plans paid rides in Seattle, Austin, Dallas, Houston, San Diego, Los Angeles, and others as Waymo keeps a gradual public rollout.

# [Goldman just found 5 million Hormuz barrels hiding in the dark](https://substack.com/redirect/06425a78-0fbd-4bcc-bfb8-8a7225b5c7ee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Goldman Sachs identified[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/96f7dc30-6e92-4631-9c9d-14d30c283153?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[a roughly 5 million-barrel-a-day"dark transit" blind spot in Hormuz,](https://substack.com/redirect/96f7dc30-6e92-4631-9c9d-14d30c283153?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** even as official tallies tout a recovery in flows through the strait.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/06425a78-0fbd-4bcc-bfb8-8a7225b5c7ee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **The advertised recovery is incomplete:** ZeroHedge said markets have been told Hormuz traffic is coming back, while Goldman still cannot see about 5 million barrels a day.
* **Dark runs are the adaptation:** Tankers are moving around the conflict with transponders dark, creating a flow the official recovery story does not capture.
* **That gap is the tape:** A 5 million-barrel-a-day miss is large enough to keep oil pricing off the official transit counts.

# [GPT-6 dropped and the cheap AI trade is still open](https://substack.com/redirect/06425a78-0fbd-4bcc-bfb8-8a7225b5c7ee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
OpenAI **[unveiled GPT-6 Astra for enterprise computer use,](https://substack.com/redirect/5c40157f-5afe-44de-8bd0-c79a402a33a6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** rolling it first to Daybreak customers, as Goldman said the model[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/7f180dbc-74c4-4882-a700-e3506790293d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[is what the AI bull case has been waiting for](https://substack.com/redirect/7f180dbc-74c4-4882-a700-e3506790293d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and AIQ threatened a breakout.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/06425a78-0fbd-4bcc-bfb8-8a7225b5c7ee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **SOTA on the office stack:** OpenAI said Astra is state-of-the-art on computer use, browser tasks, software engineering, cybersecurity, science, and professional work, including forms, records, calendars, and decks.
* **Plus and API come next:** After Daybreak enterprises, the model is slated for ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise, plus the OpenAI API and Amazon Web Services.
* **Altman calls it most aligned:** Sam Altman said Astra is the company's "most aligned model ever," set "a new standard" for safety, and took longer to ship for that reason.
* **Vol is crushed as NYFANG hits highs:** **[ZeroHedge said](https://substack.com/redirect/0633ffc0-21f8-4500-a47a-3b6c45dde3b8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** AIQ is threatening a multi-month breakout, NYFANG closed at a record, and tech options stay cheap while Astra refuels the spend narrative.

# [Goldman doubles down on Dallas as New York the cold shoulder](https://substack.com/redirect/06425a78-0fbd-4bcc-bfb8-8a7225b5c7ee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Goldman Sachs is **[building an 800,000-square-foot Dallas campus for a January 2028 opening](https://substack.com/redirect/3563ad7c-2c9c-4ada-ba19-66571442cd62?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** beside the Perot Museum, consolidating its second-largest U.S. headcount hub outside New York.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/06425a78-0fbd-4bcc-bfb8-8a7225b5c7ee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Two offices become one:** CAO Ericka Leslie said the new building will combine the firm's current Dallas sites so every business unit sits in one state-of-the-art space.
* **NYC headcount is frozen:** CEO David Solomon told CNBC New York staffing has stayed a little under 10,000 for about 20 years, while Dallas and Salt Lake City absorbed the U.S. growth.
* **Amenities are the pitch:** The campus is slated for a wellness center, gym, backup daycare, cafeteria spaces, a coffee bar, underground parking, and a 1.5-acre park.
* **Dallas crews caused a slight delay:** Leslie said the project is mostly on time, with small slips from the city's construction boom, and called Dallas a "really bright future."

Teachers-pay fight is in court: His office sued to block a teacher pay increase after City Hall approved it, arguing the bill violates state law; the United Federation of Teachers intervened. Volkswagen's supervisory board approved on top of about 50,000 already made since 2024, taking planned reductions to 100,000 as the company | | ---|---|--- Four German plants lose new models: Emden, Zwickau, Hanover, and Neckarsulm get no new vehicles unless costs fall, with alternative uses under review. Half the lineup goes in 9 years: VW plans to discontinue half its models over nine years to cut complexity after the board's surprise restructuring vote. Shares bid the bloodletting: after a year-to-date drop of more than 20%. Workers face closure risk: the deeper cuts open the door to factory closures and left staff reeling after the doubled target landed. | | | | ---|---|--- | Aug 16 | Waymo opened public driverless rides reaching 14 U.S. cities, while Amazon's Zoox started paid robotaxi shuttles | | ---|---|--- Waymo claims a 94% safety gap: The company said its driver was in 94% fewer crashes with serious injuries or worse than human drivers over the same distance, after tens of thousands signed up in each new city. Zoox needed a federal waiver: NHTSA granted a temporary FMVSS exemption on July 31 because the carriages have no steering wheel or pedals; paid airport service began Aug. 10. Four-seat carriages, no driver controls: Zoox vehicles seat 4 facing each other and run to the Convention Center, Sphere, T-Mobile Arena, and major Strip resorts. Zoox maps 10 more paid cities: After Vegas, Zoox plans paid rides in Seattle, Austin, Dallas, Houston, San Diego, Los Angeles, and others as Waymo keeps a gradual public rollout. Goldman Sachs identified even as official tallies tout a recovery in flows through the strait. | | ---|---|--- The advertised recovery is incomplete: ZeroHedge said markets have been told Hormuz traffic is coming back, while Goldman still cannot see about 5 million barrels a day. Dark runs are the adaptation: Tankers are moving around the conflict with transponders dark, creating a flow the official recovery story does not capture. That gap is the tape: A 5 million-barrel-a-day miss is large enough to keep oil pricing off the official transit counts. OpenAI rolling it first to Daybreak customers, as Goldman said the model and AIQ threatened a breakout. | | ---|---|--- SOTA on the office stack: OpenAI said Astra is state-of-the-art on computer use, browser tasks, software engineering, cybersecurity, science, and professional work, including forms, records, calendars, and decks. Plus and API come next: After Daybreak enterprises, the model is slated for ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise, plus the OpenAI API and Amazon Web Services. Altman calls it most aligned: Sam Altman said Astra is the company's "most aligned model ever," set "a new standard" for safety, and took longer to ship for that reason. Vol is crushed as NYFANG hits highs: AIQ is threatening a multi-month breakout, NYFANG closed at a record, and tech options stay cheap while Astra refuels the spend narrative. Goldman Sachs is beside the Perot Museum, consolidating its second-largest U.S. headcount hub outside New York. | | ---|---|--- Two offices become one: CAO Ericka Leslie said the new building will combine the firm's current Dallas sites so every business unit sits in one state-of-the-art space. NYC headcount is frozen: CEO David Solomon told CNBC New York staffing has stayed a little under 10,000 for about 20 years, while Dallas and Salt Lake City absorbed the U.S. growth. Amenities are the pitch: The campus is slated for a wellness center, gym, backup daycare, cafeteria spaces, a coffee bar, underground parking, and a 1.5-acre park. Dallas crews caused a slight delay: Leslie said the project is mostly on time, with small slips from the city's construction boom, and called Dallas a "really bright future." Damage to buildings in the aftermath of a U.S. strike on a wedding party in Kuhestak, Sirik County, in the Hormozgan Province of Iran. September 2, 2026. Photo by Morteza Akhondi/Getty Images.
TEHRAN, Iran--Hundreds of guests had gathered in two family homes in Kuhestak, a coastal village in Iran's southern Hormozgan province near the Strait of Hormuz, for a wedding celebration on Tuesday night when the missiles struck.
"I still hear the voices of the women who were ululating, and then suddenly the roof of the living room and the walls came down on us," Zeinab Mallahi, a guest at the wedding, told Drop Site News. "That sound follows me from night into day and from day into night."
A projectile tore through the roof of one of the homes, leaving a crater roughly 1.5 meters deep in the floor. Another struck a date palm, sending it crashing into a wall. People began screaming and "running everywhere," she recalled. "It was something I had only seen in movies. I had never seen a missile. I had never seen shrapnel. I didn't understand what was happening."
Four people were killed instantly: Four-year-old Amir Ali Karimi, 16-year old Mohammad Mallahi, 43-year-old Kolsoom Mallahi Nezhadnia, and 50-year-old Zarkhatoun Taheri. Two days later, 22-year-old Asieh Molaeinezhad, who had been critically wounded and placed in intensive care, died, bringing the death toll to five. At least 60 others were wounded.
On August 30, the U.S. began bombing Iran again, with attacks concentrated in the south of the country, after both sides had withheld strikes for weeks. Iranian authorities said at least[ 14 others](https://substack.com/redirect/533f7f25-f10b-4fa1-9b2c-2713a7a8f97d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) were killed in strikes across Iran that night. Tehran responded by launching attacks at U.S. targets in Jordan, Kuwait, Iraq, and Bahrain.
Ali Mallahi, a local fisherman and the father of the bride, told Drop Site that at least 350 people had gathered to celebrate his daughter Maryam's wedding when his house was struck.
"I really don't know what to say," Mallahi told Drop Site. "This happened in a completely residential area. There were no military facilities around the house."
As is typical of weddings in Hormozgan, the men and women were gathered in separate family homes separated by less than a hundred meters. Mallahi was with the men at his cousin Mohammad Rasoul's house, while the women had assembled at his own. The explosion came without warning.
"My first thought was that a gas cylinder had exploded in my house," Mallahi said. He rushed to check on the women, hearing a second and third explosion as he got there. "When I arrived, everybody was running in different directions."
He continued, "For a moment I just froze. I didn't know what had happened. I asked myself, did they really fire a missile at my house? What happened to my daughter's wedding? What happened to my guests? My children, my wife, everyone?"
Eight people were admitted to a hospital in Sirik, while six others were placed in intensive care at the Hazrat Abolfazl Hospital in Minab. A further 26 patients were admitted to the hospital's surgical wards, according to Pezhman Shahrokhi, a local health official. Of the six patients in intensive care, one was in critical condition and had been intubated. A total of 36 patients were later discharged after receiving diagnostic and specialized treatment.
U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM)[ described](https://substack.com/redirect/23de0615-49d1-4a21-bef0-afdf4d19f001?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the September 1 wave of strikes in southern Iran as targeting the "air-defense sites, radar systems, and maritime assets" of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. On Thursday, Vice President JD Vance claimed the U.S. was investigating the incident but added that he was "extremely skeptical" of the reports around the attack. "What I can say with 100% confidence is that unlike [Iran], the United States never targets civilians in combat. We never will do that. We never have done that, and unfortunately, obviously, sometimes things happen," he said at a White House press briefing.
A Reuters [investigation](https://substack.com/redirect/06b39275-01ac-481c-8af6-72b69bfd35e0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) found that the wedding bombing was likely a direct hit by a U.S. munition and not a ricochet off another target.
"None of us had anything to do with politics. I don't know international law, but I know what happened here is not right," Mallahi said. "America is certainly responsible. My house was in a completely residential area. I don't know what has happened to my life. My daughter's wedding was left unfinished. My relatives are in the hospital. Even my sister has to undergo surgery because of her injuries."
Hundreds gathered for the funeral on Thursday of the four victims killed on the day of the attack, including mourners, relatives, military, and civilian officials, according to state media.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/83a4abdf-92f5-4a96-b672-faad841686d8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The funeral for the victims of a strike on a wedding party in the village of Kuhestak, Sirik County, in the Hormozgan Province of Iran. September 3, 2026. Photo by Morteza Akhondi/Getty Images.
"I feel ashamed in front of my guests now," Mallahi said. "They were supposed to come here and be with us on my daughter's happy night. But now, whenever I see them, I think I will lower my head. They came here because of us, and some of them lost their children or their relatives."
More than 3,000 Iranians[ have been killed](https://substack.com/redirect/297636a9-4086-444b-8c9b-08096102bac9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) since the U.S. and Israel launched the war on February 28, according to Iranian authorities, including more than 50 during a 60-day truce before fighting resumed in July.
Mostafa Taheri, a Red Crescent emergency worker, told Drop Site his team reached the site five minutes after receiving a report of the attack. They were already on alert because of U.S. strikes the previous night.
"What I saw was happiness and grief existing in the same place," Taheri recalled. "It still looked as if a celebration was taking place, the wedding lights were still on."
Multiple wedding guests were still trapped beneath rubble when rescuers arrived. Others had been injured by fragments. Taheri said it was the first time he had encountered such a scene.
"We could hear the wounded screaming," he said. "We immediately started finding people, moving the rubble and transferring the injured."
Residents and wedding guests helped rescuers clear debris and move casualties. Some of the wounded had injuries to their hands, legs, and heads. Others were bleeding heavily.
"I saw that a child had been killed," he said. "When I asked how old he was and they told me he was four, it affected me deeply. Even now, two days later, I am still thinking about him."

# [The Supreme Court's Trust Problem & Justice Elena Kagan's Admission](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=4399133&post_id=214200307&utm_source=post-email-title&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjE0MjAwMzA3LCJpYXQiOjE3ODg1NDY2MTMsImV4cCI6MTc5MTEzODYxMywiaXNzIjoicHViLTQzOTkxMzMiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.UK1T5LzlomWiKZIZalPKk0xrlCDvLXUh_IMueFTu94c)

For years, Americans' confidence in many of the country's major institutions has [fallen to historically low levels](https://substack.com/redirect/651c99c0-f68c-4da7-8b49-86c28d0acef4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Congress, the news media, the presidency and the [Supreme Court](https://substack.com/redirect/00779fd9-fe31-4a95-80c4-8fe929416981?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) all command far less trust than they once did. Much of that decline is attributed to polarization, misinformation and growing public cynicism. But institutions also lose trust when they give people reasons to question the processes behind their authority.
A revealing example surfaced in July. At a congressional hearing, Sen. Susan Collins asked [Justice Elena Kagan](https://substack.com/redirect/95c668b0-1bb1-494b-ab13-6bcf8efcd974?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) about a scientific reference manual for federal judges called the Federal Judicial Center that carried Kagan's authored foreword. The manual has helped federal judges navigate complicated scientific evidence for more than three decades, but one chapter had become controversial enough to be withdrawn. Kagan's response was striking: she had not read the chapter before lending her name to the book. "Actually," she added, "I still haven't read it."
It was the kind of Washington moment that was almost too perfect. A Supreme Court justice standing in front of a co-equal branch and having endorsed a publication, part of it had blown up into a political controversy, and she explained that she had never read it. That made for an easy gotcha. It also revealed something more important. Powerful people attach their names to work they have not personally checked every day. Kagan could not realistically review every page of a massive scientific manual herself. The credibility of her endorsement therefore depended on whether the institutions behind the book had done that work for her. Justice Kagan looked Senator Collins in the eye and was truthful; she didn't look for combat or make the cable news infotainment cycle. As someone who lectures at Wharton Business School and has testified to Congress, it was a lesson in avoiding a crisis by being humble.
I learned the same lesson from leading a seven-person paratrooper team in Iraq or the 1.3 million Army at the Pentagon. Senior leaders inevitably delegate tasks. They cannot personally verify every report, contract, or recommendation that carries an institution's name. But delegation does not make accountability disappear. It makes the systems underneath a leader more important. If I could not check everything myself, I had to be able to trust that conflicts had been identified, assumptions challenged and problems surfaced before something reached my desk. Luckily, the backbone of our US Army is our non-commissioned officers. Having a good Sergeant was life or death.
But Justice Kagan's admission gets to the heart of the problem. No one can reasonably expect her to read every page herself. What the public can expect is that the institutions asking for her endorsement have done the vetting she cannot do personally. With trust in major institutions already near historic lows, even a small failure in that process can do real damage.

The _Reference Manual on Scientific Evidence_ shows why that distinction is important. Produced by the Federal Judicial Center with the National Academies, it is designed to help federal judges evaluate scientific and technical evidence they may not be equipped to assess on their own. In other words, its usefulness depends on trust: trust that the experts were chosen carefully, potential conflicts were disclosed, and competing evidence was treated fairly. The controversy surrounding its climate chapter suggests those safeguards deserve scrutiny.
Republican attorneys general raised concerns about the chapter earlier this year, arguing that it presented climate issues in a way that could influence ongoing litigation. The Federal Judicial Center subsequently removed the chapter from copies distributed to judges. Then, in April, the conservative Oversight Project raised a more specific concern: the chapter relied significantly on work by Michael Burger, an academic who is also counsel at Sher Edling, a law firm representing state and local governments pursuing climate-damages litigation against energy companies.
Burger's involvement in that litigation does not, by itself, invalidate his scholarship. Expertise often comes from people deeply involved in the fields they study. Nor should this controversy become an excuse to dismiss the enormous body of scientific evidence surrounding climate change. But if someone professionally involved in litigation against an industry contributes scholarship to material intended to guide judges confronting related cases, that relationship should be unmistakably disclosed and independently evaluated before the institution lends the work its authority.
By late August, weeks after Justice Kagan's testimony, the National Academies had withdrawn its version of the chapter and announced an independent review. That was the appropriate response. But it also underscored the problem: safeguards meant to protect the credibility of the manual were being examined only after the controversy had become public.
That makes Kagan's role less scandalous than her critics suggest. Justice Kagan was appointed by President Obama in 2010, and she was testifying to Congress with her colleague, Justice Amy Coney Barrett, appointed by President Trump in 2020. Other justices, including Stephen Breyer, have written forewords for earlier editions, and no one reasonably expects a Supreme Court justice to personally fact-check hundreds of pages of scientific scholarship. The episode is more useful as a test of the institutions behind the manual. If they are asking judges to rely on their work, their procedures for vetting experts, disclosing conflicts and reviewing contested material have to be strong enough to justify that trust.
The stakes are higher because confidence in the Supreme Court is already near historic lows. [Gallup](https://substack.com/redirect/e30cffeb-49de-4e6b-addd-f578a7d96fb2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) reported this summer that just 33% of Americans approve of the Court's performance, while 61% disapprove. In that environment, even a relatively technical lapse in disclosure or review can reinforce the suspicion that supposedly neutral institutions operate by rules the public cannot see.
The standard also has to be consistent. Climate litigation has prompted scrutiny of justices on both sides of the Court, including Kagan and Justice Samuel Alito. Justice Alito holds between $175-545K in oil and gas stocks, where he earned up to $2.9 million from these assets from 2005 to 2024. Public confidence will not recover if potential conflicts are treated as grave ethical concerns when they involve political opponents and harmless technicalities when they involve political allies. The same is true with insider trading by members of Congress. Institutions only earn trust by applying the same rules when doing so is inconvenient.
The climate chapter controversy is unlikely to determine how Americans ultimately view the Supreme Court. Nor should it be treated as some defining scandal. But trust rarely collapses because of one dramatic scandal. More often, it erodes through accumulation: a conflict disclosed too late, a review that comes only after controversy, an endorsement resting on assumptions no one bothered to test. Rebuilding trust requires institutions to catch those problems before the public does and to apply the same standards regardless of who benefits politically.

Here’s what Tim Hoheneder, Organizer for the grad student workers at UNH had to say:
_“UNH graduate workers have been fighting two years towards a fair first contract and a living wage. Carleigh’s strong background and experiences as a graduate labor organizer means she understands the power workers build when standing together. Carleigh reflects the commitment to collective power that graduate workers need from those seeking to represent New Hampshire.”_
And here’s what Brandon Mancilla, UAW Region 9A Director, had to say:
_“UAW is proud to endorse Carleigh Beriont. As a former UAW member herself, Carleigh understands what it takes to fight for unions. She has stood with the UNH Grad Workers in their fight for a contract, and is committed to supporting new organizing in the state. Her commitment to passing Medicare for All makes her undeniably the right choice for NH this fall.”_
As a union organizer, I helped organize UAW Local 5118, a union of graduate student workers demanding fair pay, paid leave, transparent scheduling, and anti-retaliation policies. We went on strike twice before securing our first contract.
Last Friday, I joined UNH graduate students to call for a fair contract. body:
Inside Elections just moved New Hampshire to Toss-up. I’ve been warning about this race for months. Now it’s official.
# [](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1&akid=8715%2E582294%2E5q9Otd)
Folks, it's James Carville.
Inside Elections just moved New Hampshire’s Senate race from **Tilt Democratic** to **Toss-up.**
This is the first race rater this cycle to put us in Toss-up territory. And I need you to understand what that means and how we got here.
**[🚨 Before you read another word, rush a contribution to Chris Pappas. This rating change is a five-alarm fire.](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260904_2.UkTVQl&refcode=em20260904-2&t=2&akid=8715%2E582294%2E5q9Otd)**
Let me tell you what a Toss-up rating means in plain English: The people whose entire job is to watch and analyze Senate races for a living are now saying this race could go either way.
Not probably Democratic. Not leaning our way. A coin flip.
**_And here’s what’s making me sick: This didn’t happen overnight. This race has been sliding._**
Earlier this cycle Chris Pappas was ahead. Not by a lot — this has always been a margin-of-error race — but he was ahead. Then the Republican money started hitting the airwaves. More than thirty million dollars in outside spending against us, us without enough money to fight back, and the polls started moving.
The most recent UNH Granite State Poll showed Sununu ahead for the first time this entire campaign — 45 to 43. **A five-point swing in the wrong direction.**
**And now Inside Elections has seen enough to move us to Toss-up.**
I’ve been warning about this for months. I warned you that New Hampshire was being ignored while money poured into other races. I warned you that John Sununu was a uniquely dangerous opponent with the name, the money, and a Republican machine that had decided New Hampshire was their best shot at keeping the Senate. I warned you that unanswered spending moves voters.
All of it is happening. Right now. In real time.
**[Rush a contribution to Chris Pappas today. $10, $25, whatever you can spare. Peter,
Greg Abbott’s recent ABC News interview was a total disaster. Caught off guard on live TV, he tried to flip his record.

---|---
But the facts speak for themselves.
**Myth** : He set guardrails on data centers.
**Fact:** He handed them the country's biggest tax breaks to drain our power grid, with zero regulation.
**Myth:** He’s bringing gas prices below $2 and making Texas affordable.
**Fact:** Gas is averaging $3.60, property taxes are soaring, and Texas now leads the nation in bankruptcies and uninsured families.
**Myth:** "What matters in elections is November."
**Fact:** _**Actually, that’s the one thing he got right.**_

**Chairman Maltzie’s Statement on Yesterday’s NH-01 Democrat Debate**
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | **FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE** September 4th, 2026
---
| | | **CONTACT** karina@nhrsc.com

---
| |

CONCORD, N.H. — New Hampshire Republican State Committee Chairman Scott Maltzie released the following statement after last night’s NH-01 Democrat Debate:“This debate exposed the true agenda of the Democratic Party in New Hampshire,” said NHGOP Chairman Scott Maltzie. “Each candidate was more radical than the next, and their ideas about what Granite Staters want in their next representative in Congress couldn’t be more out of touch.”“Maura Sullivan and Stefany Shaheen both support government-run healthcare policies that would fundamentally change how Americans receive and pay for healthcare. They also support expanding the Supreme Court and dismantling ICE, policies that would have serious consequences for our country and the people of New Hampshire.”“Granite Staters got a true look at what these candidates want to do if they get to Congress, and their agenda wouldn’t make people’s lives better. Last night proved why New Hampshire needs to send a Republican to Congress this November and reject the Democrats’ radical agenda.”
In case you missed it, here are the highlights:Maura Sullivan:
* Would “[absolutely](https://us.list-manage.com/wLc5CrNZVZN?e=f3aa6419cd&c2id=cbe815d8d4829b0196839495b093775b&m=7OD-prqajeF3cncMof_GHxgHIcKAatIIPuMjtbQEwkBnRDMsqI4EGVx81g==)” expand the Supreme Court
* Pledged her support to make D.C and Puerto Rico [states](https://us.list-manage.com/HURkHKVWii1?e=f3aa6419cd&c2id=cbe815d8d4829b0196839495b093775b&m=2_4TzqGrqvPwJIg3ZP_wKrv_ZLa85wa2tXlRyupNjzZ09QLYaF3nPD3aDg==)
* Wants to [impeach](https://us.list-manage.com/VLtk66tiLfs?e=f3aa6419cd&c2id=cbe815d8d4829b0196839495b093775b&m=G2tVg3ToTiDWciKNoR_HQmqMjSn6L0k6UacGA3q_LsrNuDmtcuHdpWHczg==) Trump
* Called to [abolish](https://us.list-manage.com/138IGy4i33A?e=f3aa6419cd&c2id=cbe815d8d4829b0196839495b093775b&m=mvrIaoSATaVSL1b6MXAWHQ1uRhPtvAmVr_ixvCNYME_ZPXW3bSMCkrKkLQ==) ICE
* Wants government-run healthcare by [cutting](https://us.list-manage.com/tad7zL4BsD7?e=f3aa6419cd&c2id=cbe815d8d4829b0196839495b093775b&m=S0rD0OTOxCjdIFXGGvVGiaARYarh9568rcqZp5ksbL8u5qY_26NU-yIpAA==) our defense budget
* Said the Biden administration wasn’t “[aggressive enough](https://us.list-manage.com/Jot7gF_ApnH?e=f3aa6419cd&c2id=cbe815d8d4829b0196839495b093775b&m=L3dYUxU0YD2nTukfbbHF9PFTnhzEK--K77yYtsSLxADCTw3v_Nyk0dxfmw==)” on their climate agenda

Stefany Shaheen:
* Wants to make D.C. and Puerto Rico [states](https://us.list-manage.com/bltG_fxGs4e?e=f3aa6419cd&c2id=cbe815d8d4829b0196839495b093775b&m=p9SRHZcKMYwLUgLF4TtmqRjoKOQ-0GgurIPQMYQODxMUYYYgdQHk91SiwA==)
* Says she would support adding to the number of Supreme Court justices to, “[get our democracy working the way it needs to](https://us.list-manage.com/10osSnEyo0t?e=f3aa6419cd&c2id=cbe815d8d4829b0196839495b093775b&m=dYZYS-PrY2UbqzPe9zC91lamScvXQgdN3JEevlDW9ztgeQ2VEkmVxCHPAA==)”
* Says “[Trump’s ICE needs to be dismantled](https://us.list-manage.com/hSBG4REphdt?e=f3aa6419cd&c2id=cbe815d8d4829b0196839495b093775b&m=GKYMeBZgiAJz7ynyMUGahpSUABvXVw30_TJhlZ3WSWP4OqbDZrGZyGxlJw==)”
* Promises to [impeach](https://us.list-manage.com/6t_PX7gaD4Q?e=f3aa6419cd&c2id=cbe815d8d4829b0196839495b093775b&m=1s5kj5y-x8R7BAL6ZJ9GUCTNUsvETjf0kEBn1BhGTmnETk8TOFofOJZzQw==) Trump
* Wants to take away your [private insurance ](https://us.list-manage.com/15yWnlPwBo1?e=f3aa6419cd&c2id=cbe815d8d4829b0196839495b093775b&m=WwXV79FShrvGciPEYmqsmfzj2SFTu6gR5XwE9RtpGUD-WYCVit9mGc7D2g==)to fund government-run healthcare

Christian Urrutia:
* Is “[proud](https://us.list-manage.com/knejgiJKAZN?e=f3aa6419cd&c2id=cbe815d8d4829b0196839495b093775b&m=ooZ2abNcdghTxryEsJT5Z1fSb6qNY8rtDpXIZjW1cs3hLJaTifPua7Uyzw==)” to be endorsed by a leftist group founded by Bernie Sanders
* Calls to [abolish](https://us.list-manage.com/hp4rcukBPfp?e=f3aa6419cd&c2id=cbe815d8d4829b0196839495b093775b&m=3zzZuxYnsXWfF6La780R13XbASJdHBlOjUnwjx3aVQ10HkXbvQMihQYOMQ==) immigration enforcement

Carleigh Beriont:
* When asked about funding Medicare for All, her response was “[with money](https://us.list-manage.com/8lGNB8N6kRP?e=f3aa6419cd&c2id=cbe815d8d4829b0196839495b093775b&m=mVsL6jh4zVqtFbEttneBj7QyxkvJANSprAUEfEyJ9GZTVM_3dyLcoul-Lw==)”
* Calls to [abolish](https://us.list-manage.com/n2ZDi8HrbUJ?e=f3aa6419cd&c2id=cbe815d8d4829b0196839495b093775b&m=89tgw_Kf8LaV4IR4LkbY_R4eggEL52-8bvL9pz3PvfoIrn01dP-6jBSquA==) ICE

Sarah Chadzynski:
* Believes illegal immigrants are not illegal but “[undocumented](https://us.list-manage.com/e8WjC0bPwIf?e=f3aa6419cd&c2id=cbe815d8d4829b0196839495b093775b&m=CnoHW6Zya0hqvlVvcS5ZLmOtWz7agVwZWEum2kOWc98x068wGY3ZEyGrmg==)”

**The radical left knows NY-18 is a must-win seat.** They are going to spend big, run hard, and pull out every stop to keep Pat Ryan in office. We have to be ready to match them at every turn: on the doors, on the airwaves, and in every neighborhood across this district.

**Chairman Maltzie’s Statement on Yesterday’s NH-02 Democrat Debate**
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | **FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE** September 4th, 2026
---
| | | **CONTACT** karina@nhrsc.com

---
| |

CONCORD, N.H. — New Hampshire Republican State Committee Chairman Scott Maltzie released the following statement after last night’s NH-02 Democrat Debate:“Maggie Goodlander’s performance in last night’s debate was unacceptable for an incumbent,” **said NHGOP Chairman Scott Maltzie.** “She stood by her decision to urge the military to disobey ‘illegal orders,’ yet couldn’t name a single example. That answer alone should sound a warning bell in the minds of Granite Staters and make clear that she should not be sent back to Congress.”“As if things couldn’t have been worse, she couldn’t explain why she voted present on a resolution to condemn socialism. She has been a follower in Congress, not a leader. She doesn’t have an answer because she doesn’t want to lose her base. This unaccomplished Congresswoman has not earned another two years in office, and New Hampshire will send that message in November.”In case you missed it, here are the highlights:
Maggie Goodlander:
* She “[absolutely](https://us.list-manage.com/111adnYwYR3?e=f3aa6419cd&c2id=cbe815d8d4829b0196839495b093775b&m=zvrfVn2jt911tPur5IE50A_1NbpVtdz5Osn_-ttbcMmjDI-owjGEdApRQQ==)” stands by urging the military to disobey “illegal orders”, despite not being able to name a [single one](https://us.list-manage.com/NttcQNPFLTa?e=f3aa6419cd&c2id=cbe815d8d4829b0196839495b093775b&m=BN7y03VDnqamiYps-OxBIIGPfQbkzS6wqh5mwTf6zlxkpJy4sThDga0lNg==)
* [Cannot](https://us.list-manage.com/wVYTNm_0hG0?e=f3aa6419cd&c2id=cbe815d8d4829b0196839495b093775b&m=McdtsNu22xTw4k-L1HgnnDieL11zAyR1jc7O7CGiIP5GFJRhlDyL6EQmvw==) give an answer to why she voted present on condemning socialism
* [Bragged](https://us.list-manage.com/2yXNnWcdUCT?e=f3aa6419cd&c2id=cbe815d8d4829b0196839495b093775b&m=BJ5dGeu50_dKs1MHUqdtE0sWFkdn7iju54I-5AP_gSjdB5LczakCWYakBg==) about impeaching President Trump
* Called law enforcement a “[gestapo-like force](https://us.list-manage.com/13Uw9nEtYBL?e=f3aa6419cd&c2id=cbe815d8d4829b0196839495b093775b&m=zDJLvoH-NeCMbgdHJTBlkeZyWCkqpjGSq9za5Mi5mc3GsFKEDrWEZC8ZNQ==)”

Paige Beauchemin:
* Refuses to condemn antisemitism say, “[it’s a lazy concept](https://us.list-manage.com/trtFhJ4ro3j?e=f3aa6419cd&c2id=cbe815d8d4829b0196839495b093775b&m=9zQ3LNsZ8EqwnTckD_tZsHuUXijj9rL_YiwAYqeZFFTLzKuohoFkQIabyQ==)”
* Cannot name a [single charge](https://us.list-manage.com/19geKhsAxVT?e=f3aa6419cd&c2id=cbe815d8d4829b0196839495b093775b&m=CNQUTUeWJSHqS61OhXOvkuPpKgykJgQ0BqoKfhqOica2_34BpU8QGyXjnA==) she would use to impeach President Trump
* Called the Laken Riley Act one of the “[worst pieces of legislation](https://us.list-manage.com/nfQNDJ5hH4C?e=f3aa6419cd&c2id=cbe815d8d4829b0196839495b093775b&m=AEmU54eWXcyOOZ5CqWMQUoUYPwd-JwuUT8CN4vKv_uqQuisqTDStLtXrow==)”

We want to make sure you have the facts — because there's a lot of confusion right now about mail-in voting in Arizona. Here's what you need to know: **Nothing has changed.** Secretary of State Adrian Fontes put it plainly: "The most important thing for Arizona voters to know today is simple: nothing has changed. You can still vote by mail in Arizona." But here's why we're alarmed. The Supreme Court recently cleared the way for parts of Trump's executive order on mail-in voting to move forward — an order that directs the U.S. Postal Service to only deliver ballots to people on DHS-created lists of eligible voters. In the 2020 election, **90% of Arizona voters cast their ballots by mail.** Trump's order threatens every single one of them. Attorney General Kris Mayes — who sued the Trump administration over the order — said: "So many veterans and rural Arizonans vote by mail. That's how 80 to 90% vote." Arizona and about two dozen Democratic-led states just filed a new lawsuit against the U.S. Postal Service challenging Trump's executive order — marking a new phase in the high-stakes litigation just two days after the Supreme Court ruled against them in a separate case. The fight is not over. And Arizona Democrats are in it. Here's what you can do right now: **✓ Make a plan to vote.**
Arizona's last day to register to vote in the November 3rd General Election is coming up fast. Make sure you're registered at **[Arizona.vote](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138591324/644533794/-1138595842?refcode=AU_AZD_FR_GEN_GEN_AC_20260904_PM1_V1_S2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjUvMS8xMDU1MTYiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMjJmNTAxYzAtOTJhOC1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAyMjQ4MmE5MzNiIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=6oc6DJzGQt_Q3Kmcc10plsUgJh73ijLaFoc6Nrv4GgI=&emci=1ef501c0-92a8-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&emdi=22f501c0-92a8-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&ceid=9307116)**. **✓ Vote early — and vote now.**
If you're voting by mail, return your ballot as soon as you receive it. Don't wait. Drop it at an official ballot drop box or voting location by 7:00 p.m. on Election Day. **✓ Track your ballot.**
You can track your ballot every step of the way through the Arizona Voter Information Portal at **[Arizona.vote](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138591325/644533797/-1138595842?refcode=AU_AZD_FR_GEN_GEN_AC_20260904_PM1_V1_S2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjUvMS8xMDU1MTYiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMjJmNTAxYzAtOTJhOC1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAyMjQ4MmE5MzNiIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=6oc6DJzGQt_Q3Kmcc10plsUgJh73ijLaFoc6Nrv4GgI=&emci=1ef501c0-92a8-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&emdi=22f501c0-92a8-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&ceid=9307116)**. **✓ Spread the word.**
Forward this email to friends and family who vote by mail and make sure they know their right to vote is protected — for now. Arizona Democrats are fighting in the courts, on the ground, and at the ballot box to make sure every Arizonan's vote is counted. [**Will you chip in $10 or whatever you can today to help us protect mail-in voting and turn out every Democratic vote in November?**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138591326/644533799/-390295490?amount=10&refcode=AU_AZD_FR_GEN_GEN_AC_20260904_PM1_V1_S2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjUvMS8xMDU1MTYiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMjJmNTAxYzAtOTJhOC1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAyMjQ4MmE5MzNiIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=6oc6DJzGQt_Q3Kmcc10plsUgJh73ijLaFoc6Nrv4GgI=) | [PROTECT ARIZONA'S VOTES →](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138591327/644533801/-390295490?amount=10&refcode=AU_AZD_FR_GEN_GEN_AC_20260904_PM1_V1_S2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjUvMS8xMDU1MTYiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMjJmNTAxYzAtOTJhOC1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAyMjQ4MmE5MzNiIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=6oc6DJzGQt_Q3Kmcc10plsUgJh73ijLaFoc6Nrv4GgI=)

clean_body: | = We want to make sure you have the facts — because there's a lot of confusion right now about mail-in voting in Arizona. Here's what you need to know: Nothing has changed. Secretary of State Adrian Fontes put it plainly: "The most important thing for Arizona voters to know today is simple: nothing has changed. You can still vote by mail in Arizona." But here's why we're alarmed. The Supreme Court recently cleared the way for parts of Trump's executive order on mail-in voting to move forward — an order that directs the U.S. Postal Service to only deliver ballots to people on DHS-created lists of eligible voters. In the 2020 election, 90% of Arizona voters cast their ballots by mail. Trump's order threatens every single one of them. Attorney General Kris Mayes — who sued the Trump administration over the order — said: "So many veterans and rural Arizonans vote by mail. That's how 80 to 90% vote." Arizona and about two dozen Democratic-led states just filed a new lawsuit against the U.S. Postal Service challenging Trump's executive order — marking a new phase in the high-stakes litigation just two days after the Supreme Court ruled against them in a separate case. The fight is not over. And Arizona Democrats are in it. Here's what you can do right now: ✓ Make a plan to vote. Arizona's last day to register to vote in the November 3rd General Election is coming up fast. Make sure you're registered at . ✓ Vote early — and vote now. If you're voting by mail, return your ballot as soon as you receive it. Don't wait. Drop it at an official ballot drop box or voting location by 7:00 p.m. on Election Day. ✓ Track your ballot. You can track your ballot every step of the way through the Arizona Voter Information Portal at . ✓ Spread the word. Forward this email to friends and family who vote by mail and make sure they know their right to vote is protected — for now. Arizona Democrats are fighting in the courts, on the ground, and at the ballot box to make sure every Arizonan's vote is counted. = | = Nothing has changed today. But the fight is far from over. 💙🌵 – Arizona Democratic Party Arizona Democratic Party PO Box 36123 Phoenix, AZ 85067-6123 United States mailto:info@azdem.org | PAID FOR BY THE ARIZONA DEMOCRATIC PARTY. _**Cliff 's Note:**_
##### I have known Jake Tapper a long time. So has David. So, it turns out, has Hunter Biden--about thirty years, going back to when Jake was a kid in Washington and nobody had heard of him.
##### That is what makes the clip below different from every other cable-news complaint you have read this year. Hunter is not making an argument about media bias in the abstract. He is telling you where a specific book came from, who was originally writing it, and what it was originally about. And then he says the quietest, most alarming sentence in the whole interview, which is that he was there for all of it and he remembers.
##### The clip is free. Watch it.
##### [The full ninety minutes is for paid subscribers](https://substack.com/redirect/f17adc4c-9df3-4ef4-9824-ea627125fb42?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). _**-- Cliff**_
In 2015, a reporter named Alex Thompson was writing a book about Beau Biden.
Beau had stage four glioblastoma. The prognosis is about two years and almost nobody beats it. He was also deciding whether to run for governor, which meant he was careful about what he said publicly about his own condition. Hunter explains why, and it is the part of this that stopped me:
"My brother wanted to believe, like me and his entire family and everyone that loved him, that he was going to beat all the odds--that he was going to be that 0.02 percent that makes it out. And that's the only way that you can enter into the fight that is required of you, just by virtue of wanting to live."
Out of that guardedness grew a storyline: the Bidens are secretive about their health. Nine years later that storyline had a much bigger subject. Same reporter. Much bigger name on the cover.
Hunter traces the whole thing there. He also does not spare his father: he says he panicked the moment Joe Biden walked out on that debate stage, that he had never seen him like that before and has not since. What he will not accept is who got graded on it--while Donald Trump talked for ninety minutes and nobody in the room stopped him once.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/45dda6b7-a0b3-4966-9fe9-176d9ec2e5e4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
That clip is twelve minutes of an hour and a half. Behind that card: the distinction he draws about addiction that I have never heard anyone make in public. The paintings, the congressional subpoenas, and the billions in federal contracts going to the current president's family. What he actually thinks about Kamala Harris distancing herself from his father. An argument about Pharaoh I am still turning over. He did not dodge a single question.

Sometimes, I have no other option. My husband and I still own our auto repair shop in rural Skamania County, and like so many families out here, we've had to figure out child care one day at a time. Around here, it's not just expensive—sometimes there simply isn't an opening anywhere. **_How are you supposed to go to work if there’s nowhere safe for your child to go?_** That's why I worked with Republicans and Democrats to introduce legislation that expands access to child care in rural communities like ours. Because parents shouldn't have to choose between earning a paycheck and caring for their kids. I've always believed the best ideas come from people who have actually lived the problem they're trying to solve. That's the perspective I bring to Congress every day. **[If you believe DC needs more representatives who solve real problems instead of chasing political fights, will you chip in $10 or whatever you can today?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138593477/644540493/-995582223?refcode=260904-childcare&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NTkyOCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwODY4YWRlZC05NmE4LWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTkzM2IiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=nU_5Bt5yymZKhLLnFOwJLpL2j3l5hT8M1NgNmHp63FE=)**

Teammates, We are **_exactly_****60 days** from Election Day, and every single one of them counts. This race is a toss-up, which means flipping NY-17 is possible — but it is _not_ guaranteed. The whole country is watching, and taking back the House runs right through NY-17. So we MUST get this done! But it is going to be a really hard fight. That means we need to approach every day with the urgency and purpose like we are running from behind. For the next 9 weeks we need all hands on deck knocking doors, making calls, and talking to voters across the district. This election is about protecting American values, ensuring families can do more than just make ends meet, and sending someone to Congress who will fight for the Hudson Valley. That is what's on the line this election. We need you out there with us. Because together we can win and make a real difference.
Team Cait

H.J. Resolution 1 has
failed in Congress.

The GOP designed this resolution to block any expansion of the Supreme
Court — a direct threat to judicial independence.

But let’s be honest: while the GOP’s effort to lock in a stacked court
suffered a setback, the crisis facing our judicial system hasn’t vanished.

It’s now clearer than ever that expanding the Supreme Court isn't radical
anymore. It's mainstream.

Why the shift? Voters are done with a Court that answers to billionaires,
not to them. Done with a Court that allows unlimited corporate cash in our
elections. Done with a Court that guts our rights while protecting the
powerful.

They've watched this Court dismantle basic protections through backdoor
"shadow docket" rulings, gut the Voting Rights Act, and rule in favor of
Trump and his allies more often than not.

Voters see the con for what it is: our courts, meant to serve
independently, are instead operating as a partisan weapon for the powerful
— a shield for corruption rather than a safeguard for our rights.

This is why Demand Justice exists. We’re exposing judicial corruption at
all levels and building the case for real structural reform — because a
broken Court doesn't fix itself.

With so much at stake, we
can’t afford to step back now.

name: Sr. Anne Elizabeth Eder
subject: They have no place to go
body:
The situation isn't good.

| | | |
---
| |
---
| | | Dear Friend, "We have no place to go." That's what Sister Francois-Dorothee tells me the poor children of the impoverished town of Matjieskloof in South Africa keep telling her. The situation isn't good. The children of Matjieskloof always had a hard life. It's a small town where most of the homes are made of tin siding and indoor plumbing is non-existent. But now things have gotten so much worse. At the start of this past year, schools in South Africa were still shut down and the kids literally had no place to go. With no air conditioning, internet, or even much space in their homes, staying inside hasn't been an option in the sweltering African heat. **So kids have taken to playing in the small garbage dumps that litter the town. ** And those are the kids that haven't tragically fallen prey to alcohol, drugs, and other horrible things that the gangs of a nearby city peddle them. No one is watching these children and they have nowhere to go. [That's why the Oblate Sisters of Saint Francis de Sales want to give those children a place of their own. And it's why I'm asking today if you'll help. ](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyUkcGOmzAURb_G7BxhYwxesEhFqKJO2mqQpkvr2X4QjwxG2KTq31cZdT6g26P3rnTu_XXTN_DBr_N3WLDzKek96XzHP3d44Bq3ABZznKPmJZe0VLQUGmz2D9QCCtfVnLVTW2DHmrata8ZYU9w7C04KqZzhyCcrGlmpBo0TkvESS8UK3z3zSlUKpkTNmpNyOAnjmKmxqUFWRJTH5iDjya_JO0w2xm2LwWdv0ynucxG6e85bItWZ8IHwIaE9djzBii7mk40L4UM0ATLS5FPGPdE40ZTptMNqfaIOaYKAifBhg0ZZy01NpRNARf2-vNuWgpkcdYqhMVaYlrWkGo686BSP3SKp-tfLG-HyiRZ0_lhI1V9u5-vLP2hh2cDPK6n6D922YvpL_1X_GIdRv17e9Mexvn17GejPM72O4-djXDOumVT9dRxH-tlVsXdu--1D8Ek2RJTzAj48VYv839M9Ov43AAD__3DHo90) **Sister Francois-Dorothee — who leads our mission in Matjieskloof — has cleared off some land** **and started building an outdoor community center (with the help of some older children)... ** **...so kids have a safe place to be kids.** The children in town are very excited and have been using their crayons to show how they would like this space to look. I wish you could see the beaming smiles on these children imagining what it would be like to have a place to play that isn't a garbage dump. But the Oblate Sisters would like this space to be so much more. We want this to be a place where children can be taught daily. Fed daily. And where our Sisters can pray with them daily. However, with just the Sisters and children themselves working on this center, progress has been moving far too slow. These children can't wait years. They're losing their childhoods right now. Unfortunately, it's not going to be cheap to hire professionals who can build quickly. And our Sisters in Matjieskloof just don't have that kind of money. **Which is why Sister Francois-Dorothee has asked me to reach out to people like you who might be able to help.** My name is Sister Anne Elizabeth Eder and I'm the North American Delegate for the Oblate Sisters of Saint Francis de Sales. Saint Leonie Aviat founded the Oblate Sisters of Saint Francis de Sales in 1866 after visiting a factory and seeing the harsh conditions that so many were working under. She knew that these least privileged in society especially needed to hear the words of Christ. Our mission in Matjieskloof was founded under her direction in 1885. **[And in our 138 years in Matjieskloof, I'm not sure if the children there have ever needed our help more than now. ](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyUkcGOmzAURb_G7BxhYwxesEhFqKJO2mqQpkvr2X4QjwxG2KTq31cZdT6g26P3rnTu_XXTN_DBr_N3WLDzKek96XzHP3d44Bq3ABZznKPmJZe0VLQUGmz2D9QCCtfVnLVTW2DHmrata8ZYU9w7C04KqZzhyCcrGlmpBo0TkvESS8UK3z3zSlUKpkTNmpNyOAnjmKmxqUFWRJTH5iDjya_JO0w2xm2LwWdv0ynucxG6e85bItWZ8IHwIaE9djzBii7mk40L4UM0ATLS5FPGPdE40ZTptMNqfaIOaYKAifBhg0ZZy01NpRNARf2-vNuWgpkcdYqhMVaYlrWkGo686BSP3SKp-tfLG-HyiRZ0_lhI1V9u5-vLP2hh2cDPK6n6D922YvpL_1X_GIdRv17e9Mexvn17GejPM72O4-djXDOumVT9dRxH-tlVsXdu--1D8Ek2RJTzAj48VYv839M9Ov43AAD__3DHo90)**I know you're miles and miles away from these children, but today you can have a big impact on their lives. Specifically, I am asking you to do two things:
---
| | | **1\. Will you pray for the children of Matjieskloof?** Please pray they find the strength to make it through the hardships of their daily lives. **2\. Will you send a one-time gift of $25** so we can finish building the urgently needed outdoor community center for the children of Matjieskloof — so our Oblate Sisters can continue to feed, educate, and pray with them?
---
| | | [ **DONATE ** ](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyUkcGOmzAURb_G7BxhYwxesEhFqKJO2mqQpkvr2X4QjwxG2KTq31cZdT6g26P3rnTu_XXTN_DBr_N3WLDzKek96XzHP3d44Bq3ABZznKPmJZe0VLQUGmz2D9QCCtfVnLVTW2DHmrata8ZYU9w7C04KqZzhyCcrGlmpBo0TkvESS8UK3z3zSlUKpkTNmpNyOAnjmKmxqUFWRJTH5iDjya_JO0w2xm2LwWdv0ynucxG6e85bItWZ8IHwIaE9djzBii7mk40L4UM0ATLS5FPGPdE40ZTptMNqfaIOaYKAifBhg0ZZy01NpRNARf2-vNuWgpkcdYqhMVaYlrWkGo686BSP3SKp-tfLG-HyiRZ0_lhI1V9u5-vLP2hh2cDPK6n6D922YvpL_1X_GIdRv17e9Mexvn17GejPM72O4-djXDOumVT9dRxH-tlVsXdu--1D8Ek2RJTzAj48VYv839M9Ov43AAD__3DHo90)
---
| | | I understand that it might not be easy to spare much, especially right now. I would never want you to give money that you truly need for your own family. But I know we often spend $25 without really thinking about it on things we truly don't need. These children need you. [**That's why if you can afford to send a larger amount — say $35, $50, or even $100 — it would be most appreciated.** ](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyUkcGOmzAURb_G7BxhYwxesEhFqKJO2mqQpkvr2X4QjwxG2KTq31cZdT6g26P3rnTu_XXTN_DBr_N3WLDzKek96XzHP3d44Bq3ABZznKPmJZe0VLQUGmz2D9QCCtfVnLVTW2DHmrata8ZYU9w7C04KqZzhyCcrGlmpBo0TkvESS8UK3z3zSlUKpkTNmpNyOAnjmKmxqUFWRJTH5iDjya_JO0w2xm2LwWdv0ynucxG6e85bItWZ8IHwIaE9djzBii7mk40L4UM0ATLS5FPGPdE40ZTptMNqfaIOaYKAifBhg0ZZy01NpRNARf2-vNuWgpkcdYqhMVaYlrWkGo686BSP3SKp-tfLG-HyiRZ0_lhI1V9u5-vLP2hh2cDPK6n6D922YvpL_1X_GIdRv17e9Mexvn17GejPM72O4-djXDOumVT9dRxH-tlVsXdu--1D8Ek2RJTzAj48VYv839M9Ov43AAD__3DHo90)Please don't forget the words of our Savior: _"Whatever you did for one of these least brothers of mine, you did for me."_ So if you've been particularly blessed and can give a larger amount, I hope you'll consider gifts of $250, $500, $1,000, or even $10,000. But any gift will help us. Whether you give $25 or $1,000, I thank you for helping shine light into the lives of these children. You'll be in my prayers.
---
| | | God Bless,
---
| | |
---
| | **Sister Anne Elizabeth Eder** Oblate Sisters of Saint Francis de Sales

clean_body: The situation isn't good. | | | | | | | | | Dear Friend, "We have no place to go." That's what Sister Francois-Dorothee tells me the poor children of the impoverished town of Matjieskloof in South Africa keep telling her. The situation isn't good. The children of Matjieskloof always had a hard life. It's a small town where most of the homes are made of tin siding and indoor plumbing is non-existent. But now things have gotten so much worse. At the start of this past year, schools in South Africa were still shut down and the kids literally had no place to go. With no air conditioning, internet, or even much space in their homes, staying inside hasn't been an option in the sweltering African heat. So kids have taken to playing in the small garbage dumps that litter the town. And those are the kids that haven't tragically fallen prey to alcohol, drugs, and other horrible things that the gangs of a nearby city peddle them. No one is watching these children and they have nowhere to go. Sister Francois-Dorothee — who leads our mission in Matjieskloof — has cleared off some land and started building an outdoor community center (with the help of some older children)... ...so kids have a safe place to be kids. The children in town are very excited and have been using their crayons to show how they would like this space to look. I wish you could see the beaming smiles on these children imagining what it would be like to have a place to play that isn't a garbage dump. But the Oblate Sisters would like this space to be so much more. We want this to be a place where children can be taught daily. Fed daily. And where our Sisters can pray with them daily. However, with just the Sisters and children themselves working on this center, progress has been moving far too slow. These children can't wait years. They're losing their childhoods right now. Unfortunately, it's not going to be cheap to hire professionals who can build quickly. And our Sisters in Matjieskloof just don't have that kind of money. Which is why Sister Francois-Dorothee has asked me to reach out to people like you who might be able to help. My name is Sister Anne Elizabeth Eder and I'm the North American Delegate for the Oblate Sisters of Saint Francis de Sales. Saint Leonie Aviat founded the Oblate Sisters of Saint Francis de Sales in 1866 after visiting a factory and seeing the harsh conditions that so many were working under. She knew that these least privileged in society especially needed to hear the words of Christ. Our mission in Matjieskloof was founded under her direction in 1885. know you're miles and miles away from these children, but today you can have a big impact on their lives. Specifically, I am asking you to do two things: | | | 1\. Will you pray for the children of Matjieskloof? Please pray they find the strength to make it through the hardships of their daily lives. 2\. Will you send a one-time gift of $25 so we can finish building the urgently needed outdoor community center for the children of Matjieskloof — so our Oblate Sisters can continue to feed, educate, and pray with them? | | | | | | I understand that it might not be easy to spare much, especially right now. I would never want you to give money that you truly need for your own family. But I know we often spend $25 without really thinking about it on things we truly don't need. These children need you. don't forget the words of our Savior: "Whatever you did for one of these least brothers of mine, you did for me." So if you've been particularly blessed and can give a larger amount, I hope you'll consider gifts of $250, $500, $1,000, or even $10,000. But any gift will help us. Whether you give $25 or $1,000, I thank you for helping shine light into the lives of these children. You'll be in my prayers. | | | God Bless, | | | | | Sister Anne Elizabeth Eder Oblate Sisters of Saint Francis de Sales | | | | | | P.S. The children of Matjieskloof in South Africa have no place to go. They're literally playing in garbage dumps. We need to give them a safe place where they can be kids. Please make a one-time contribution of $25 or more to help these children during this critical time. | | | God bless you for your generosity. I will be praying for you. | | The Oblate Sisters of Saint Francis de Sales, Inc. is recognized as having exempt status under section 501(c)(3) ofthe Internal Revenue Code. Hollowing out the military's leadership corps has set us up for the exact scenario we now see playing out in the Middle East. Driscoll's departure comes amid pushback from commanders across all branches of the service as the White House pushes us closer to the brink of a ground invasion in Iran. Yet instead of working to end this disastrous illegal war, Hegseth is building a taxpayer-funded troll army of MAGA influencers inside the Pentagon to defend his glaring incompetence online. He killed the program built to protect civilian lives in our strikes because he decided it was "woke", and shortly after, an American strike killed a school full of little girls in Iran. Equally concerning are the reports that Hegseth has downplayed our own casualties and battle damage from his Iran war in ways Congress needs to investigate. And when one exhausted sailor from the Abraham Lincoln went overboard after nine brutal months at sea, Hegseth's Pentagon answered with disciplinary charges instead of a counselor. Feed them food that has not spoiled. Fix the plumbing. Bring them home when you said you would. **Any staff sergeant in the force manages all of that before their first cup of coffee.** Hegseth cannot, and a man who fails the logistical basics of the job does not magically succeed at the hard parts. The hard parts are deterring enemies and protecting American lives in the most volatile stretch of geopolitics in a generation, and he is failing those, too. Hegseth thinks you can wear patriotism as if it's a costume. Real leaders understand it is earned in sweat and in standing by your people when it counts. Pete Hegseth has spent his entire tenure at the Pentagon proving he slept through that lesson. And the past few weeks have shown a man so consumed with his own ego and reputation that he will always protect himself before he respects our troops. Let's begin with Hegseth's latest round of petty grievances gutting the senior leadership of every branch of our armed forces, most recently with the resignation of Army Secretary Dan Driscoll. | Hollowing out the military's leadership corps has set us up for the exact scenario we now see playing out in the Middle East. Driscoll's departure comes amid pushback from commanders across all branches of the service as the White House pushes us closer to the brink of a ground invasion in Iran. Yet instead of working to end this disastrous illegal war, Hegseth is building a taxpayer-funded troll army of MAGA influencers inside the Pentagon to defend his glaring incompetence online. He killed the program built to protect civilian lives in our strikes because he decided it was "woke", and shortly after, an American strike killed a school full of little girls in Iran. Equally concerning are the reports that Hegseth has downplayed our own casualties and battle damage from his Iran war in ways Congress needs to investigate. And when one exhausted sailor from the Abraham Lincoln went overboard after nine brutal months at sea, Hegseth's Pentagon answered with disciplinary charges instead of a counselor. Taking care of troops is the least complicated part of the whole enterprise. Feed them food that has not spoiled. Fix the plumbing. Bring them home when you said you would. Hegseth cannot, and a man who fails the logistical basics of the job does not magically succeed at the hard parts. Hegseth thinks you can wear patriotism as if it's a costume. Real leaders understand it is earned in sweat and in standing by your people when it counts. When I get to Congress, I will fight for his immediate removal and for real accountability for all of it. Dear Friend, A lot happens in the months when statehouses are dark. That is exactly the point of this week's email.We have 169 state lawmakers from two dozen states signed onto a letter to President Trump about the 2030 Census, and the list is still growing. We have a Georgia caucus that caught a secret twenty billion dollar deal cut four months after the legislature went home. And we have Oklahoma and South Carolina doing the unglamorous work nobody assigned them.Let's get into it.
---
|
---
**THE CENSUS LETTER** The Census Bureau decides how many seats in Congress your state gets for an entire decade. It has not had a Senate-confirmed director since February of last year. Nineteen months, an agency that redraws the political map of America, run by whoever happens to be filling in. So your **State Freedom Caucus Network** organized a letter to President Trump asking him to nominate one. The Federalist broke it on August 24 with 142 signatures. We are at 169 now, from two dozen states, and lawmakers are still adding their names.Here is why our members care so much. In 2022, the Census Bureau published its own audit of the 2020 count and admitted it got it wrong in fourteen states. It undercounted six, five of them Republican-led. It overcounted eight, six of them Democrat-led. Arkansas alone was short by more than five percent. The Bureau published all of that, apologized for none of it, and the congressional seats stayed exactly where that flawed count put them. Ten years of representation, handed out on numbers the government itself says were wrong. **Missouri Freedom Caucus Chairman Nick Schroer** put it plainly: "The U.S. Constitution calls for an actual enumeration of our citizens; not a misleading tally padded by illegal aliens and skewed by statistical gimmickry. President Trump must nominate a Census Bureau director who will restore that constitutional standard and ensure the 2030 Census accurately counts only U.S. citizens."Now here is the part we are proudest of. We started the letter with our own Freedom Caucus members, then took it to every single Republican state lawmaker in the country, in all fifty states, whether they have a Freedom Caucus or not. That is why you will find signers from Maine, Michigan and Wisconsin on that list. We are still sending it. **CALL TO ACTION.** Go look at the list of signers below. If your state representative or your state senator is not on it, call their office and tell them to sign. There is no form to fill out, because we only accept signatures that come from a lawmaker's official government email address, which is how we know every name on that list is real. The letter is already sitting in their inbox. Every Republican state lawmaker in America got it. Some of them got it twice.[**SEE THE FULL LIST OF SIGNERS**](http://give.statefreedomcaucus.org/ls/click?upn=u001.SSCAglCEkhp55PDWKhWTjoHWZ4tqlEaSTHuQd2qYNv9ek8Fd9uKvteqHLA5kyPoOTWAmoOKZl-2B9GnC9YhH-2FLWg-3D-3DhPTp_9XnTPLnaEjN9OHWhKYUffDeECIVzR9M-2B5LaO5RH8NVBZyx1SQGGYhOdwcjZYtHerCPoymoFE4cFFA5e60xHKVM0XuYXDCO69xV6X61a-2FFr3RbUotvwc-2BX7bPhUzveqf8ucRYFv66BQgvP5JFetwfsyTPYwZcDQXfAI7cViT6ibIDMuMsWvQmbV9gKUKFX4TML3LrRDMrnMPaWqWm09UrXABOMzdK17EfvnpGVKKYUPXkP8QCa0lavciAOqOxfQ13V7oJvOKX73wHW6b2VZMZo7VSedgfzAyB0njWbg10SCk-3D)
