**GEORGIA** Here is something most people never think about. A regular state legislator gavels in, votes for a few months, gavels out, and goes back to a full-time job. For most of the year, nobody at the statehouse is watching anything. Freedom Caucuses do not work that way. They are on duty 365 days a year, and the**Georgia Freedom Caucus** just showed you why that matters. The Georgia General Assembly adjourned on April 2. On July 21, with every legislator in the state back home at their day jobs, the Effingham County development authority quietly approved a twenty-billion-dollar OpenAI data center. Look at how it was done. The project moved under a code name, "Project Camellia." The development authority's own CEO was gagged by a non-disclosure agreement until eight days before the vote. Back in April, he told the public the authority "was not actively considering" a data center project while he was negotiating one. The vote itself was moved to a Tuesday at OpenAI's request, off the authority's normal schedule. Notice went out three business days ahead, which violates Georgia's seven-day requirement, to a grand total of seven email addresses. It was tacked to the building but never posted online. The local paper had already gone to press and would not print again until after the vote. Three OpenAI representatives showed up. Zero members of the public did. The vote was unanimous.And what did Effingham County taxpayers get for their trouble? A deal that cuts OpenAI's property tax assessment for fifteen years and freezes the rate. When that runs out, OpenAI has the option to buy the entire 1,400-acre property for ten dollars. Ten dollars.Your **Georgia Freedom Caucus** [caught it and said so out loud](http://give.statefreedomcaucus.org/ls/click?upn=u001.SSCAglCEkhp55PDWKhWTjja-2FX-2BHiJMkQeHavsUeprX-2BEIPiK97CZl6S91XhnjrGNK-2Byjfq9hfR0MO94rtzK0NCYwl2B-2FADf5mxBJdWOo0-2F8-3D8w08_9XnTPLnaEjN9OHWhKYUffDeECIVzR9M-2B5LaO5RH8NVBZyx1SQGGYhOdwcjZYtHerCPoymoFE4cFFA5e60xHKVM0XuYXDCO69xV6X61a-2FFr3RbUotvwc-2BX7bPhUzveqf8ucRYFv66BQgvP5JFetwfsyTPYwZcDQXfAI7cViT6ibKCe6VCPwNVww3BOKTvHhCM2ziqXpf4vHVfwa8EzgKtQkienIdSYePEqOotdM3-2Bs53ItXCHsHeHNO9vZIbtR6ZKOi3-2FV2W0A43fcmVk9DhD2yZLRqcLqviWRB3ugG4GpLg-3D), and they are right about the principle. **_Secretive deals like this are wrong_**. And taxpayers should not be subsidizing data centers, whether that comes as a check, a tax break, or a power bill that goes up because a server farm moved in down the road. As the caucus told every official in the state: take note.

Her argument is simple: Flock photographs and catalogs every vehicle that drives past, with no warrant and no suspicion of anything, which is precisely the kind of general search the Fourth Amendment was written to forbid. Three states, three of our caucuses, one fight. Our members are not letting this one go. **⚡️SOUTH CAROLINA** : Nobody in South Carolina really holds Clemson University accountable except your **South Carolina Freedom Caucus and their allies**. Almost a year ago to the day, the caucus demanded Clemson get rid of the professors who publicly celebrated the assassination of Charlie Kirk, and those people are gone. Long gone. This week the caucus [made public](http://give.statefreedomcaucus.org/ls/click?upn=u001.SSCAglCEkhp55PDWKhWTjoyqjO-2F7Lw7RiV-2F-2FO65-2FN-2BtDplmixcXRHAOpEf1lWAC4dXYGW2zCpzVHn-2Fn1pieQf4X3liFrRMt4BRgjjYWRaHw-3DDs6__9XnTPLnaEjN9OHWhKYUffDeECIVzR9M-2B5LaO5RH8NVBZyx1SQGGYhOdwcjZYtHerCPoymoFE4cFFA5e60xHKVM0XuYXDCO69xV6X61a-2FFr3RbUotvwc-2BX7bPhUzveqf8ucRYFv66BQgvP5JFetwfsyTPYwZcDQXfAI7cViT6ibKOOnYHaBFkqkItSdzyil-2BmItsVFP4qI48ZWixqg6GPPgtHah5OG-2FHOI992fsUfjanMW98XHFr63WmvxNMdjzwyVozrZ0wu84f-2FPcIK5SpNm-2BoAUgJk9YGnIkJDMTn2GW4-3D) a "land acknowledgement" buried in the syllabus for a K-3 reading course, informing the next generation of Palmetto State teachers that they are standing on stolen land and pointing them toward a group called "Decolonize Clemson." Clemson's funding next year isn't going to get rubber-stamped without the SC Freedom Caucus reminding voters what they are paying for.

clean_body: | | | | | Dear Friend, A lot happens in the months when statehouses are dark. That is exactly the point of this week's email.We have 169 state lawmakers from two dozen states signed onto a letter to President Trump about the 2030 Census, and the list is still growing. We have a Georgia caucus that caught a secret twenty billion dollar deal cut four months after the legislature went home. And we have Oklahoma and South Carolina doing the unglamorous work nobody assigned them.Let's get into it. | THE CENSUS LETTER The Census Bureau decides how many seats in Congress your state gets for an entire decade. It has not had a Senate-confirmed director since February of last year. Nineteen months, an agency that redraws the political map of America, run by whoever happens to be filling in. So your State Freedom Caucus Network organized a letter to President Trump asking him to nominate one. The Federalist broke it on August 24 with 142 signatures. We are at 169 now, from two dozen states, and lawmakers are still adding their names.Here is why our members care so much. In 2022, the Census Bureau published its own audit of the 2020 count and admitted it got it wrong in fourteen states. It undercounted six, five of them Republican-led. It overcounted eight, six of them Democrat-led. Arkansas alone was short by more than five percent. The Bureau published all of that, apologized for none of it, and the congressional seats stayed exactly where that flawed count put them. Ten years of representation, handed out on numbers the government itself says were wrong. Missouri Freedom Caucus Chairman Nick Schroer put it plainly: "The U.S. Constitution calls for an actual enumeration of our citizens; not a misleading tally padded by illegal aliens and skewed by statistical gimmickry. President Trump must nominate a Census Bureau director who will restore that constitutional standard and ensure the 2030 Census accurately counts only U.S. citizens."Now here is the part we are proudest of. We started the letter with our own Freedom Caucus members, then took it to every single Republican state lawmaker in the country, in all fifty states, whether they have a Freedom Caucus or not. That is why you will find signers from Maine, Michigan and Wisconsin on that list. We are still sending it. CALL TO ACTION. Go look at the list of signers below. If your state representative or your state senator is not on it, call their office and tell them to sign. There is no form to fill out, because we only accept signatures that come from a lawmaker's official government email address, which is how we know every name on that list is real. The letter is already sitting in their inbox. Every Republican state lawmaker in America got it. Some of them got it twice. | GEORGIA Here is something most people never think about. A regular state legislator gavels in, votes for a few months, gavels out, and goes back to a full-time job. For most of the year, nobody at the statehouse is watching anything. Freedom Caucuses do not work that way. They are on duty 365 days a year, and theGeorgia Freedom Caucus just showed you why that matters. The Georgia General Assembly adjourned on April 2. On July 21, with every legislator in the state back home at their day jobs, the Effingham County development authority quietly approved a twenty-billion-dollar OpenAI data center. Look at how it was done. The project moved under a code name, "Project Camellia." The development authority's own CEO was gagged by a non-disclosure agreement until eight days before the vote. Back in April, he told the public the authority "was not actively considering" a data center project while he was negotiating one. The vote itself was moved to a Tuesday at OpenAI's request, off the authority's normal schedule. Notice went out three business days ahead, which violates Georgia's seven-day requirement, to a grand total of seven email addresses. It was tacked to the building but never posted online. The local paper had already gone to press and would not print again until after the vote. Three OpenAI representatives showed up. Zero members of the public did. The vote was unanimous.And what did Effingham County taxpayers get for their trouble? A deal that cuts OpenAI's property tax assessment for fifteen years and freezes the rate. When that runs out, OpenAI has the option to buy the entire 1,400-acre property for ten dollars. Ten dollars.Your Georgia Freedom Caucus , and they are right about the principle. Secretive deals like this are wrong. And taxpayers should not be subsidizing data centers, whether that comes as a check, a tax break, or a power bill that goes up because a server farm moved in down the road. As the caucus told every official in the state: take note. | RADIO CLIP OF THE WEEK Sit in a statehouse gallery for an afternoon and you will notice something. Confidence runs a long way ahead of knowledge in those rooms. Our friend Rep. Darin Chappell of the Missouri Freedom Caucus said it better than we can, and he said it in one sentence. Take a listen. 🎧 Subscribe on (or on your preferred podcast platform)📣 Follow us on X \- 👍 Follow us on Facebook \- | QUICK HITS ⚡️OKLAHOMA : We have told you twice now about the fight over Flock surveillance cameras, first in West Virginia and then in Missouri, and this week Oklahoma Freedom Caucus member Sen. Julie McIntosh . Her argument is simple: Flock photographs and catalogs every vehicle that drives past, with no warrant and no suspicion of anything, which is precisely the kind of general search the Fourth Amendment was written to forbid. Three states, three of our caucuses, one fight. Our members are not letting this one go. ⚡️SOUTH CAROLINA : Nobody in South Carolina really holds Clemson University accountable except your South Carolina Freedom Caucus and their allies. Almost a year ago to the day, the caucus demanded Clemson get rid of the professors who publicly celebrated the assassination of Charlie Kirk, and those people are gone. Long gone. This week the caucus a "land acknowledgement" buried in the syllabus for a K-3 reading course, informing the next generation of Palmetto State teachers that they are standing on stolen land and pointing them toward a group called "Decolonize Clemson." Clemson's funding next year isn't going to get rubber-stamped without the SC Freedom Caucus reminding voters what they are paying for. | WE NEED YOUR HELP TO KEEP THE MOMENTUM None of what you just read was in anybody's job description. The legislative session is out. No bills were considered. No votes taken.Our people do hard out-of-session work because they took the oath seriously, and because you stand behind them when they do. If you want more of this, you can pitch in right here. We'll be back with another update soon. Until then, please be sure to our efforts so that we can support our State Freedom Caucuses!In Liberty, Andy RothPresidentState Freedom Caucus Network | |

I was asked about my future this weekend. I told them I'm focused on yours.

| | | | Hey Fellow American, I was just on Meet the Press.... Kristen Welker asked me about 2028. About whether I'm going to run for president again. But here's the truth I told her on national television this weekend, and the truth I want to tell you directly right now: **This is not the season right now.** In the last decade, there has not been another Republican who has campaigned for more Senate candidates, more House candidates, more gubernatorial candidates than I have. I have been on the road. I have been in the arena. I have shown up in states where it was hard and uncomfortable and politically complicated, because that's what this fight demands. __I am doing it again right now_._ I need you to understand what we're actually fighting because this isn't just about seats and majorities and who controls which chamber. This is about something far bigger. **_The Democrat Party I came up watching is gone_.** What replaced it is something my father would have recognized immediately, because he lived it. He was tortured in a Cuban prison. He watched his country get strangled by a communist regime that promised the people everything, free healthcare, free education, power to the people, and delivered misery, silence, and chains. **That ideology, socialism, Marxism, the DSA agenda, is winning Democratic primaries across this country right now.** They elected a Democratic Socialist as mayor of New York City. Their endorsed candidates swept primaries in Michigan and Florida. And now that same machine is flooding money into Senate races that were never supposed to be competitive. **Texas. Iowa. Alaska. Michigan. Georgia.** James Talarico alone has $21.5 million in the bank to try to flip the Texas Senate seat. Democrats are outraising Republicans in nearly every battleground state. The Cook Political Report recently called both Texas and Iowa toss-ups. **_The map is shifting, and money is the reason_.** Chuck Schumer only needs a few of these seats to take back the majority. And the moment he does and the tax cuts get reversed, the border gets opened, conservative judges get blocked, and everything we have fought for gets dismantled piece by piece by people who openly admire the ideology that destroyed my father's country. _I will not let that happen._ I told Kristen Welker this weekend that this is the season of the midterms. I meant it. I am going to spend every day between now and November 3rd on the road, on the trail, fighting for every conservative candidate who needs someone to show up for them. **But I need to know you're fighting with me.** Not in October when it's almost too late. Lead Story · The 2026 MapMISSOURI'S HIGH COURT BLOCKS THE GOP CONGRESSIONAL MAP, SENDING IT TO A NOVEMBER REFERENDUMWhat's Happening
* The Missouri Supreme Court ruled **unanimously** Thursday that the state's newly enacted Republican-drawn congressional map cannot be used in November unless voters approve it in a statewide referendum.
* The court held the referendum petition "was legal, sufficient, and timely, and the secretary incorrectly concluded otherwise," and that the new map "did not go into effect and will not go into effect unless and until approved by the voters." The map drawn after the 2020 census "remains in full force and effect for the November 2026 general election."
* Opponents, organized as **People Not Politicians** , submitted **more than 300,000 signatures** to force the referendum. Rep. Emanuel Cleaver put the figure at "more than 305,000 Missourians" — the two counts have not been reconciled.
* Republican Secretary of State **Denny Hoskins** rejected that petition on primary Election Day last month, arguing referendums cannot be used for congressional redistricting. A lower court agreed with him before the high court reversed both.
* Attorney General **Catherine Hanaway** (R) is appealing to the U.S. Supreme Court: "Never before in American history has a court overturned a congressional map after a primary and before a general election. This unprecedented decision clearly violates federal law and has thrust our state into a full-fledged constitutional crisis."

The Situation
* Republicans hold **six of Missouri's eight** U.S. House seats. The new lines were drawn to put a **seventh** in reach by pushing Cleaver's Kansas City-based 5th District east into rural territory.
* Missouri **already held its primaries under the new map**. Candidates who won those primaries will now run under the old boundaries.
* **Five of the seven** justices on the court, including the chief justice, were appointed by Republican governors.
* President Trump on Truth Social called the ruling "horrible, ridiculous, and unConstitutional" and said "This is a Dark Day for 'Justice' in Missouri!" He added that "there won't be enough time to change the map back with the Election coming up in a very short period of time." The constitutional claim is attributed in his post only to unnamed "Legal Scholars."
* Gov. **Mike Kehoe** (R), who signed the map last September, said he is "extremely disappointed in today's decision by unelected judges and their lack of respect for the legislative process." Cleaver posted that "the people fought back and won."

The PerspectiveOverturning a map after a primary has been run under it is genuinely disruptive, and Hanaway is right that voters and candidates deserve better than musical-chairs districts nine weeks out. But conservatives should be careful which argument they pick up here. This was a unanimous court, five of whose seven members were seated by Republican governors, enforcing a referendum right written into Missouri's own constitution — the same tool the right has used to fight tax hikes and Medicaid expansion in that state. The complaint that carries weight is the timing. The complaint that "unelected judges" thwarted the legislature does not, because the thing they enforced was a vote of the people. The EconomyDEBT HITS $40 TRILLION AND HOUSE REPUBLICANS START TALKING ABOUT A FISCAL COMMISSIONWhat's Happening
* The national debt crossed **$40 trillion** last month. The **House Budget Committee** will hold a full hearing on creating a bipartisan fiscal commission to address deficits.
* Budget Chairman **Jodey Arrington** (R-Texas) said the hearing is about "how we create this mechanism," pointing to three precedents: the **BRAC** base-closing commission, the **1983 National Commission on Social Security Reform** , and **Simpson-Bowles** in 2010.
* Rep. **Bryan Steil** (R-Wis.): "I've been a supporter of a fiscal commission for a long time... I think we need to ultimately have the adult conversation with the American people and bring a resolution to the floor and address it."
* Rep. **Greg Murphy** (R-N.C.), of Ways and Means, on the debt: "I'm terrified of it myself... the day of reckoning is coming."
* Not everyone is sold. Rep. **Eric Burlison** (R-Mo.) of the Freedom Caucus: "Do we really need to study the problem? I think it's a clear math problem... we all know what we need to do, and that's reduce spending."

The Situation
* Bond markets are the forcing function. After the $40 trillion mark, 30-year Treasury yields reached levels not seen in roughly two decades, and the 10-year pushed closer to 5% earlier this week. Exact figures were not published with the report — treat the levels as directional.
* Rep. **Nathaniel Moran** (R-Texas) said he has only "begun to hear from constituents about the yield issue just in the last week or so."
* Rep. **Darin LaHood** (R-Ill.) named the political problem plainly: "We're at an existential point in terms of where our debt is at. The scary part is you do polling, and you ask the American people the top 10 issues, debt and deficit isn't in the top 10."
* **Carolyn Bourdeaux** , a former Georgia Democratic congresswoman now running the Concord Coalition: "Mortgages, car loans, credit card debt, small-business loans — these interest rates affect everything."
* Financial Services Chairman **French Hill** (R-Ark.), who prefers a balanced budget amendment, warned that Congress "has tended to wait" for "a real significant motivating demand signal." The 1983 Social Security commission was convened only after projections showed the trust fund running dry.

The PerspectiveBurlison is right on the math and wrong on the politics, which is the whole problem in one sentence. Everyone in that room knows spending is the driver; nobody wants to own the vote. That is precisely what a commission is for — not to discover the answer, but to distribute the blame widely enough that the answer can pass. Conservatives should be clear-eyed that commissions have historically arrived at tax increases alongside spending restraint, and should insist on a mandate weighted toward the latter before signing on. TradeLUTNICK SAYS CANADA'S LIBERALS BLEW UP THE TRADE DEAL "TO GET THEMSELVES ELECTED"What's Happening
* Commerce Secretary **Howard Lutnick** , in a Bloomberg interview, blamed the collapse of U.S.-Canada trade talks on Canadian domestic politics: "This is the Canadian Liberal Party using their economy to get themselves elected, even if they're selling their own citizens down the river. It's sad and disappointing."
* Talks **collapsed Aug. 21** , hours before a deadline set by President Trump.
* The latest tariff round covers roughly **$20 billion** of Canadian goods — **hockey sticks, wine, cement, lumber** , and certain apparel and beauty products. Canada has retaliated with tariffs of its own.
* Lutnick's account of the breakdown: "We worked... six weeks of negotiations, and we hammered out a deal." Then, "Friday at 4 o'clock, for example, my Canadian counterparts called me and said, 'We'd like heavy trucks.' And I said no... There's no new topic that you're coming up with now." He says he asked whether they were trying to blow up the deal and was told, "I'm not allowed to say that."
* On a dispute over French-language requirements, Lutnick called the issue "nonsense": "We have a deal with France. We have a deal with Italy. We have a deal with Germany. We don't care about their language."

The Situation
* Prime Minister **Mark Carney** tells it the other way. He blamed last-minute American changes he called "unfair" and "uneconomic," citing proposed shifts on automobile tariffs and restrictions on Canada's ability to negotiate trade deals with other countries. **Neither account has been independently corroborated** ; both are participants describing a closed-door negotiation.
* Lutnick's quotes reached American audiences through a clip of the Bloomberg interview posted by a White House account, not a full transcript — worth noting on framing, though the words themselves are his.
* Canada had initially sought an interim agreement ahead of a broader **USMCA** renegotiation, according to Lutnick.
* The tariffs stem from measures first announced in July and rest on a provision of a law dating to the Great Depression. The statute was not named in the reporting.
* Trump separately signed an executive order renaming Lake Ontario "Lake America," saying Canada has "been ripping us off for a long time on trade."

The PerspectiveIf Lutnick's version holds up, Ottawa reopened a closed deal for domestic political reasons and Canadian consumers are paying for it — and an administration that refuses to reward that is doing its job. But hockey sticks, wine and cement are not leverage against Ottawa; they are a tax on the Americans who buy them, and lumber tariffs land on the price of a house at a moment when affordability is the ballgame. The honest conservative position is that tariffs are a tool, not a virtue: worth using to force a better deal, not worth keeping if the deal never comes. Six weeks of negotiation produced an agreement once. The PentagonARMY SECRETARY RESIGNS, TRUMP NAMES ADAM TELLE ACTING, AND A GOP SENATOR CALLS FOR HEGSETH'S REMOVALWhat's Happening
* Army Secretary **Dan Driscoll** submitted his resignation this week and said Wednesday was his "last full day." His statement: "As a third-generation Army veteran, it has been the honor of a lifetime to serve as the Secretary of the Army under President Trump and Secretary Hegseth."
* Trump announced Thursday on Truth Social: "I am pleased to announce that Adam Telle, the current Assistant Secretary of the Army for Civil Works, will become Acting Secretary of the Army, effective immediately," calling him "a Great Patriot, who is respected by all."
* Telle was Senate-confirmed in 2025 for Civil Works, overseeing flood protection, waterways and Clean Water Act permitting. He previously served as chief of staff to **Sen. Bill Hagerty** (R-Tenn.), ran the White House legislative affairs Senate team in Trump's first term, worked on Senate Appropriations, and spent **10 years** with the late Sen. Thad Cochran (R-Miss.).
* Sen. **Thom Tillis** (R-N.C.), who is not seeking reelection, used the vacancy to call for Defense Secretary **Pete Hegseth's** removal: "I urge the President to find a new leader at the Pentagon who will retain and empower our military talent rather than diminish it."
* Tillis, citing eight years on Senate Armed Services: "I have never witnessed more inept management of the brave men and women who serve our country. He is intimidated by competence and retreats to ginning up culture wars instead of soberly attending to the vital work of our national defense."

The Situation
* The White House is not budging. Spokeswoman **Anna Kelly** : "The President has complete trust in Secretary Hegseth, who is doing an incredible job leading the Pentagon. The results of Operations Midnight Hammer, Absolute Resolve, Southern Spear, and Epic Fury speak for themselves." The War Department declined to comment.
* Reporting that Driscoll and Hegseth clashed over Army transformation and readiness — including a claim that Hegseth blocked those efforts by firing the generals responsible — rests on a **single source familiar with the matter, speaking anonymously**. There is no on-record confirmation of the dispute.
* This is escalation rather than a first strike from Tillis, who previously said he would "love to see Pete Hegseth fired because he's incompetent and doing a horrible job." His count of flag officers "forced into retirement" was not quantified.
* Tillis praised both Driscoll and retired Army chief of staff **Gen. Randy George** for "a transformative period of innovation in how we array our forces and equip our Soldiers."
* Telle is viewed as having strong Senate relationships, which matters because Army nominees are currently stalled in the Senate. He takes the job with U.S. forces engaged in an Iran conflict now past six months.

The PerspectiveA service secretary walking out during an active war is not an ordinary personnel note, and Tillis is a retiring senator with eight years on Armed Services and nothing left to gain by saying it out loud. That deserves a hearing, not a press release. At the same time, one anonymous source is thin evidence for the story everyone is telling about why Driscoll left, and Tillis has a history with Hegseth that colors the charge. The administration's own answer is a list of operation names, which is not the same as an account of why the Army keeps losing its civilian leadership. It's just the truth. | Friday, September 4, 2026| Missouri Map Blocked For November ---|--- 6-minute read · 4 stories Lead Story · The 2026 MapMISSOURI'S HIGH COURT BLOCKS THE GOP CONGRESSIONAL MAP, SENDING IT TO A NOVEMBER REFERENDUMWhat's Happening The Missouri Supreme Court ruled unanimously Thursday that the state's newly enacted Republican-drawn congressional map cannot be used in November unless voters approve it in a statewide referendum. The court held the referendum petition "was legal, sufficient, and timely, and the secretary incorrectly concluded otherwise," and that the new map "did not go into effect and will not go into effect unless and until approved by the voters." The map drawn after the 2020 census "remains in full force and effect for the November 2026 general election." Opponents, organized as People Not Politicians , submitted more than 300,000 signatures to force the referendum. Rep. Emanuel Cleaver put the figure at "more than 305,000 Missourians" — the two counts have not been reconciled. Republican Secretary of State Denny Hoskins rejected that petition on primary Election Day last month, arguing referendums cannot be used for congressional redistricting. A lower court agreed with him before the high court reversed both. Attorney General Catherine Hanaway (R) is appealing to the U.S. Supreme Court: "Never before in American history has a court overturned a congressional map after a primary and before a general election. This unprecedented decision clearly violates federal law and has thrust our state into a full-fledged constitutional crisis." The Situation Republicans hold six of Missouri's eight U.S. House seats. The new lines were drawn to put a seventh in reach by pushing Cleaver's Kansas City-based 5th District east into rural territory. Missouri already held its primaries under the new map. Candidates who won those primaries will now run under the old boundaries. Five of the seven justices on the court, including the chief justice, were appointed by Republican governors. President Trump on Truth Social called the ruling "horrible, ridiculous, and unConstitutional" and said "This is a Dark Day for 'Justice' in Missouri!" He added that "there won't be enough time to change the map back with the Election coming up in a very short period of time." The constitutional claim is attributed in his post only to unnamed "Legal Scholars." Gov. Mike Kehoe (R), who signed the map last September, said he is "extremely disappointed in today's decision by unelected judges and their lack of respect for the legislative process." Cleaver posted that "the people fought back and won." The PerspectiveOverturning a map after a primary has been run under it is genuinely disruptive, and Hanaway is right that voters and candidates deserve better than musical-chairs districts nine weeks out. But conservatives should be careful which argument they pick up here. This was a unanimous court, five of whose seven members were seated by Republican governors, enforcing a referendum right written into Missouri's own constitution — the same tool the right has used to fight tax hikes and Medicaid expansion in that state. The complaint that carries weight is the timing. The complaint that "unelected judges" thwarted the legislature does not, because the thing they enforced was a vote of the people. If the map is good policy, November is a chance to say so at the ballot box. The EconomyDEBT HITS $40 TRILLION AND HOUSE REPUBLICANS START TALKING ABOUT A FISCAL COMMISSIONWhat's Happening The national debt crossed $40 trillion last month. The House Budget Committee will hold a full hearing on creating a bipartisan fiscal commission to address deficits. Budget Chairman Jodey Arrington (R-Texas) said the hearing is about "how we create this mechanism," pointing to three precedents: the BRAC base-closing commission, the 1983 National Commission on Social Security Reform , and Simpson-Bowles in 2010. Rep. Bryan Steil (R-Wis.): "I've been a supporter of a fiscal commission for a long time... I think we need to ultimately have the adult conversation with the American people and bring a resolution to the floor and address it." Rep. Greg Murphy (R-N.C.), of Ways and Means, on the debt: "I'm terrified of it myself... the day of reckoning is coming." Not everyone is sold. Rep. Eric Burlison (R-Mo.) of the Freedom Caucus: "Do we really need to study the problem? I think it's a clear math problem... we all know what we need to do, and that's reduce spending." The Situation Bond markets are the forcing function. After the $40 trillion mark, 30-year Treasury yields reached levels not seen in roughly two decades, and the 10-year pushed closer to 5% earlier this week. Exact figures were not published with the report — treat the levels as directional. Rep. Nathaniel Moran (R-Texas) said he has only "begun to hear from constituents about the yield issue just in the last week or so." Rep. Darin LaHood (R-Ill.) named the political problem plainly: "We're at an existential point in terms of where our debt is at. The scary part is you do polling, and you ask the American people the top 10 issues, debt and deficit isn't in the top 10." Carolyn Bourdeaux , a former Georgia Democratic congresswoman now running the Concord Coalition: "Mortgages, car loans, credit card debt, small-business loans — these interest rates affect everything." Financial Services Chairman French Hill (R-Ark.), who prefers a balanced budget amendment, warned that Congress "has tended to wait" for "a real significant motivating demand signal." The 1983 Social Security commission was convened only after projections showed the trust fund running dry. The PerspectiveBurlison is right on the math and wrong on the politics, which is the whole problem in one sentence. Everyone in that room knows spending is the driver; nobody wants to own the vote. That is precisely what a commission is for — not to discover the answer, but to distribute the blame widely enough that the answer can pass. Conservatives should be clear-eyed that commissions have historically arrived at tax increases alongside spending restraint, and should insist on a mandate weighted toward the latter before signing on. But a party that campaigned on fiscal sanity cannot spend a decade calling $40 trillion an emergency and then treat the first serious mechanism to address it as somebody else's problem. TradeLUTNICK SAYS CANADA'S LIBERALS BLEW UP THE TRADE DEAL "TO GET THEMSELVES ELECTED"What's Happening Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick , in a Bloomberg interview, blamed the collapse of U.S.-Canada trade talks on Canadian domestic politics: "This is the Canadian Liberal Party using their economy to get themselves elected, even if they're selling their own citizens down the river. It's sad and disappointing." Talks collapsed Aug. 21 , hours before a deadline set by President Trump. The latest tariff round covers roughly $20 billion of Canadian goods — hockey sticks, wine, cement, lumber , and certain apparel and beauty products. Canada has retaliated with tariffs of its own. Lutnick's account of the breakdown: "We worked... six weeks of negotiations, and we hammered out a deal." Then, "Friday at 4 o'clock, for example, my Canadian counterparts called me and said, 'We'd like heavy trucks.' And I said no... There's no new topic that you're coming up with now." He says he asked whether they were trying to blow up the deal and was told, "I'm not allowed to say that." On a dispute over French-language requirements, Lutnick called the issue "nonsense": "We have a deal with France. We have a deal with Italy. We have a deal with Germany. We don't care about their language." The Situation Prime Minister Mark Carney tells it the other way. He blamed last-minute American changes he called "unfair" and "uneconomic," citing proposed shifts on automobile tariffs and restrictions on Canada's ability to negotiate trade deals with other countries. Neither account has been independently corroborated ; both are participants describing a closed-door negotiation. Lutnick's quotes reached American audiences through a clip of the Bloomberg interview posted by a White House account, not a full transcript — worth noting on framing, though the words themselves are his. Canada had initially sought an interim agreement ahead of a broader USMCA renegotiation, according to Lutnick. The tariffs stem from measures first announced in July and rest on a provision of a law dating to the Great Depression. The statute was not named in the reporting. Trump separately signed an executive order renaming Lake Ontario "Lake America," saying Canada has "been ripping us off for a long time on trade." The PerspectiveIf Lutnick's version holds up, Ottawa reopened a closed deal for domestic political reasons and Canadian consumers are paying for it — and an administration that refuses to reward that is doing its job. But hockey sticks, wine and cement are not leverage against Ottawa; they are a tax on the Americans who buy them, and lumber tariffs land on the price of a house at a moment when affordability is the ballgame. The honest conservative position is that tariffs are a tool, not a virtue: worth using to force a better deal, not worth keeping if the deal never comes. Six weeks of negotiation produced an agreement once. Somebody should go get it. The PentagonARMY SECRETARY RESIGNS, TRUMP NAMES ADAM TELLE ACTING, AND A GOP SENATOR CALLS FOR HEGSETH'S REMOVALWhat's Happening Army Secretary Dan Driscoll submitted his resignation this week and said Wednesday was his "last full day." His statement: "As a third-generation Army veteran, it has been the honor of a lifetime to serve as the Secretary of the Army under President Trump and Secretary Hegseth." Trump announced Thursday on Truth Social: "I am pleased to announce that Adam Telle, the current Assistant Secretary of the Army for Civil Works, will become Acting Secretary of the Army, effective immediately," calling him "a Great Patriot, who is respected by all." Telle was Senate-confirmed in 2025 for Civil Works, overseeing flood protection, waterways and Clean Water Act permitting. He previously served as chief of staff to Sen. Bill Hagerty (R-Tenn.), ran the White House legislative affairs Senate team in Trump's first term, worked on Senate Appropriations, and spent 10 years with the late Sen. Thad Cochran (R-Miss.). Sen. Thom Tillis (R-N.C.), who is not seeking reelection, used the vacancy to call for Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's removal: "I urge the President to find a new leader at the Pentagon who will retain and empower our military talent rather than diminish it." Tillis, citing eight years on Senate Armed Services: "I have never witnessed more inept management of the brave men and women who serve our country. He is intimidated by competence and retreats to ginning up culture wars instead of soberly attending to the vital work of our national defense." The Situation The White House is not budging. Spokeswoman Anna Kelly : "The President has complete trust in Secretary Hegseth, who is doing an incredible job leading the Pentagon. The results of Operations Midnight Hammer, Absolute Resolve, Southern Spear, and Epic Fury speak for themselves." The War Department declined to comment. Reporting that Driscoll and Hegseth clashed over Army transformation and readiness — including a claim that Hegseth blocked those efforts by firing the generals responsible — rests on a single source familiar with the matter, speaking anonymously. There is no on-record confirmation of the dispute. This is escalation rather than a first strike from Tillis, who previously said he would "love to see Pete Hegseth fired because he's incompetent and doing a horrible job." His count of flag officers "forced into retirement" was not quantified. Tillis praised both Driscoll and retired Army chief of staff Gen. Randy George for "a transformative period of innovation in how we array our forces and equip our Soldiers." * Telle is viewed as having strong Senate relationships, which matters because Army nominees are currently stalled in the Senate. He takes the job with U.S. forces engaged in an Iran conflict now past six months. The PerspectiveA service secretary walking out during an active war is not an ordinary personnel note, and Tillis is a retiring senator with eight years on Armed Services and nothing left to gain by saying it out loud. That deserves a hearing, not a press release. At the same time, one anonymous source is thin evidence for the story everyone is telling about why Driscoll left, and Tillis has a history with Hegseth that colors the charge. The administration's own answer is a list of operation names, which is not the same as an account of why the Army keeps losing its civilian leadership. Senate Armed Services should ask Driscoll to testify. Soldiers in the field are owed a chain of command that is stable, and taxpayers are owed an explanation that does not depend on a leak. | ⚡ The Bottom LineFour stories, one uncomfortable pattern: the hard decisions keep getting handed to somebody else. ## Nepal Principal Saves 1,643 Children from Flood
Rajendra Dawadi was in his office at Tribhuvan Trishuli Secondary School in Nepal's Nuwakot district when his phone rang around 9:20 a.m. on Aug. 26. A friend was [warning that a nearby village](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJysUD3OnTAQPA10RstiDBQu0rzuS5sS-XnXsJGxn4wFye0jcoavHM2PZubX1_rlJErafrqDbdjCWkNeE99n5Fq5rIdEPnMgvnKVnFx0iWIudK4IaBQsCvTqfJWLV-1asoEZeWjZ9tM8jyPiPLS75feAhkY9IgCgNhODX0bjA-F7BN23Yp88WEAjgNbYhTCYt_Y09aZfYDKNBiapuXS_s6S6c4h_88Wl8_loo91r_ZzN8KPBV4Ov-767RPV6yAfmEkk9qxp8Jf64qCo7v3NRhT3LxaRCzJnU7UqStKl7d1XtrEge35-qTveIemX0oPwukQon1ffLNKMxbbH0uSVGOc3UaNgOJ_F_sfoNn14W_wUAAP__F6iN0Q) had been swept away and telling him to run. Instead, the 47-year-old principal rang the school bell, evacuated the classrooms and told bus drivers to turn back. The children fled uphill and took shelter beneath a bodhi tree. Minutes later, floodwaters destroyed the school. [All 1,643 students survived](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyskbGupDAMRb8mdEEhZAIUFNvQvW23RB7iDFmFGGEPaP5-xav2A15jHcnSvTq6f77mL0g5lddv2HCMrzhLpLngxRlF8Ji3lJEpBjxJEhXIUEKmI_BsjfXaDNq4GRZJJ84OqjBGRItthWPT9f3jYW3fVus4DKFf2odvXQ9PCAGG-OgQo7fGhwhNlcY7zwzGWWOcs3WMrX-6JXSNbwbTeeUMhiR01H8pFVkx5g-deNQLbVUeV5GdVftL2UnZ6bquWlZkge9_vX2UnYARyp7f_D_r21XZ6W5XdjLDfRplp4I7ZL0fqSzpJoYTg268azXLO2AR1lsqb0HWT4x0oOZlJcr6AtYBWQ76YNCyYtGZWPSaWNNV9EobVscY9ivlnNh3ypnXBil_q8gPrHCO9l8AAAD___L-oYY), though two school workers were swept away. Rajendra lost his home too, but the destruction of the school hit harder. "_I feel more pain about losing the school than losing my own house_ ," he said. Rajendra is now [appealing to India for help rebuilding the school](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJysULsO2zAQ-xp7UyCfFD8GDV2ypWtHQ7FO9hVnnSCrDvL3hdNf6ESCIAiSv57z0xNTWn_6HV1c41yjzAnfB2OtWOadGA-JAU-pJMmzT4GlhGMGDb3Sk9J29kulE2fr2-AiIqBp0XXDON7vAKNpN2cHC-ANAvRmQT2MoZsMjCMa80Ibh5bclacnbUFra-EWo-lfdglD13eTHvrGagxUpdx-C6W6YeSPnFhui-wtu63WfDTmRwOPBh7BE38yScJ_hgYe16YvZM-H2rCIyoXSQtmz8jnjJVdRlAL5ixR8_SEOKrJIUMWffsWgjmUT4ba4kN_ETEc_NFavuyf-Nqn_4cTTwd8AAAD__x3Pi0I) so his students can return to class.
## Principal Stands By Homeless Student
Rob Burnside spent 31 years in education and was principal of Lakota East High School near Cincinnati when he learned one of his students, Landerius "DeDe" Hayes, was homeless. DeDe's mother had moved out of the district, and school officials told Burnside [the student had to go](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyskD1uhTAQhE9jOiOzmL_CRRq6lzYlMvYaNs-wCFug3D4iZ0g30kgz-r6v1_SyFGlfPu2GJixhyoGnHe8UMWc8p40iJg4eL87Eu41295FPnyZQ0Eo1SKUn6zJdOGlbeBMQAesCTdX1fdMA9HWxmg583zdBV82Mwaq5VxrbObi59k4NCgoyz54alAaltIYyhLqdtfNd1VaD6lqhFXrKfJbfTHteMcQfvvAsHW9FNGvORxL1h4BRwHjfd-nm9HA8vYDxiQJGXonlcdLu6LBRRvvmbCXalOVKyyqTW5mjnHF573wnaTc8yVkBY3Eaf9wUI6W2E1otm6X4d57_wdtl4DcAAP__0cSGsw). At times, DeDe slept in a car because his father’s mobile home was too cold. Rob couldn't accept it. He let DeDe keep attending classes. When he told his wife, Angel, about the situation, [her first words were](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyskL3OnDAQAJ8GOiOzmL_CRRq6L21KZPAa78l4ke0D3dtHl2dIPxqN5s_P-mMoUDx-mxO1O9xaHK8RnxywFEzrSQEzO4s3F-Jogok2cLJ5BQmDkLOQajV7oRtXZWqrHSJgV6Nux2nqe4Cpq71WvRzm2YLpFbbGuW1At29WYjeNuI1tTfrrk7NUIKVS0DjXDZva7dgO7SzHoVISLRVOzYspFo8ufPjG1Ox81kH7Uq5cdb8qWCpYnudp3tfDqfjPF6hgMVGwJxZXorjTZYIInIvwlMWLN0FRgAQlHCfhMVwUD2GE5xMD5ixyeVuMpYKlTtpeD4VAeRgrJY_TUPgXUf7Dv1vD3wAAAP__CgiJNA), "_Well, he can come stay with us_." DeDe moved in. The district found out and told Rob he could step down or be terminated. DeDe offered to leave so Rob could keep his job. Rob refused. "_DeDe, you're part of this family_ ," he told him. "_We're not gonna turn our back on you_." The Burnsides became DeDe's legal guardians, and he later attended a different high school. This past May, he graduated with Rob and Angel cheering from the stands. He's now [working toward becoming an aviation mechanic](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyskEHO2yAQRk-Dd0RkIDgsWGRjpVX_qmordWmRzODQYCYyxFZ6-io9Q_efPr33fn2MHyHlVKavYSYfpzi2yGOhrWZqjZZxTpkqR6SVW-ISciiYecE6ggIrlZPKjOHa0kqjCR36SASkO_L7_ng8HACOurt512uHuLdaO0vYK7CAx4OKOh6cUxfskn__KacMKGUM7GLU9mKu2O_t3qneCqMIU-Nl95tTaTeK-cUrLbsrz132t9YeVeiTgEHAsG3brj5LedX76897IWCYmFG-zQQMFpwSMHxbUrmmR8jyC1eq8pyq_MwXeYqNFvkz3FOZ5KcizzxTplrlj_ZEKk2eSX6n-KyEsrE8XUJBLt3i8bGlnFO1vTBqmkPK__Dafyi7evgbAAD__45wkLI).
## Husband Takes Paralyzed Wife on Epic Journey
Liu Peijin and his wife were childhood classmates who dreamed of exploring China together in retirement. In 2010, complications from diabetes left her partially paralyzed, and repeated hospital stays failed to improve her condition. Rather than give up on their dream, Liu loaded up a car in 2014 and [hit the road](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyskL_u3CAMx5-GbESEkMANDF2y_bp2jHzBXNwSiMC96N6-uuvSB-hiWbI-_v758bV-ASXKj-9woI-PuHIsa8arJWTGuh6UsJUY8FmYSoYEOaRSQ1u10rNUN6nMChvTE1cDXfARUePYoR-sc9OktRu73ceAdgKr8T47p-6bcwaDmaYBrDXjLXbk3__UTRmtlDG6j3Gc72YLdpiHm7KzMAoDcan9z0KZd4zpVZ5Y-60cXfI789nE-E3oRejluq6ed2wMn3t_vIReoCHkM_1u_-7ynVXo5a0u9KKc0MvwHoFQlix5R1kLBJkLS8pyL-0khiS3nTI2lAdkyfALmzyhQno1DPKi-IHxpO0vzZXOrvpwXpQStdkKox4HUPrY5__Q_NPrPwEAAP__n-OcPQ). He later upgraded to a campervan outfitted with two beds, a sink and dining table, and a full stock of medical supplies. He describes himself as "[the driver, cook, doctor, nurse, and carer, all in one](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJys0DGOnjAQBeDTQGdkjIGfwkUauk2bEg14DJM1HmSPQJvTR_vnCjnA9_Te-_WxfABFSvtPONGFPSwSeEn4lIgimJeTIhYOHm8W4gQRko-cfVmMNoPSk9J2gU3oxsVC7V1ANNjV6Nrx9ep7Y15dfTg92mA72FaArVvHwXYrDm0_rX2Po21DTe47T0_aGq2tNU0I3bDazY_t0E56HCqr0ZNwbn4zJTkwxC--MTcbn3V0h8hVqu5HZebKzM_zNDuz_x6SUB7Onw3nvTKzJ1SclByoMoNXiUVRUgeXiwSi2g5KWFCdkJTAJxZ1QYb49Qe9eii8MV60_dOS6arMXGfnr4dipDKMldX7CRTfxeQ_fHo78zcAAP__V6-RMA)." Over the past decade, they have traveled through 31 of China's provincial-level regions, sometimes spending three months on the road at a stretch. The result has been remarkable. Under Liu's care, his wife has avoided muscle and joint atrophy, maintained good coordination, and can still communicate largely as before. Liu says life on the road has made her ["100 times" more spirited](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJys0LFuwyAUheGnwZsjfA3YDAxdvKVrR3RjLjEVhgioI7995T5D5yN90vm_7vaOIYb0_MSdjH9623y2id41UmtU7B4i1ewdHbmFnDBicjEXVy1wUD3XPRcW1xYOsgI7ZzwR0NiRGaZ5lhJgHrvN6EF7cOMqpZdaa-lwVTQAKpz1TA_ZBXN5XHMBnAsBN-9H9RCrmwY1aD4pJji50HK5feeQ2kY-nvmgclvz3kWztfaqbPxgsDBYKp71Ghgs-8lguQ4xWLaf-sDk-hcWjGcl17-Dp74VPCh2xbjXO8QYqpqY4M8dQ_zT2z-EOQz8BgAA__-pEXrO) than she was during her years in and out of hospitals. The couple recently completed their tour of China and are already planning to hit the road again.

A whistleblower just confirmed that the USPS has been secretly building software to gut mail-in voting, in direct defiance of a court order blocking Trump's plan.
According to the whistleblower, a project like this normally takes nine months to a year. But this software was built in just a matter of weeks.
The system checks ballot barcodes against information uploaded by state election officials. If even just one bad barcode is detected, the entire batch gets rejected--upwards of ten thousand ballots getting rejected at once for each error.

Democrats have built our entire turnout operation around early and mail-in voting. We identify our voters, we knock on their doors, we call them, we get them to bank their ballot early. Once they vote, we move on to the next name on the list. It's incredibly effective at boosting turnout.
Republicans do the opposite. They wait until Election Day. That is why 2020 produced the "red mirage," Trump's early lead built on in-person votes, before Democrats surged ahead once mail-in ballots got counted.
Trump wants to break our best organizing tool and force Democrats to vote in person on Election Day, all while threatening to deploy ICE and the National Guard at polling locations and flooding the polls with over a thousand DOJ "election monitors" to intimidate voters and suppress turnout.
There is no doubt what Trump is trying to implement is unconstitutional. But with MAGA extremists controlling the Supreme Court, that may not matter. We just watched them gut the Voting Rights Act. We cannot rely on them saving us here.

# **[Bessent's boom is real and the press is still asleep](https://substack.com/redirect/276f3ef8-490c-468c-9140-c2565986f657?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Kudlow just replayed the G20 tape with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, and the wires still won't run it. Bessent said the president's policies laid the groundwork: regulatory certainty, almost 14 million barrels of oil a day, record natural-gas and LNG exports, and permanent 100% bonus depreciation that can write off a bunch of costs in year one. Non-financial productivity is running 3.1% a year for two years "nothing like it since the 1990s."
* **Winners?** Energy exporters sitting on almost 14 million barrels a day, data-center builders expensing the building on day one, and builders actually pouring the concrete.
* **Losers?** Every editor still selling recession fan fiction while ISM manufacturing prints eight straight up months and services run fifteen. The doomsday desk just got lapped.
* **Next?** Watch whether 3.1% productivity and roughly $300 billion in refunds show up in GDP. Bonus depreciation does not stay a secret once the capex hits.

This is the cycle the press refuses to count. Tax-free tips, tax-free overtime, data centers that generate their own power and water and then cut the local property bill. You don't have to like Bessent. You do have to read a productivity print we haven't seen since the 1990s. The boom is running. The coverage isn't.

# **[Waller's pause lasted one day, then jobs murdered $80,000 Bitcoin](https://substack.com/redirect/276f3ef8-490c-468c-9140-c2565986f657?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Bitcoin tagged $82,000 Friday morning, about $700 shy of the $83,000 ceiling that's capped it since February, then August payrolls sent it back under $80,000. Employers added 162,000 jobs, nearly triple the estimate, June and July got revised up 55,000, and unemployment sat at 4.1%. Waller gave the debasement crowd one night. The dollar and yields took it back by lunch.
* **Winners?** Anyone short Thursday's melt-up. Two-year yields, the dollar, and Fed hawks just got a 162,000-job permission slip heading into September 16's Fed Announcement.
* **Losers?** The August 19 Bessent-buyback trade: Bitcoin, Gold, Strategy's 18% rip, Robinhood's 16% rip, Coinbase's 10% pop, and the longs who bought Waller's Lennon line.
* **Next?** September 11 CPI decides if "give disinflation a chance" still has a pulse. Until then $80,000 is a ceiling, not a floor.

Thursday wasn't a Bitcoin renaissance. It was a one-day dollar dump after Waller cut hike odds from 63% to 52% and juiced SpaceX 6.2% and Tesla 5.4% for nearly $200 billion of combined cap. Friday's 162,000 print put the hike back on the table and tagged Bitcoin as low as $79,197. Debasement trades die when labor refuses to cooperate.

---
| | | What's happening right now across this country should alarm every single one of us.

Antisemitic attacks are surging. Islamophobia is spreading unchecked. LGBTQ+ Americans are facing threats and violence simply for existing openly. And South Asian Americans are experiencing hate, harassment, and violence at a level that demands more than words.

No American should feel they don't belong in this country because of where they were born, how they worship, who they love, or what their name sounds like.

I've lived that truth my whole life. And this week, I decided to act on at least one piece of it.

I brought together every South Asian member of Congress, along with state and local elected officials from seven states and leading advocacy organizations, for a national roundtable in Washington focused on the surge in hate targeting our community:

---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138595936/644548470/1090555623?refcode=260904_roundtable&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDUvMS83MzE2OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkOGMxMjZmMi05ZGE4LWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTkzM2IiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=FAN9O6Xuy6KMhREYZK0UOatSEM9wLJQj1T91ghajs2Q=)
---
We discussed what our communities are actually experiencing right now, what's driving this surge in hate, and — most importantly — what we can actually do to stop it.

Here's the truth: Hate crimes across many different communities are dramatically underreported, and the federal government doesn't have a clear picture of what's really going on or why.

That's exactly why I reintroduced the Hate Crimes Commission Act earlier this year. This legislation would create a bipartisan commission to investigate what's actually driving this rise in hate — including the role social media and technology play in spreading it — so we can build real strategies to stop it, for every community being targeted.

**I've faced this hatred personally. I've had a sitting elected official call for the mass deportation of Indians and label me a "foreign occupier." I've watched a demonstrator tear an Indian flag apart while a crowd chanted hate. I know exactly what this feels like, and I refuse to let any community face it alone.**

This is exactly why I founded Equal Opportunity Now — to support leaders who will stand up and fight for every community being told they don't belong, instead of staying silent while hate goes unanswered.

[**Will you chip in $25 or $50 to Equal Opportunity Now today to help us keep fighting for a country where no one has to hide who they are?**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138595940/644548475/1090555623?refcode=260904_roundtable&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDUvMS83MzE2OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkOGMxMjZmMi05ZGE4LWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTkzM2IiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=FAN9O6Xuy6KMhREYZK0UOatSEM9wLJQj1T91ghajs2Q=)

clean_body: | | | | = | | | What's happening right now across this country should alarm every single one of us. Antisemitic attacks are surging. Islamophobia is spreading unchecked. LGBTQ+ Americans are facing threats and violence simply for existing openly. And South Asian Americans are experiencing hate, harassment, and violence at a level that demands more than words. No American should feel they don't belong in this country because of where they were born, how they worship, who they love, or what their name sounds like. I've lived that truth my whole life. And this week, I decided to act on at least one piece of it. I brought together every South Asian member of Congress, along with state and local elected officials from seven states and leading advocacy organizations, for a national roundtable in Washington focused on the surge in hate targeting our community: = We discussed what our communities are actually experiencing right now, what's driving this surge in hate, and — most importantly — what we can actually do to stop it. Here's the truth: Hate crimes across many different communities are dramatically underreported, and the federal government doesn't have a clear picture of what's really going on or why. That's exactly why I reintroduced the Hate Crimes Commission Act earlier this year. This legislation would create a bipartisan commission to investigate what's actually driving this rise in hate — including the role social media and technology play in spreading it — so we can build real strategies to stop it, for every community being targeted. I've faced this hatred personally. I've had a sitting elected official call for the mass deportation of Indians and label me a "foreign occupier." I've watched a demonstrator tear an Indian flag apart while a crowd chanted hate. I know exactly what this feels like, and I refuse to let any community face it alone. This is exactly why I founded Equal Opportunity Now — to support leaders who will stand up and fight for every community being told they don't belong, instead of staying silent while hate goes unanswered. = = = | | | No American should feel like a stranger in their own home. **Pappas Under Fire for Accepting China-Linked Cash**
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | **FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE** September 4th, 2026
---
| | | **CONTACT** karina@nhrsc.com

---
| |

**CONCORD, N.H. —** Today, the New York Post published an article entitled, “Beijing-linked businessman accused of undermining US gave thousands to Senate Dem contenders, records reveal,” identifying Chris Pappas as one of the recipients of campaign contributions from Pin Ni.In response, New Hampshire Republican State Committee Chairman Scott Maltzie and New Hampshire Republican National Committeeman William O’Brien released the following statements:“This raises serious questions that Chris Pappas needs to answer. The New York Post reports that Pin Ni has been identified in documents as a member of the Chinese Communist Party and has contributed thousands of dollars to Pappas’ campaign. Granite Staters deserve to know why Pappas accepted these contributions and whether he will return the money,” **said NHGOP Chairman Scott Maltzie.** “This has crossed a line where no American patriot should go. For that reason, he should resign immediately from Congress and suspend his campaign,” **said National Committeeman William O’Brien.**
Here is an excerpt from the article:
**Beijing-linked businessman accused of undermining US gave thousands to Senate Dem contenders, records reveal** Ryan King[New York Post](https://us.list-manage.com/1Yzk8cRauCl?e=f3aa6419cd&c2id=cbe815d8d4829b0196839495b093775b&m=H1AVSdrxr4tCu2Mf-3Ce7tPI1oqS1HQaW75PpwFah5TpSn33jCDW5f6WIg==)September 4, 2026 _A manufacturing magnate suspected of helping the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) wage economic war on the US has donated thousands of dollars to Democratic Senate candidates, campaign finance records reveal.__**Pin Ni, the president of Illinois-based Wanxiang America Corporation, gave $7,000 to the campaigns of Rep. Chris Pappas (D-NH), Minnesota Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan, Sen. John Hickenlooper (D-Colo.) and former North Carolina Gov. Roy Cooper.**__While federal law limits individual donations to $3,500 per campaign, Pin gave to each of the four Democrats’ primary and general election runs for a total of $28,000 in contributions.__...__The most recent donation from Pin, made Aug. 10, went to Pappas..._

subject: 43 wins for Maryland. Why I still voted NO.
disclaimer_text:

body:
https://elfrethformaryland.com/ [https://elfrethformaryland.com/]

Friend,

Serving on the House Armed Services Committee is one of the greatest honors of my life. Representing the U.S. Naval Academy and thousands of military families in MD-03, I take our national security personally.

I spent months in committee fighting for our service members and delivering for Maryland, and we scored huge wins in this year’s defense bill: 43 of our individual priorities passed , including $86 million to protect the Naval Academy from severe flooding.

So why did I vote NO when the defense bill hit the House floor?

Because doing this job means knowing the difference between supporting our troops and handing Washington a trillion-dollar blank check with zero accountability.

I couldn't in good conscience authorize $1.15 trillion while, at the same time, this Administration drives an unchecked conflict in Iran with no end in sight, no clear strategy, and zero answers for American families struggling with rising costs. To make matters worse, House leadership turned a bill that has passed with bipartisan support for 60 years into a playground for partisan culture wars.

I will always fight for our service members, fund world-class veteran care, and secure real investments for Maryland. But I will never rubber-stamp reckless spending or policies that put our troops in harm's way.

Where do you stand on national security accountability? Hit reply and let me know—I read our inbox directly.

Onward,

Sarah Elfreth

After 88 years on this Earth, I have learned a couple of things about war: **All wars are climate disasters.** Every war is driven by untold amounts of fossil fuels and comes at an unimaginable cost to all of us. But not all of us are bearing that cost. Between April and June of this year, five Big Oil giants made **_$48 billion_** in profit as Trump’s war in Iran continued. The path to a more livable world requires us to break the feedback loop between war and climate disaster – because **war is incompatible with a healthy planet for all.** I truly believe the vast majority of people in this country have learned the lessons of the Vietnam War, the Iraq War, and so many other unnecessary and illegal wars, and have come to understand who truly profits in the name of war-mongering. It is the fossil fuel industry and its oily CEOs making billions from war. The same powerful interests who’ve spent decades buying influence in our political system and blocking climate action. I’ve seen this cycle play out for far too long to stop fighting now. **And one of the most powerful things we can do is elect climate leaders who are brave enough to meet this moment with the urgency it demands.** That’s why I founded the Jane Fonda Climate PAC. The status quo simply isn’t cutting it. We need leaders willing to fight for bold solutions. Leaders who refuse fossil fuel money. clean_body: | After 88 years on this Earth, I have learned a couple of things about war: All wars are climate disasters. Every war is driven by untold amounts of fossil fuels and comes at an unimaginable cost to all of us. But not all of us are bearing that cost. Between April and June of this year, five Big Oil giants made $48 billion in profit as Trump’s war in Iran continued. The path to a more livable world requires us to break the feedback loop between war and climate disaster – because war is incompatible with a healthy planet for all. I truly believe the vast majority of people in this country have learned the lessons of the Vietnam War, the Iraq War, and so many other unnecessary and illegal wars, and have come to understand who truly profits in the name of war-mongering. It is the fossil fuel industry and its oily CEOs making billions from war. The same powerful interests who’ve spent decades buying influence in our political system and blocking climate action. I’ve seen this cycle play out for far too long to stop fighting now. And one of the most powerful things we can do is elect climate leaders who are brave enough to meet this moment with the urgency it demands. That’s why I founded the Jane Fonda Climate PAC. The status quo simply isn’t cutting it. We need leaders willing to fight for bold solutions. Leaders who refuse fossil fuel money. Leaders who will put people, peace, and a livable future ahead of corporate profits. = | = When I leave this place, I want my grandkids to know that I did everything in my power to create a livable, cleaner future for them. # Before you vote, hear it from me — not from anyone else.
Friends, Before you vote, I am asking you to take a little time this weekend and hear directly from me. For almost **40 years** , I have served Rhode Island families as an oral and maxillofacial surgeon. I built my practice here. I raised my children here in East Greenwich with my wife, Carol. I have treated our most vulnerable patients in our hospitals, our correctional facilities, and our children’s programs. That is not a talking point. That is a life’s work. I am a **Republican**. I am the candidate endorsed by the Rhode Island Republican Party. And I have never needed a costume or a slogan to prove who I am. Leadership is showing up when it costs you something. Integrity is telling people the truth and standing by it after the cameras are off. I am running because I love this state and I love the people in it. I have been here in our best times and in our worst times. I have testified in Washington, D.C., on healthcare. I have stood at the Rhode Island State House to defend the Second Amendment. I challenged the government when it imposed unconstitutional mandates and tried to shut down my practice. And when Rhode Island faced one of the darkest nights in our history — The Station nightclub fire — I was called in to help the State Medical Examiner’s office identify the lost and serve families living through the worst hours of their lives. That is what love of Rhode Island looks like. Not a speech. Showing up. I have been here for our families when it was quiet and when it was unbearable. Now I want to represent all of us in Congress. This race is about **your grocery bill, your electric bill, your healthcare, your safety, and the future we leave our children and grandchildren**. In this debate, I tell you exactly where I stand and what I will fight for in Congress. I want you to watch. I want you to compare the candidates. Then decide for yourself who has the roots, the record, and the character to represent the Second District. I will not ask you to take my word for it. I will ask you to look me in the eye on that stage and judge the man for yourself.

## I am the Republican best prepared to defeat Seth Magaziner.
This primary is not a sideshow. The winner on September 9 is the only Republican who will stand across from Congressman Seth Magaziner in November. If we nominate the wrong messenger, Magaziner keeps the seat. If we nominate a serious Rhode Islander with roots, standing, and a record, we can take this district back. Magaziner and Washington Democrats have given Rhode Island families higher costs, higher electric bills, weaker borders, and a government that lectures the people who pay the tab. I will not match him with noise. I will beat that record with a lifetime of service in this district and a clear plan to put Rhode Island families first. **Why I am the one to do it:** **I have the roots.** I have lived and practiced in Congressional District 2 for nearly four decades. Magaziner cannot call me a visitor. I have treated our neighbors, paid our taxes, and raised my family here. **I have the standing.** I am a surgeon who has cared for Rhode Island’s most vulnerable patients. I have testified in Washington on healthcare and at the State House in defense of our constitutional rights. That is a harder record for a career Democrat to smear than a candidate who handed Washington an easy attack ad. **I have the party behind me.** I earned the endorsement of the Rhode Island Republican Party because Republicans across this state judged me ready to carry our banner against Magaziner. **I have already stood up to the Democratic machine.** When the state imposed unconstitutional mandates and tried to shut down my practice, I did not fold. I took the fight to court. That is the backbone it takes to confront Magaziner in a statewide media market. **I can win people Magaziner takes for granted.** I represent this entire district — Republicans, independents, and Democrats who are tired of being talked down to. November is won by the candidate who has been here for all of us, in good times and in grief, and can look Rhode Island in the eye and be believed.
---
Please watch. Compare the candidates. Decide for yourself who can beat Seth Magaziner and who will fight for you in Congress. I hope to earn your trust, your support, and your vote on **Wednesday, September 9**. Respectfully, Dr. Stephen “Doc” Skoly Republican for Congress • Rhode Island’s 2nd District

body:
If you ever doubted we could win America’s youth back from the Left...

| | | [](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckc2unDAMhZ8m7BiBE8JkwaLqCKmLe7ddRiYxTFSS0PxQ9e0r7swTdGfZx-fIn39-6A90uwvbJ3qazOl0ynqhNSb6G-vmTqpHDOgpOYNJQwey7VTbCY2muJO0wMZOxkoODU39eL8Pgxi5ap7TsCARGFw5Aki-SEC5ChoFiBGl6Bs3XXad6gR0YuDyhhKspAE4KDVK0zPR1cNioXwzMWRKJ16ZLoR4VTHcTPTNPj1LOTLj3xjMDOZMpia6YSAby6VgMJeaggtbe0QXSlszMphHNazLMFKrSPFWkMVWEfEW1_u6DtSTJGR8zrEmQ9pES4w_vv_47Dm_S8FA1uK1J-uqZ_xBHt3-br5WGH88MVnMvzSa3--RQX-g2wLjj3LUjC-MLvsvtG9RoXRZNmmyxx-37y7LkYluuyK-Ti7_-alzgn8BAAD__8ycpQU)
---
| | Friend,
---
If you ever doubted we could win America's youth back from the Left...

If you ever wondered whether we'd lost the next generation for good...

If you ever sat up at night -- watching the news, seeing what's happening in our schools, our culture, our country -- and thought, _" Is it already too late?" _

You're not alone.

A lot of good people have been asking the same question.

**But I want to tell you something that might just change how you feel about the future of this country... **

Just one year ago, Turning Point USA's high school program -- which is now called "Club America" -- was in about 1,200 schools.

That was no small feat.

Starting a single chapter today takes serious courage. Students get mocked. Threatened. Investigated. Sometimes even physically attacked.

So reaching 1,200 chapters already felt like a miracle.

_Then Charlie called me... _

He said: "Andrew, I love what we're doing with our high school program -- but we've got to move faster."

I told him, "We are."

Charlie replied, "No you're not thinking what I'm thinking... I want to be in 35,000 high schools."

I laughed. I told him, "Charlie, there aren't even 35,000 high schools in America."

"Okay," he said, "How many are there?"

"About 27,000."

Without skipping a beat, Charlie said, "Okay, great. Let's do 27,000!"
I'll be honest -- I froze.

We didn't have the numbers. We didn't have the staff. We didn't have the roadmap yet.

But he wasn't fazed.

He said, "Don't worry. We'll figure it out. We'll do it together."

That was Charlie.

He didn't think small. He didn't move slow. He didn't settle for "maybe someday."

He believed in going now.

And he believed that if the mission was right, the path would reveal itself.

He chased what others only dreamed about... and turned what others thought impossible into reality.

That's why he built Turning Point USA in the first place.

That's why tens of thousands of students were inspired by Charlie to start chapters of their own -- _many in schools where they were explicitly told not to. _

**And that 's why today -- less than a year later -- we're not in 1,200 schools anymore: **
---
[](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckc2unDAMhZ8m7BiBE8JkwaLqCKmLe7ddRiYxTFSS0PxQ9e0r7swTdGfZx-fIn39-6A90uwvbJ3qazOl0ynqhNSb6G-vmTqpHDOgpOYNJQwey7VTbCY2muJO0wMZOxkoODU39eL8Pgxi5ap7TsCARGFw5Aki-SEC5ChoFiBGl6Bs3XXad6gR0YuDyhhKspAE4KDVK0zPR1cNioXwzMWRKJ16ZLoR4VTHcTPTNPj1LOTLj3xjMDOZMpia6YSAby6VgMJeaggtbe0QXSlszMphHNazLMFKrSPFWkMVWEfEW1_u6DtSTJGR8zrEmQ9pES4w_vv_47Dm_S8FA1uK1J-uqZ_xBHt3-br5WGH88MVnMvzSa3--RQX-g2wLjj3LUjC-MLvsvtG9RoXRZNmmyxx-37y7LkYluuyK-Ti7_-alzgn8BAAD__8ycpQU)
---
We're in 3,300.

That's roughly 13% of all high schools in America.

Eight states have officially partnered with Club America to bring our chapters into every school statewide.

✅ Florida
✅ Texas
✅ Tennessee
✅ Oklahoma
✅ Montana
✅ Nebraska
✅ Arkansas
✅ Indiana

And we're just getting started.

Think about that: 13% of America's youth now have a place at school where they can say it's okay to love this country...

That it's okay to be bold. That it's okay to believe in God, in family, and in freedom.

_That 's what Club America is about... _

**Giving the next generation a place where they can find their courage, develop grit, and learn how to lead the fight for their country. **
---
[](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckc2unDAMhZ8m7BiBE8JkwaLqCKmLe7ddRiYxTFSS0PxQ9e0r7swTdGfZx-fIn39-6A90uwvbJ3qazOl0ynqhNSb6G-vmTqpHDOgpOYNJQwey7VTbCY2muJO0wMZOxkoODU39eL8Pgxi5ap7TsCARGFw5Aki-SEC5ChoFiBGl6Bs3XXad6gR0YuDyhhKspAE4KDVK0zPR1cNioXwzMWRKJ16ZLoR4VTHcTPTNPj1LOTLj3xjMDOZMpia6YSAby6VgMJeaggtbe0QXSlszMphHNazLMFKrSPFWkMVWEfEW1_u6DtSTJGR8zrEmQ9pES4w_vv_47Dm_S8FA1uK1J-uqZ_xBHt3-br5WGH88MVnMvzSa3--RQX-g2wLjj3LUjC-MLvsvtG9RoXRZNmmyxx-37y7LkYluuyK-Ti7_-alzgn8BAAD__8ycpQU)
---
_But now, Friend, the question is... _

**What will it take to bring Club America to the next 3,300 schools? What will it take to bring it to all 27,000? **

Because here's the truth:

These students aren't just signing up. _They 're stepping up. _

They're leading chapters in schools where America is attacked... where they're often targeted for daring to say what they believe... and where speaking the truth is dangerous.

But that isn't stopping them.

They're still showing up. They're speaking out. And they're growing stronger than ever.

They're becoming exactly the kind of young patriots Charlie believed in -- not just bold, _but brave_. Not just loud, but _principled_.

**Every time a student starts a new chapter, we make sure they 're not standing alone. **

**We send them an activism kit -- American flags, pocket Constitutions, chapter materials, and leadership tools. **

These kits give student leaders everything they need to rally their peers and stand strong on their campuses.

Each one costs just $25 to pack and ship.

And so the next generation wouldn't be handed over to the Left by default.

Let's make Charlie's dream real -- 27,000 high schools. And a generation that doesn't apologize for loving this country.

It's up to us to finish what he started.

One chapter. One student. One school at a time.

Let's move faster. Let's push further. Let's get this done -- for Charlie, and for the country we all love.

Peter – we know, we know.
We send you a lot of emails, and we truly wish we didn’t have to.
What you might not realize is that a major part of our campaign’s fundraising comes from folks like you chipping in to emails just like this.
Roy understands that it’s not possible for you to donate to every email we send – and he doesn’t expect you to! [**_But we’re hoping you’ll pitch in to this one. Here’s why:_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1345&amount=5&t=8&akid=3196%2E124072%2Ekjg1cl)
This November’s U.S. Senate race in North Carolina will be one of the most competitive, most expensive and most consequential in the country. Experts say there’s no path back to the Senate majority without flipping this battleground seat, so the stakes could not be higher.
That means national Republicans have singled Roy out as their top target for defeat. Dark-money groups are spending nearly $100 million so far to halt our momentum and smear Roy’s character with baseless attack ads.
**With a recent poll showing Roy statistically tied with MAGA Republican Michael Whatley, their attacks are clearly working.**

Already a paid subscriber? Then like, share, and keep showing up in the comments. It matters more than you know.
* * *
The miraculous news arrived this morning: the latest jobs report came much stronger than what anyone expected. A gift from heaven for the Trump administration, right on schedule.

I laughed. I'll be honest with you -- I scoffed and chuckled a little when I saw it, because I don't believe a single number that comes out of this administration. Not one.

Yesterday's ADP report told a completely different story. Almost no job growth. Manufacturing jobs lost. Wage growth so slow against inflation that it functions as a pay cut. That report got a shrug. Today's number got the full treatment. All day long the MAGA media machine has been running its victory lap -- the Golden Age of America is here.

But you and I know exactly who the Golden Age is for. A handful of corrupt people inside Donald Trump's White House and inside his family. That is the entire list. There is no Golden Age for you and me.

They're lying about these numbers. Let's be clear about it. They fired the head of the Bureau of Labor Statistics last year. We are two months out from an election. You don't need to be a genius to see the plan: convince people the economy is better when it fundamentally isn't, and hold that lie together just long enough to get through November.

And this is hardly the first time. I could spend the rest of this newsletter cataloguing the dumpster fire of things these people lie about. But forget the small stuff. A few weeks ago they were caught lying about the number of American servicemen and women killed and wounded in the illegal war in Iran Donald Trump launched. They lied about the dead. If you will lie about that, you will absolutely lie about a jobs number. There is no bottom with these people, and anyone taking today's report seriously deserves to be laughed at.

Now let's say I'm wrong. Let's say the numbers are real. So what?

Inflation in this country is brutal. Trump's war in Iran. Historically high gas and diesel prices. Tariffs that are both incompetently implemented and a pure exercise in the vanity of one man, making everything you touch more expensive. What exactly is a great jobs report worth when you need two or three of those jobs to cover your grocery bill? A job is not a life. A job used to be a floor you could build something on. Now it's just a thing you collect several of and still come up short.

So when I hear the MAGA media machine tell me the Golden Age is here, that Republicans have been saved in the midterms, that we have finally hit the miraculous moment where the economy takes off -- I know what I'm listening to. It's fucking cope. That's all it is. Cope, and more cope, and more cope on top of that.
* * *
