* * *
Meanwhile the average person is sitting at home right now, struggling, quietly giving up on the American dream. Convinced they will never own a home. Never pay off the student loans. Never retire with dignity. Never start the family they wanted. Never start the business from the idea they have been carrying around for years, the one they still believe in when nobody's looking. Never marry the person they've been putting it off with because the timing was never right and now it never will be. People are delaying their entire lives because of this economy. That is the story that matters, and nobody at the BLS is telling it.

And what is Donald Trump doing? Giving tours of his big beautiful ballroom. Building an arch with his name on it. Talking openly about how he has to build his legacy right now, while he's still here, because he knows perfectly well that nobody is going to do it for him after he's gone.

He's right about that part. Maybe somebody would want to build a monument to this man if he had ever done one single thing worth remembering. What has he actually done? He dragged this nation to the bottom. He destroyed the global economy. He embarrassed and humiliated our military. He got eighteen American servicemen and women killed. He put people in harm's way for nothing. He terrorized immigrant communities. That's the record. That's the whole marble slab.

Nobody is going to remember anything good about Donald Trump's life. The minute he's gone, the rest of the country will say out loud what it already knows -- that he was a failed, lame duck president -- and all of it will catch up to him. We are very close to that moment now. Very close to the day when suddenly everybody was against all of it the whole time.

That includes the Republican congressional candidates who are right now begging Donald Trump to stay the hell out of their districts while simultaneously begging him to spend a piece of that $400 million dollar war chest to save them in November. They want the money. They just don't want the man anywhere near a camera in their state. It's not going to work.

So do not let them gaslight you. Do not let them gaslight anybody you love into believing this economy is strong. The daily indignity that the vast majority of Americans are living through -- at the gas pump, at the grocery store, when they crack open a laptop and look at a house they will never be able to buy -- that is the real economy. That's the one you live in. It's destroying people's belief that tomorrow can be better than today, and that is a much harder thing to rebuild than a factory.

They can print any number they want. They can put it on every screen in America and have every anchor read it in the same reverent voice. It doesn't change what's in your account at the end of the month. And it doesn't change what you already know.
With urgency,
--Mike

What DSA wants to do to the Senate, the presidency and the courts

[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

PRESENTED BY ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

Hi friends!

Here's a summary of today's top stories:

🏔️ HERE IN COLORADO... The Colorado Supreme Court rejected Xcel's
bid to fast-track a Cheyenne County eminent domain dispute
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
voters will decide a dozen-plus measures in November
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
including a Democratic plan to replace the flat income tax with a
graduated system versus a conservative cap; a 4.25-million-gallon
Pueblo sewage spill continues fouling the Arkansas River during
harvest
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
and Patti Fox testified to Congress
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
that an illegal immigrant driver left her daughter permanently
disabled, condemning sanctuary policies and school anti-ICE walkouts.

🇺🇸 ON THE NATIONAL STAGE... Rep. Lauren Boebert warned against
unregulated license-plate surveillance
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
tracking Americans without warrants; DSA's new platform calls to
abolish the Senate and Electoral College
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
a stance even Sanders and Warren reject; and a Utah judge ruled Tyler
Robinson will stand trial on all seven charges
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
including death-penalty-eligible murder, in Charlie Kirk's
assassination.

🗣️ COMMENTARY SPOTLIGHT... Alejandro Bermúdez frames Colorado's
ballot fights over trans athletes and minors' surgeries as a national
test case, noting 73% of Americans oppose trans athletes competing
outside their birth sex
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
Kelly Sloan warns Mamdani's socialism makes private property
"perpetually insecure"
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
and shouldn't be dismissed as fringe.

This is your Mountain Minute for Friday, September 4, 2026.

– Team RMV

TODAY'S TOP STORIES

WHAT DSA WANTS TO DO TO THE SENATE, THE PRESIDENCY AND THE COURTS
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY SHAINA COLE, ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

Cliff Connolly wanted his fellow socialists to understand why the
fight was worth having.

“The whole point of having the Senate, the president, and the
Supreme Court is so that, if popular legislation passes through the
House of Representatives, the ruling class has these other levels they
can pull to stop it from happening,” he said, according to City
Journal, which reported from inside the meeting. He pointed to the
Supreme Court striking down President Biden’s student debt plan as
his example.

Connolly sits on the Democratic Socialists of America’s National
Political Committee, the group’s highest governing body between
conventions. He was arguing for language DSA has now adopted as
official policy: a plan to take apart the basic structure of the
federal government and build a different one.

READ MORE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

SIX ONLINE SCHOOLS, A $15 MILLION BALANCE, ONE DISTRICT: WHAT D49 TOOK
ON WHEN IT DISSOLVED ERBOCES
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY SHAINA COLE, ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

_A district serving fewer than 500 local co-op students is now on the
hook for six online schools and a contested $15 million balance._

*
A MESSY DISSOLUTION: D49 voted to dissolve ERBOCES on Aug. 17 even
after Pikes Peak State College reversed its planned withdrawal, and
the state now questions whether the college was ever a validly
recognized member in the first place.

*
A BIG ADMINISTRATIVE PICKUP: D49 becomes the governing body and
authorizer for six multi-district online schools that served 4,707
students last year, plus their special education obligations, even
though fewer than 500 ERBOCES students actually live in the district.

*
AN UNRESOLVED $15 MILLION FIGHT: Education Commissioner Susana
Córdova has challenged whether ERBOCES's reserves should flow
entirely to D49 as a "windfall" or return to the State Education Fund,
alongside separate demands over a disputed $3 million loan and nearly
$800,000 in payments to a private school.

BIG GOVERNMENT OR INDIVIDUAL FREEDOM: THERE IS NO THIRD CHOICE.
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY JAY DAVIDSON | COMMENTARY | SEPTEMBER 4

_Both good and evil ideas start with a vision. That vision promises to
solve a problem we have. Politicians fit the same mold. How to
differentiate, how do we tell if a vision is good or evil?_

BERMÚDEZ: COLORADO VOTERS BECOME A TEST CASE FOR DEMOCRATS’
TRANSGENDER LONG GAME
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
BY ALEJANDRO BERMUDEZ | COMMENTARY | SEPTEMBER 3

_As national LGBT activists prepare a decade-long campaign to reshape

body:

In exactly **14 days** , absentee ballots officially hit mailboxes across Minnesota's Second Congressional District.My roots run deep in this community. My mother taught school in Shakopee for over 25 years, and my father worked in real estate. Growing up here taught me early on that government decisions directly impact working families.In the Minnesota Senate, I worked to balance budgets, improve roads, expand childcare access, and support local small businesses. As we prepare for the general election, I am taking that same practical approach to Washington through the **Pratt Playbook** :
* **Restore Economic Stability:** Using 30 years of finance and banking experience to lower costs, curb reckless spending, and support small businesses.
* **Protect Communities & Borders:** Supporting law enforcement, first responders, and policies that keep neighborhoods safe and secure our borders.
* **Keep Bad Actors Out of Our Wallets:** Cracking down on fraud, waste, and financial scams to protect taxpayer dollars.
* **Make Government Work for People:** Asking one simple question in D.C.— _"What is best for Minnesota families?"_

Friend,

As a grandfather, I find it deeply concerning to think that paper transgender dolls could be used to indoctrinate children in public elementary schools.

**I am calling for an immediate investigation into this “MyGender Dolls” project.**

This is not about tolerance or kindness. This is about whether young children in public schools are being exposed to radical gender ideology through curriculum materials that many parents find inappropriate and confusing.

For years, activists have pushed to introduce complex adult concepts about gender identity into classrooms at younger and younger ages. **Many parents have been shut out of the conversation and called bigots simply for wanting to protect their children’s innocence and decide these matters themselves at home.**

| | _With just four days until the primary, I am using each day to discuss an issue I have highlighted on the campaign trail. For Day 4, I am highlighting the need to reduce global nuclear dangers through domestic policy and diplomacy._
* * *
Dear David, For several years, I lived in the Marshall Islands, where the U.S. dropped 67 nuclear bombs in the 1940s and 1950s and told families it was “for the good of mankind.” Today, Marshallese in the Pacific and in the United States, as well as the American service members who helped carry out and clean up after the tests, carry the scars of wounds that have never fully healed. **[We owe it to the Marshallese, to our citizens, and to future generations to make sure that we have proper guardrails in place to ensure that we don’t repeat one of our country’s worst mistakes. I am the only candidate in this race with a stated position AGAINST nuclear testing and FOR nuclear disarmament. Will you pitch in to help me bring this essential work to Congress?](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/4c6vl4QAwB7WcSZZlE2hWA~~/AAUS1hA~/-UieCzTxTd2j4m5_2qDmuMwYNxTqhZ_UwdEpIsLr5X34twKPqHGEF32ZQuPORO2VF7MxBNyGqDVSgNCt6s68Zufxj3ZoZqPxiu4p3ZEiU8HbwpWlCLW-p8kHE5_EcZy7WiLPaTzcVO_-rdHgU8meAQ~~)** | | [DONATE](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/4c6vl4QAwB7WcSZZlE2hWA~~/AAUS1hA~/-UieCzTxTd2j4m5_2qDmuMwYNxTqhZ_UwdEpIsLr5X34twKPqHGEF32ZQuPORO2VF7MxBNyGqDVSgNCt6s68Zufxj3ZoZqPxiu4p3ZEiU8HbwpWlCLW-p8kHE5_EcZy7WiLPaTzcVO_-rdHgU8meAQ~~)

Right now, one person has the power to launch a nuclear weapon without Congressional approval: Donald Trump.
That’s dangerous and undemocratic. **No single leader should hold that kind of power, especially when that President is Trump, who’s shown a willingness to, at the very least, threaten the use of nuclear weapons.**
One of the Trump Administration’s first actions in January of this year was to suspend the review boards responsible for evaluating the medical claims of over 700,000 former US government employees who worked during the Cold War in US nuclear facilities.
He’s also repeatedly floated a return to explosive nuclear testing. He made a sweetheart deal with OpenAI to allow the use of artificial intelligence in our weapons systems.
And the New START Treaty, the last remaining agreement limiting U.S. and Russian nuclear arsenals, officially expired earlier this year.
We currently have a system where the Commander in Chief has sole control over the US nuclear arsenal. That’s why I’ll fight to pass the Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty, move laws forward that require Congress to authorize the use of nuclear weapons, and restore the checks and balances that our Founders intended.

clean_body: An issue a day | | | | With just four days until the primary, I am using each day to discuss an issue I have highlighted on the campaign trail. For Day 4, I am highlighting the need to reduce global nuclear dangers through domestic policy and diplomacy. Dear David, For several years, I lived in the Marshall Islands, where the U.S. dropped 67 nuclear bombs in the 1940s and 1950s and told families it was “for the good of mankind.” Today, Marshallese in the Pacific and in the United States, as well as the American service members who helped carry out and clean up after the tests, carry the scars of wounds that have never fully healed. ~~ | | ~~ Right now, one person has the power to launch a nuclear weapon without Congressional approval: Donald Trump. That’s dangerous and undemocratic. No single leader should hold that kind of power, especially when that President is Trump, who’s shown a willingness to, at the very least, threaten the use of nuclear weapons. One of the Trump Administration’s first actions in January of this year was to suspend the review boards responsible for evaluating the medical claims of over 700,000 former US government employees who worked during the Cold War in US nuclear facilities. He’s also repeatedly floated a return to explosive nuclear testing. He made a sweetheart deal with OpenAI to allow the use of artificial intelligence in our weapons systems. And the New START Treaty, the last remaining agreement limiting U.S. and Russian nuclear arsenals, officially expired earlier this year. We currently have a system where the Commander in Chief has sole control over the US nuclear arsenal. That’s why I’ll fight to pass the Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty, move laws forward that require Congress to authorize the use of nuclear weapons, and restore the checks and balances that our Founders intended. ~~ If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | | | ~~ Kommol tata to all of our cherished friends, mentors, and students in the RMI who shared these stories with me. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
I was asked about my future this weekend. I told them I'm focused on yours.

| | | | Hey Peter, I was just on Meet the Press.... Kristen Welker asked me about 2028. About whether I'm going to run for president again. But here's the truth I told her on national television this weekend, and the truth I want to tell you directly right now: **This is not the season right now.** In the last decade, there has not been another Republican who has campaigned for more Senate candidates, more House candidates, more gubernatorial candidates than I have. I have been on the road. I have been in the arena. I have shown up in states where it was hard and uncomfortable and politically complicated, because that's what this fight demands. __I am doing it again right now_._ I need you to understand what we're actually fighting because this isn't just about seats and majorities and who controls which chamber. This is about something far bigger. **_The Democrat Party I came up watching is gone_.** What replaced it is something my father would have recognized immediately, because he lived it. He was tortured in a Cuban prison. He watched his country get strangled by a communist regime that promised the people everything, free healthcare, free education, power to the people, and delivered misery, silence, and chains. **That ideology, socialism, Marxism, the DSA agenda, is winning Democratic primaries across this country right now.** They elected a Democratic Socialist as mayor of New York City. Their endorsed candidates swept primaries in Michigan and Florida. And now that same machine is flooding money into Senate races that were never supposed to be competitive. **Texas. Iowa. Alaska. Michigan. Georgia.** James Talarico alone has $21.5 million in the bank to try to flip the Texas Senate seat. Democrats are outraising Republicans in nearly every battleground state. The Cook Political Report recently called both Texas and Iowa toss-ups. **_The map is shifting, and money is the reason_.** Chuck Schumer only needs a few of these seats to take back the majority. And the moment he does and the tax cuts get reversed, the border gets opened, conservative judges get blocked, and everything we have fought for gets dismantled piece by piece by people who openly admire the ideology that destroyed my father's country. _I will not let that happen._ I told Kristen Welker this weekend that this is the season of the midterms. I meant it. I am going to spend every day between now and November 3rd on the road, on the trail, fighting for every conservative candidate who needs someone to show up for them. **But I need to know you're fighting with me.** Not in October when it's almost too late. Right now, while there's still time to close the fundraising gap, get ads on the air, and build the ground game that shows up on Election Day. **Will you chip in today? | | We are still in Oregon's wildfire season. And already, it's the worst on record, with over 2.5 million acres burned. It didn't have to be this way.**This was a policy choice.** **[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138597945/644555298/-2044921950?refcode=2026-09-04-wf&recurring=0&amount=&amounts=10,30,50,100,200&refcode2=a68afcbe-a5a8-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDEvMS84OTQxMiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhNjhhZmNiZS1hNWE4LWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTkzM2IiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=lFBGG2GxnDXvxrFdpIlnuxoqDGk10RHeRgYUhWYgtQM=)** In 2025, the Trump administration took a sledgehammer to wildfire preparedness:
* It defunded federal programs that help states like Oregon marshal resources on the ground to limit fire damage
* Teaming up with Elon Musk and DOGE, the administration fired 1,400 qualified federal firefighting personnel — **jobs that haven't been replaced**
* They reorganized the Forest Service, replacing high-ranking experts with political lackeys and defunding 57 research stations that studied drought and forest management

**The Trump administration both made it harder to prepare for fires and harder to contain them once they ignite.** This is a betrayal of our forests and wildlife. It endangers people, homes, and livelihoods. It makes the air less breathable. Every step of the way, I've pressed the Trump administration on how these cuts would impact what was sure to be a brutal fire season. And each time, it was clear they didn't have a plan. **Restoring the necessary funding and personnel to the Forest Service is a top priority of mine.** I'll continue to hold this administration accountable for its reckless actions, and I'll keep working closely with state officials to ensure that Oregonians remain safe. name: OnePA Team
subject: Politicians should not get richer from information the public never sees
body:
Public office should not come with the power to move markets and trade stocks for personal profit. | |
---
Peter, **In northeastern Pennsylvania, people got tired of watching elected officials trade stocks while making decisions that can move markets, impact entire industries, and determine whether working families can afford health care, energy, housing, and other basic needs.** So they organized. This summer, residents of Lackawanna and Luzerne Counties collected and submitted more than 40,000 signatures as part of a grassroots campaign to put insider trading restrictions before voters. Pennsylvania Rep. Rob Bresnahan is one of the most prolific stock traders in Congress, making nearly 650 individual stock trades in 2025. **He also sold more than $100,000 in stock in companies that manage Medicaid patients shortly before voting for nearly $1 trillion in cuts to the program.** Our communities should never have to wonder whether an elected official is thinking about the people they represent or the stocks sitting in their portfolio. Public service comes with enormous power. It should never come with a private financial advantage. **The rules should be clear. If an elected official or government employee learns something because of their public position, they should be prohibited from using that information to make an individual stock trade or prediction-market bet. States should also require strong financial transparency and meaningful accountability when those rules are broken.** [**Tell your state legislators to ban insider trading by public officials and put public service ahead of private profit.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm39uU1mwbYMW9amKE-asg_toAraRXdyqRMDpzio_X5zK-euNprZ_AzDZ7GRq1BvlLBy8z1HcGMtCt-FhDTx8p-xnak8g19fjoKBQfBouor1EBMJ94uU8ZVycrVqD0nu5KN7Jchbbf1GXpF68xNbMl-xqvnpLYCwEhdtaq4dcduXfQn-WQBy0rYD-QKQVEStuxRamDzfGU8dVehx1d2B6psc2LIqdCukwcY-NQ05dVcUwr-Q4pMz9cBGeZfq7Q8YHanzcnipl8d5DoSLAOxo4-gdqjoBE22Q1WCf2E5RZwNmhHwv6uI1yV6_MGBbFPBc7R5VSGABV0Ie0YFvii85Pw_G7jitBo1FCFV2szk-JzOakwA1slxHPt9QyoSXa6SHfRBHGKTtSSL_qbY39Lsj6FwwBngQ_wJOYbOhgoAqg98Xu9KCPvzEbJPqNuxXG09t-zBM/4tr/IV9A_9KmSxyV3aCEyPkx1g/h0/h001.gKhVjcfddCuv-JyhU4nosB3svlX94ICMHnqO4fbRe0U) | | [SIGN & SEND](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm39uU1mwbYMW9amKE-asg_toAraRXdyqRMDpzio_X5zK-euNprZ_AzDZ7GRq1BvlLBy8z1HcGMtCt-FhDTx8p-xnak8g19fjoKBQfBouor1EBO-p6NP0C4TCmSB89gHvKLlbzn8OwomjlFt-XxoNvBLJ26wxMH-akHywPLG0w-OdSGIUI7w6BXMdzD9FK3H2AqreurzvAKWM55dzL1zofQG3HyfjevWRrnP5lSDJK3MGJw-ztmLA4cQ8tR_D9zUJhqyniFEj45BNrAcCw_wplV2zeNVryBFbUoGlWPA2t9GCd_8Mppa8_Sb6rg0Rf0yHcseY8mCjLT-kGDkxAc59RUwnO1VJKh1L9C4o2KuSivmXMJuUQqHeFjWSSxXlyYXmMNKBo6t32LvvrVlT1SOEeFoJVVQ6KEHhfkq9OH1Ug-UWh_m5sHSlxGObIG1KzHfz5v0/4tr/IV9A_9KmSxyV3aCEyPkx1g/h1/h001.OZ5Rv2KRriWWz2TQm2LTLAJMxGtVk49Gx_090WF5CfA)
---
This problem reaches far beyond one politician or one corner of Pennsylvania. Elected officials routinely receive information that the public does not have. They sit in briefings, write laws, oversee public contracts, meet with regulators, and make decisions that can send stock prices moving before ordinary people ever know what happened.
**Nationally, 72% support prohibiting members of Congress and their live-in families from trading individual stocks.** In Pennsylvania, that rises to 74%, including 70% of Republicans and 77% of Democrats. This is basic accountability, and state lawmakers should not need another scandal before they act.
The ballot effort in Lackawanna and Luzerne Counties would specifically prohibit officials and employees from trading or betting based on nonpublic information learned through their official service while increasing public reporting on financial activity and ethics complaints.
**This is what building power from the ground up looks like. When powerful people refuse to police themselves, communities do not have to sit around waiting for them.** Neighbors organize, build support, force the issue into public view, and demand a government that works for the people who elected it.
Every state can raise that standard. No family struggling with the cost of health care, groceries, utilities, or rent should have to watch politicians use access that comes with public office to protect or grow their own wealth. **Our communities deserve decisions made for the public good, free from questions about whose portfolio might benefit.**
[**Send a message to your state legislators and demand strong insider-trading protections for public officials now.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm39uU1mwbYMW9amKE-asg_toAraRXdyqRMDpzio_X5zK-euNprZ_AzDZ7GRq1BvlLBy8z1HcGMtCt-FhDTx8p-xnak8g19fjoKBQfBouor1EBN6Cddg6sjkPEIDLo0QpKoyWZeuV4J4r1sVu6IrIsIBZqL7Na5ikGuNmRDApzWyE60SySXlUHoaCtCNJuLjeEe_EB2OotKf35zkI45hUzuZ5BqxM4yXokJHz1ouHL1YMbjtVxPHUHb6u9K4BdK-J4d_7JKIwpW1jBwNg9FPfs9NhQknXyYtIL3B0z1vMisuoBR9dazO5EIc2MMJUn8DLNnR3-z14cfhw1nDQL61A3g8QVo7grqOSLixFkFWhU76FUqV9SyrEs5RNEbFtlkkr8timmLCcc15WTT2RSHnsNFfy-cOE3bFaP57KmIQXOpp5IZA0rpBcZjukePHoSWm2ouk/4tr/IV9A_9KmSxyV3aCEyPkx1g/h2/h001.7RR8Wj0UPkaoyncghuIE5HymhFP8o709caZbLUJUSb0)
Let’s put public service ahead of private profit.
-OnePA

> _" So, the first thing to know is that the immigrant community in Arkansas, in the United States and I don't care whether these are folks that have documents or not. This is a community that is essential to the fabric, the social, cultural, and economic fabric of this country."_
This isn't Shoffner's first pro-open-borders moment caught on camera. Last year, she posted a video to her own Facebook page endorsing a plan that would let mega-farms reliant on illegal immigrant labor help rewrite America's immigration laws, a scheme that would let illegal immigration keep driving down farm wages while letting the employers who hire illegal labor off the hook.
Shoffner even called the idea "radical" herself:
> _" So here's a radical idea. What if we actually asked farmers and other businesses that rely on foreign-born workers what they need? name: Pramila Jayapal
subject: Citizens United has to go

body:
Working people deserve better.
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20260904-6684-footer&t=1&akid=6684%2E420207%2EgYNiil)
**Our democracy is not a commodity to be sold to the highest bidder, Peter.**
But since the passage of _Citizens United_ over 15 years ago, that’s exactly what it's become — and working families have had to bear the weight of it ever since.
We feel it every single day.
💸 At the gas pump.
💸 In the grocery store
💸 Visiting the doctor’s office.
We watch our priorities get buried beneath a sea of dark money — including this year. AIPAC has already spent over $100 million to influence our elections, while Elon Musk plans to spend $100 million.
Each year, the same corporations and billionaires buy more and more influence in our elections rewriting the rules shaping our daily lives.
**This is completely unacceptable. Working people deserve better.**
Since my very first days in Congress, I’ve felt a deep sense of pride while leading the charge to overturn _Citizens United_ and I won’t stop fighting until we get big money out of politics.
We’ve seen some progress. Earlier this year, Hawaii made history becoming the first state in the country to sign a bill into law stripping corporations of the power to spend in their state’s politics entirely. Candidates like Abdul El-Sayed won despite more than $60 million in outside money spent trying to defeat him.
That’s proof our movement is building — and it’s proof that this fight can be won.
**It’s time to reverse this ruling, bring trust and transparency back into our government, and put power back into the hands of working people.**
[**Will you add your name to this petition to demand Congress rein in corporate power and overturn _Citizens United?_**](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/sign/em20260904-citizens-united-petition/?source=em20260904-6684&t=2&akid=6684%2E420207%2EgYNiil)

Thank you,
Pramila Jayapal

body:
Organized labor is one of the greatest achievements our country has ever made.
| | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138598642/644557714/-201694504?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS84NzY1OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjNDJlOWI3ZS1hYWE4LWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTkzM2IiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=XQnUYD65TQA9xsbH9ccDoedmqdug30merGzkqiQ_J5U=&emci=cc390013-6c9b-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&emdi=c42e9b7e-aaa8-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&ceid=9494239)
---

| | I was raised in a union household. As the son of a union power line worker and a mom who managed the books while raising eight kids, I learned early in life the value of a dollar and the importance of hard work — and how unions helped families like mine thrive. **I know firsthand that a good-paying, union job is the key to growing the middle class. So, ahead of the Labor Day Weekend, I wanted to share what unions mean to me and our community.** We are facing a crisis across America, where some of our hardest workers struggle each day to feed their families and afford the basics. I believe that unions are the first and best support system for America's working class. September 4, 2026
Gloria Steinem, one of the most influential women in American history, passed away at the age of 92. She was at the vanguard of the feminist movement in the 1960s and 1970s and her agenda prevailed.
The feminist movement is basically about one word - control. And for a woman to have control over her life, she needs two things - money in the bank and access to abortion. Without either, a woman is subject to vicissitudes of some man, a government hand out and biological dice - unless she chooses to be celibate and lonely.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/da0b8c2d-3dfc-42b1-b3f5-7728c6745170?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---

But a closer look at the feminist movement reveals that Steinem's views benefited two groups, upper middle-class women and high-IQ women, which is why these two groups are her biggest fans.
Steinem's main claim to fame was fighting for abortion access. She even dedicated her book _My Life on the Road_ to the doctor who arranged her illegal abortion in England when she was twenty-two years old. Like Fleetwood Mac's Stevie Nicks who also trumpeted her abortion, Steinem believed that the reason for her success in life was because she was not saddled with taking care of a child.

Upper middle-class women have the same experience. Most upper middle-class men do not wish to marry young but want a guaranteed sexual partner. Thus, they demand potential spouses move in with them for a "trial run" to satisfy this powerful primitive evolutionary drive. Many women waste the best years of their lives hoping some live-in boyfriend will marry them and having the option of aborting a pregnancy that their live-in boyfriend demands enhances their odds of eventual marriage and an upper middle-class lifestyle.

The same is true for the high-IQ women. In the past, becoming a highly paid professional such as a lawyer, medical doctor or finance expert was problematic for smart women, not only because of discrimination in the admission processes, but also because the education and training required for these jobs meant delaying childbearing until thirty and often beyond. Legalized abortion solved this problem.
Furthermore, as women entered the workplace, corporate America realized women were great workers and could make money off their labor. To paraphrase Charlotte Whitton, the first female mayor of Ottawa, Canada: "In order for women to succeed in the workplace, they must work twice as hard as men. Luckily this is not difficult."
But what about the 80% of women who are not upper middle class or gifted with high-IQs? As pointed out by the feminist nemesis Phyllis Schlafly, these women once had superior rights that protected them. They could not be forced to join the military where they could be killed or maimed. They received preference in alimony payments and did not have to make a living in dangerous work such as coal mining or combat.

Schlafly accurately predicted economic serfdom for women. She foresaw that dual incomes would cause housing prices to skyrocket. And she hit the nail on the head. Women now work like dogs to pay for increased housing costs while spending a fortune on childcare and then returning to a home where they are still responsible for most of the household chores.

Furthermore, men no longer take responsibility for their sexual behavior. The idea that legalized abortion liberated women is the biggest scam going. Legalized abortion liberated men. Now an unwanted pregnancy is no longer "their problem," it is "her problem." While the Planned Parenthood crowd predicted that legalized abortion would reduce out-of-wedlock births, the exact opposite occurred - as anyone with a normal libido could have foreseen. Many women now have a choice, have an abortion or live in poverty as a single mother. Given this option, it is amazing that the abortion rate isn't higher.
The irony is that many of the liberal women who are Steinem acolytes are miserable, in spite of being the most pampered demographic in human history and receiving everything they desire. Primary care doctors observed years ago about the travails of satisfying "angry women." The political class eventually caught up with this trend labelling them as AWFULs (Angry White Female Upscale Liberals).
But for the foreseeable future, Steinem's worldview will be public policy. But few people are happy with it. America is no longer a place where one income can support a family thanks to Steinem and her followers. Thus, public opinion polls state that 70% of the population believe America is on the wrong track, no matter what party occupies the White House.

In the past, becoming a highly paid professional such as a lawyer, medical doctor or finance expert was problematic for smart women, not only because of discrimination in the admission processes, but also because the education and training required for these jobs meant delaying childbearing until thirty and often beyond. Legalized abortion solved this problem. Furthermore, as women entered the workplace, corporate America realized women were great workers and could make money off their labor. To paraphrase Charlotte Whitton, the first female mayor of Ottawa, Canada: "In order for women to succeed in the workplace, they must work twice as hard as men. Luckily this is not difficult." But what about the 80% of women who are not upper middle class or gifted with high-IQs? As pointed out by the feminist nemesis Phyllis Schlafly, these women once had superior rights that protected them. They could not be forced to join the military where they could be killed or maimed. They received preference in alimony payments and did not have to make a living in dangerous work such as coal mining or combat. Schlafly accurately predicted economic serfdom for women. She foresaw that dual incomes would cause housing prices to skyrocket. And she hit the nail on the head. Women now work like dogs to pay for increased housing costs while spending a fortune on childcare and then returning to a home where they are still responsible for most of the household chores. Furthermore, men no longer take responsibility for their sexual behavior. The idea that legalized abortion liberated women is the biggest scam going. Legalized abortion liberated men. Now an unwanted pregnancy is no longer "their problem," it is "her problem." While the Planned Parenthood crowd predicted that legalized abortion would reduce out-of-wedlock births, the exact opposite occurred - as anyone with a normal libido could have foreseen. Many women now have a choice, have an abortion or live in poverty as a single mother. Given this option, it is amazing that the abortion rate isn't higher. The irony is that many of the liberal women who are Steinem acolytes are miserable, in spite of being the most pampered demographic in human history and receiving everything they desire. Primary care doctors observed years ago about the travails of satisfying "angry women." The political class eventually caught up with this trend labelling them as AWFULs (Angry White Female Upscale Liberals). But for the foreseeable future, Steinem's worldview will be public policy. But few people are happy with it. America is no longer a place where one income can support a family thanks to Steinem and her followers. Thus, public opinion polls state that 70% of the population believe America is on the wrong track, no matter what party occupies the White House. **I know that we can build a Wisconsin** where parents don’t have to choose between childcare and their mortgage payment.
**I know that we can build a Wisconsin** where women have freedom over their own bodies.
**And I know that we can build a Wisconsin** where our children can grow up, workers are protected, and seniors can retire without worry.
**This isn’t a pipe dream, Derek; it can be our reality. But if Tiffany and Varnam win, this vision for a better Wisconsin will be flushed down the drain.**

name: David Hogg
subject: The margins are razor thin
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY LEADERS WE DESERVE, LEADERSWEDESERVE
body:
Just 34 votes stand between Daniel Lander and victory.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260904-3&t=1&akid=3973%2E587540%2Ega4oWb)
**34 votes, Peter.**
That’s all that stands in between Daniel Lander and unseating 20-year incumbent and President pro tempore of the Massachusetts Senate William Brownsberger — an official recount is underway.
This is exactly the kind of fight Leaders We Deserve was built to win. When young, forward-thinking progressives step up to challenge the status quo, they don’t just make noise, they shake up the entire system. Asleep-at-the-wheel incumbents everywhere should be scared.
**Because here’s the truth: Daniel is taking on a system built to protect entrenched incumbents.** A State Senator who has spent his career taking money from real estate industry donors and commercial developers. That’s exactly why Brownsberger helped kill a plan to shield working families from rising property taxes, opposed rent control, and stomped out affordable housing bills. He answers to them — not the people of his district.
Daniel is different. He’s spent his entire career fighting for justice and housing affordability — and voters saw that.
That’s why in a race nobody thought would be this close, Daniel is neck and neck with Brownsberger. The margins have swung back and forth all week, from 61 to now just **34 votes**.
That’s the power of our movement.
We’re in this fight together, and we’re so proud to stand with Daniel. We need you with us too to make sure every vote is counted.

Peter, It's Becca. **I want to tell you about something that happened because I honestly think it says a lot about where we are right now.** The White House launched a new online “arcade” with retro-style video games built around this administration’s agenda. One game, “Rio Run,” turns immigration enforcement and deportation into entertainment. Another, “Build the Wall,” talks about a “zombie border siege” and tells players to defend the border from a “coming horde.” I know. It sounds ridiculous. But beneath the surface, it's much more than that. [_**I don’t think we can afford to laugh this stuff off. If you want someone in Congress who will keep calling it out when our government crosses these lines, will you click here and chip in $10, $25, or whatever makes sense for you today?**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138600667/644562896/-925757080?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM0MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2MDZmMzI4ZS1hZmE4LWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTkzM2IiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=3YC-dr5sQ94gx0o_WAjy2y6N9OgQGBhD6ApEKonqbPk=) **[I'M WITH YOU, BECCA!](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138600668/644562897/-925757080?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM0MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2MDZmMzI4ZS1hZmE4LWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTkzM2IiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=3YC-dr5sQ94gx0o_WAjy2y6N9OgQGBhD6ApEKonqbPk=)** Because underneath the arcade graphics and the jokes, there is something serious happening. When our government starts packaging rhetoric about immigrants as entertainment, language and imagery that should shock us can start to feel normal. And that is exactly how the political conversation shifts. We’ve already seen how quickly ugly claims can take hold. In 2024, false allegations spread that Haitian immigrants in Springfield, Ohio were stealing and eating people’s pets. JD Vance helped amplify those claims even though local officials said there was no credible evidence behind them. **They're testing what we are willing to accept in our political discourse. That's why I don’t think we can shrug, roll our eyes, and move on every time something like this happens.** Over the past year, I’ve traveled to Chicago and Minnesota as part of congressional oversight of ICE operations, and I’ve kept pressing the Department of Homeland Security for answers about how immigration enforcement is being carried out. So yes, I’m paying attention to this. [_**And I’m going to keep asking questions, demanding accountability, and refusing to let cruelty become just another normal part of our politics. And if you want me to keep doing that work, I hope you’ll chip in today and help me keep fighting!**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138600669/644562898/-925757080?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM0MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2MDZmMzI4ZS1hZmE4LWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTkzM2IiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=3YC-dr5sQ94gx0o_WAjy2y6N9OgQGBhD6ApEKonqbPk=) I don’t want us to ever get to a place where dehumanizing language becomes background noise and we barely notice anymore because we’ve heard it all before. We should notice. We should push back. **And we should expect better from the people running our government.** Thanks for being in this with me, — Becca

subject: Judicial Watch: Unseal Rudy Giuliani Seizure Records
body:
Navy Wastes $3.4 Billion on Inoperable Submarines

[INSIDE JW]

JUDICIAL WATCH: UNSEAL RECORDS OF SEIZURE OF RUDY GIULIANI’S PHONE
AND EMAIL!

[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=85166&L=38602&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cueW91dHViZS5jb20vd2F0Y2g/dj0yOVVncjZROUNpMCZ1dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&hash=650fb07de514f6d7a057110a7501e52916b8df4d35f72f5d9a12b76a02b69d77]

With former New York City Mayor Rudy Giuliani we filed a motion
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=85166&L=38588&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2dpdWxpYW5pLW1vdGlvbi10by11bnNlYWwtMjAyNi8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnMmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9Q01qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNE&hash=0a32ff404dc2c4f9a4643c2e932b1d5fa57fea9c8c2f31e117b4aa7f9fc38c54]
asking the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York
to unseal materials related to two search warrants issued by the Biden
Justice Department targeting Giuliani’s electronic information and
telephone records.

The warrants authorized the government to seize and search
Giuliani’s iCloud account and obtain prospective and historical
location information for two telephone numbers assigned to him (_In re
Search Warrants Executed on April 28, 2021_ (No. 21-mc-00425 (JPO)).

Giuliani, a longtime attorney and adviser to President Donald J.
Trump, served as U.S. associate attorney general from 1981 to 1983 and
U.S. attorney for the Southern District of New York from 1983 to 1989.
He was elected mayor of New York in 1994 and served until 2001.

The motion, filed before U.S. District Judge J. Paul Oetken, seeks
materials related to:

> 1. November 4, 2019 – Warrant to search iCloud account belonging
> to Mayor Giuliani; and

> 2. April 13, 2021 – Warrant for prospective and historical
> location information for two telephone numbers assigned to Mayor
> Giuliani.

We are asking the court to unseal the materials under the common-law
right of access to judicial records, the First Amendment, and
Giuliani’s right to access judicial records under the Warrant Clause
of the Fourth Amendment. The motion argues that the warrant materials
are judicial records subject to a presumption of public access and
that no compelling governmental interest justifies their continued
sealing.

In our motion, we state: “Judicial Watch is investigating the
potential politicization of numerous federal law enforcement agencies
and whether they abused their powers to attack associates of a
political opponent.”

The motion points out that “[a] similar request was previously
granted pursuant to an application from The New York Times.... As
Mayor Giuliani is a direct party in interest, the bases for disclosure
are even greater in this instance.”

The motion argues that the presumption of public access outweighs any
countervailing interests:

> The records are being sought to enhance the public’s understanding
> of the United States’ targeting of President Trump’s attorney by
> the Biden administration. The public has a real interest in knowing
> the evidence underlying the search warrant application and whether
> the warrant was sought for legitimate law enforcement purposes
> rather than to target a political opponent's ally.

***

> There is no ongoing prosecution that disclosure could jeopardize, no
> witness whose safety is at risk, and no trial whose fairness could
> be compromised.

The motion asserts that Giuliani cannot determine whether “the
warrant that authorized the search was constitutionally defective
without first seeing the materials ...”

> because they are no longer certified to conduct normal operations

> inactive idle time for attack submarines. This is when a sub
> designated for decommissioning cannot be inducted into a dry dock in

> pier-side until a shipyard has the capacity in a dry dock to defuel
> their nuclear reactor,” according to the GAO.

> time. Although this technically differs from active idle time when
> operational subs wait for maintenance, both are tremendously
> inefficient, drain taxpayer resources and slash the number of
> submarines available for deployment. In the period examined, fiscal
> year 2016 through 2025, the maintenance delays wasted huge amounts
> of public funds to sustain both crews and submarines that provided

The warrants authorized the government to seize and search Giuliani’s iCloud account and obtain prospective and historical location information for two telephone numbers assigned to him (In re Search Warrants Executed on April 28, 2021 (No. 21-mc-00425 (JPO)). Giuliani, a longtime attorney and adviser to President Donald J. Trump, served as U.S. associate attorney general from 1981 to 1983 and U.S. attorney for the Southern District of New York from 1983 to 1989. He was elected mayor of New York in 1994 and served until 2001. The motion, filed before U.S. District Judge J. Paul Oetken, seeks materials related to: 1. November 4, 2019 – Warrant to search iCloud account belonging to Mayor Giuliani; and 2. April 13, 2021 – Warrant for prospective and historical location information for two telephone numbers assigned to Mayor Giuliani. We are asking the court to unseal the materials under the common-law right of access to judicial records, the First Amendment, and Giuliani’s right to access judicial records under the Warrant Clause of the Fourth Amendment. The motion argues that the warrant materials are judicial records subject to a presumption of public access and that no compelling governmental interest justifies their continued sealing. In our motion, we state: “Judicial Watch is investigating the potential politicization of numerous federal law enforcement agencies and whether they abused their powers to attack associates of a political opponent.” The motion points out that “[a] similar request was previously granted pursuant to an application from The New York Times.... As Mayor Giuliani is a direct party in interest, the bases for disclosure are even greater in this instance.” The motion argues that the presumption of public access outweighs any countervailing interests: The records are being sought to enhance the public’s understanding of the United States’ targeting of President Trump’s attorney by the Biden administration. The public has a real interest in knowing the evidence underlying the search warrant application and whether the warrant was sought for legitimate law enforcement purposes rather than to target a political opponent's ally. There is no ongoing prosecution that disclosure could jeopardize, no witness whose safety is at risk, and no trial whose fairness could be compromised. The motion asserts that Giuliani cannot determine whether “the warrant that authorized the search was constitutionally defective without first seeing the materials ...” On April 28, 2021, at approximately 6 a.m., federal agents executed search warrants [] at Giuliani’s Manhattan apartment and his office, seizing his cellphone and other electronic devices. Agents reportedly seized additional materials, including a computer used by longtime assistant Jo Ann Zafonte. We previously filed a Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) lawsuit [] [ the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia after the Justice Department failed to respond to a February 2026 FOIA request. The request, which included a signed certification of identity from Giuliani himself, seeks all records related to the April 2021 search warrants. The American people have a right to know why the federal government secretly targeted America’s Mayor Rudy Giuliani and what evidence was used to justify these searches. Giuliani was never charged with a federal crime, yet the government has kept the warrant materials hidden. Trump, filed a motion [] asking the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York to unseal the search warrant materials related to three search warrants targeting Toensing’s iCloud account, Gmail account, and cell phone (In re Search Warrants Executed on April 28, 2021 (No. 21-mc-00425 (JPO))). We also moved to unseal [] the search warrant materials related to a November 18, 2024, warrant that authorized the federal government to seize the entire Google account of Michael Caputo, a longtime ally and policy adviser to President Donald J. Trump. In April 2026, we obtained records [] revealing the FBI’s concerns about the legal basis for the raid of then-former President Donald J. Trump’s Mar-a-Lago home. The records expose deep concerns within the FBI itself, including explicit objections from field agents who warned the U.S. Department of Justice that the unprecedented August 8, 2022, raid on Trump’s home lacked probable cause. In June 2023, we uncovered records [] from the Justice Department that show top officials of the National Security Division discussing the political implications of Trump allowing CNN to use closed-circuit TV (CCTV) footage of the raid on his Mar-a-Lago home. In September 2022, we filed [] lawsuits against the DOJ for its records and the FBI’s records about the Mar-a-Lago raid search warrant application and approval, as well as communications about the warrant between the FBI, Executive Office of the President and the Secret Service. Ethan Leonard and Neal Brickman of the Brickman Law Group in New York, New York are representing Judicial Watch and Giuliani in this matter. NAVY WASTES $3.4 BILLION TO SUSTAIN SUBMARINES WITH "NO OPERATIONAL CAPABILITY" While the Trump administration can be commended for its support of our military, one part of the War Department is falling behind. Our Corruption Chronicles blog explains []. Adding to the pain of a staggering $40 trillion national debt [], which undoubtedly includes wasteful government spending and failed projects, a new federal audit [] reveals the U.S. Navy has wasted billions of taxpayer dollars to sustain idle submarines and crews that “provide no operational capability.” The scandal involves the country’s fleet of submarines, critical to national defense because they carry out Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance (ISR) missions, project power ashore with Tomahawk cruise missiles and support battle group operations. As of fiscal year 2025, the Navy has 44 attack submarines, according to the probe, recently published by the Government Accountability Office (GAO), the investigative arm of Congress, and the vessels are some of the most requested assets by global combatant commanders. However, in the last 10 years the Navy has lost over 15,000 operational days and an estimated $3.4 billion because maintenance delays have kept active attack submarines idle. “Lost operational days include delays completing depot maintenance and active idle time,” the GAO report states. “Active idle time describes a period when an attack submarine and its crew must remain pier-side because they are no longer certified to conduct normal operations and cannot be inducted into a maintenance period.” The probe also found that the Navy faces “significant challenges” managing inactive idle time for attack submarines. This is when a sub designated for decommissioning cannot be inducted into a dry dock in a shipyard. “As a result, the submarine and its crew must remain pier-side until a shipyard has the capacity in a dry dock to defuel their nuclear reactor,” according to the GAO. The Navy’s 44 active attack submarines need access to shipyards for maintenance and repairs, but the constant backlog of older vessels that have been designated for decommissioning block access to the dry docks creating a serious holding pattern known as idle time. Although this technically differs from active idle time when operational subs wait for maintenance, both are tremendously inefficient, drain taxpayer resources and slash the number of submarines available for deployment. In the period examined, fiscal year 2016 through 2025, the maintenance delays wasted huge amounts of public funds to sustain both crews and submarines that provided no operational capability and contributed nothing to national defense. “Inactive idle time for submarines has grown and is projected to worsen,” the GAO confirms, adding that “without mitigation, 15 attack submarines will enter inactive idle time from fiscal year 2026 through fiscal year 2030.” During that time the Navy could incur over 14,000 days of inactive idle time and $3.1 billion in costs to operate and support the inactive submarines, the probe found. The attack submarines get serviced at four aging public facilities— Portsmouth Naval Shipyard, Norfolk Naval Shipyard, Puget Sound Naval Shipyard, and Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard—described by the Navy as “ [ [ [ inefficient. The work is very involved and time-consuming and includes overhauls, alterations, refits, restorations and nuclear refueling. GAO investigators determined that the costly maintenance backlog has persisted since at least fiscal year 2008 with no improvement in site. “Further, the U.S. Navy only completed about 11 percent of attack submarine depot maintenance on time at the public shipyards, from fiscal years 2016 through 2025,” the report states. It appears that the Navy is not that concerned about the problem and hasn’t even bothered to fully evaluate alternative options to more efficiently decommission attack submarines and develop and implement an inactivation plan that could allow it to reduce inactive idle time for crews to save billions. Congressional investigators reveal that they made two common-sense recommendations, that the Navy decommission attack subs more efficiently and develop a plan to reduce inactive idle time. Seemingly dismissive of the GAO’s findings, the Navy “verbally concurred” with the watchdog’s recommendations but did not bother to provide written comments as is customary after getting slammed in a federal audit. It also failed to disclose when it will make changes to its inefficient, decades-long system that continues fleecing American taxpayers out of huge sums amid record-breaking national debt. #
I’m proud to endorse Angie Nixon for Senate.
I’d like to share more about why I am supporting Angie but first: _[please split a contribution between our campaigns today.](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20260904-nixon.jYUtuE&refcode=em20260904-12232-P_FND_SPL_END&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=3&akid=12232%2E2526796%2EpVIdzN)_
Angie Nixon is a Florida State Representative, union organizer, and mother. She was born and raised in Jacksonville and has dedicated her career to the fight for hardworking Floridians.
Angie knows what’s at stake because she’s lived it — watching her mom work two jobs to get by, attending underfunded public schools. She brought that lived experience to the Florida State House, where she expanded childcare and fought against price gouging.
Angie did not secure the Democratic nomination by yielding to major political machines; she did it by building community and fiercely committing to her values.
**She won despite being outspent 16:1 in the primary.**
Now, on November 3rd, Angie Nixon will be up against incumbent Republican Senator Ashley Moody — a rubber stamp for Trump’s agenda. Ashley Moody is an extremist who voted to expand funding for ICE and for cuts to Medicaid under Trump’s One Big Beautiful Bill. She also introduced a piece of legislation aimed at restricting access to reproductive healthcare.
Angie has 60 days left to reach and turn out millions of voters up and down Florida. Her campaign needs the resources for sending mailers, running ads, paying staff and more.
Like me, Angie rejects all corporate PAC donations, so she’s truly counting on our grassroots support to win.
[ So, I’m personally asking: Will you please split a $5 donation between our campaigns today? Every donation will help Angie reach the voters needed to win and keep our progressive movement strong.](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20260904-nixon.jYUtuE&refcode=em20260904-12232-P_FND_SPL_END&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=4&akid=12232%2E2526796%2EpVIdzN)

**[Contribute $5](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20260904-nixon.jYUtuE&refcode=em20260904-12232-P_FND_SPL_END&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=24&akid=12232%2E2526796%2EpVIdzN)**
Angie can win. But only if we all get behind her. Let’s do this.
Pa’lante,
Alexandria

# Meet Virginia McIntyre
A New Voice for New York’s 25th District Dear Neighbor, I’m Virginia McIntyre, and I’m running to represent New York’s 25th Congressional District. As a Monroe County Legislator, educator, and lifelong member of this community, I've seen firsthand how government waste, public-safety concerns, rising healthcare and utility costs, and political division are affecting families here. I’m running for Congress to bring practical, accountable leadership to Washington and make sure the voices of Monroe and Ontario Counties are heard. |
## My priorities include:
✓ Making Affordability a Priority ✓ Protecting taxpayers and demanding responsible spending ✓ Fighting to reduce the costs of healthcare and utilities ✓ Supporting law enforcement and safer communities ✓ Strengthening education and career opportunities ✓ Actively Engaging with the Community Year-Round ✓ Working across party lines to deliver results
---
For too long, Washington has been more focused on partisan politics than solving the problems people face every day. I believe our representative should listen, show up, and put the people of our district first.
This campaign is about returning power to the people and electing a representative who will work for you—not the political machine.
I invite you to visit our website to learn more about my background, our priorities, and our plan to bring practical, accountable leadership to Washington.

Peter, Something is wrong when a member of Congress treats his office like a trading desk instead of a place to represent families. Let’s go through the facts: On May 15, 2025, Congressman Rob Bresnahan sold up to $130,000 in stocks tied to health insurers like Centene, Elevance Health, UnitedHealth, and CVS Health. One week later, on May 22, he was the deciding vote for a Republican mega bill that slashed Medicaid funding by nearly $1 trillion. **Centene’s stock plunged 40% after the bill was signed into law.** That same May 15, Bresnahan bought Lockheed Martin stock. On June 13, 2025, war with Iran escalated and the U.S. launched strikes on Iran. **Those market moves lined up with votes and developments that raise real questions about whose interests he is serving.** In January 2026, a report named 10 rural Pennsylvania hospitals at immediate risk of closure, in part because of the Medicaid cuts he supported. **On March 27, Bresnahan dumped up to $250,000 of Pennsylvania hospital bonds just one month after voting for the budget resolution that paved the way for those cuts.** In May 2025 he made 81 trades selling clean energy holdings and buying fossil fuel stocks in moves worth at least $200,000 and as much as $1.45 million. **Just ten days later he voted for a bill that helps big oil and hurts clean energy and working families facing higher energy bills.** This is not a one-off pattern. Bresnahan ranks as the second-most active trader this Congress. He has made over 652 trades totaling $8.48 million in volume. **The numbers speak for themselves: Bresnahan isn’t in Congress to serve us, he’s serving himself while profiting off of people’s pain.** **I ran for public office to clean up a culture of corruption and make government work for real people. Now, I’m running for Congress to bring that same fight to Washington. I support banning Congressional stock trading, I won’t take corporate PAC money, and I will demand accountability and transparency in government.** [**We need to expose these conflicts and build the resources to win this seat. Beto’s traveling throughout Texas to visit every major college campus before Election Day on November 3rd. His goal? To reach, register and turn out as many new Democratic voters as possible.
Here's why this matters:
* We have the second youngest median age of any state
* There were roughly 1.3 million Texans ages 18 to 24 registered to vote in 2020
* Young voters have historically had lower turnout rates than other age groups

clean_body: Peter, I'm going to make a prediction... When the votes are counted this November, the radical left is going to be in a state of total shock. And the political establishment is going to spend weeks trying to explain what hit them. But that only happens if Republicans like you are on record before the Midterms. That is how consequential this moment is. But here is the part the pundits won't tell you. None of that happens automatically. The Democrats are at war with the American people -- open borders, defunding ICE, eliminating voter ID, putting men in women's sports. You name it, they are on the wrong side of it. And yet they are running the most radical, well-funded Senate candidates in states across this country who are counting on Republicans to stay home and let them walk right in. I will not let that happen. And I don't think you will either. I made you a prediction at the beginning of this email. I stand by every word of it. But that prediction is built on one assumption -- that Republicans like you are engaged and ready to fight. That is where your assessment comes in. Sincerely, Newt Gingrich Former Speaker of the House | Paid for by the NRSC. Not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee. |

body:

Peter,

Eight years ago today, Ayanna won her first primary — unseating a ten-term
incumbent as a fearless, first-time candidate with a movement behind her.

This past Tuesday, she secured the Democratic nomination for
Massachusetts' 7th Congressional District again, and is headed to the
general election to keep delivering for her people.

Ayanna has fought for bold, transformative change. Time and again, she’s
stood up for what her community deserves — abortion access, canceling
student debt, housing justice — and has secured over $35 million in
federal funding for local job training, health centers, transit
improvements, and climate resilience.

Her leadership goes beyond policy, and she's working to confront extremism
directly, no matter what. Recently, she called out Republicans for their
attack on birthright citizenship, exposing their attempt to “codify” the
“Great Replacement Theory” into law — labeling it an assault on democracy.

That’s the kind of fearless leadership we need in Congress, someone who
won’t back down from the tough fights to protect our communities.

Ayanna’s ready to continue the work: building an economy that serves
working families, ensuring immigration policies are rooted in dignity,
securing the schools every child deserves, and advocating for
diplomacy-first foreign policy instead of endless war.

With less than nine weeks until Election Day, entrenched powers are doing
everything they can to weaken our movement. But we know we can fight back
with the power of this grassroots team on our side.

That’s why I’m asking for your support today -- and that’s why my team set up a personal link for you to use, so I know it’s coming directly from you: I know this team has never backed down when the stakes are this high -- so thank you for your support. Elevate, Wes

body:
| | | |
---
| | | It’s Mary Peltola here with a humble request: Can you please split a $20 contribution between Equal Opportunity Now and my campaign as we begin the general election?
---
[ **CONTRIBUTE NOW TO HELP FLIP THE SENATE!** ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138602128/644567777/916216164?refcode=260904_peltolahumbly&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDUvMS83MzE2OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2NGIxYjU4My1iNmE4LWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTkzM2IiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=CeDZHOxAoCjDYYp3RlLf2ADAQKpNlrurS8HnT4xdhTk=)

I’m sorry to be so upfront because – to be honest – Yup’ik people don’t like asking for money. In fact, I hate it! But I wouldn’t ask if your support wasn’t so important.

Yup’ik people also believe that when we set our mind to something, we can do anything. We use the word **"ikayuquluta"** when we work together to overcome challenges.

I firmly believe that, and I think we're at a point, certainly in Alaska, where we need to rise up and say we expect a Congress that helps all of us and isn't just in it for the millionaires and billionaires.

That means we all have to do our part.

This team has stood by my side since I launched this campaign just a few months ago, and I’m hopeful that today will be no different.

So I have to humbly ask:

[**Can you split a contribution of $20, $50, or whatever you can afford, between Equal Opportunity Now and my campaign to help us win on November 3? With everyone chipping in just a little bit, I know we can get where we need to be.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138602129/644567778/916216164?refcode=260904_peltolahumbly&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDUvMS83MzE2OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2NGIxYjU4My1iNmE4LWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTkzM2IiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=CeDZHOxAoCjDYYp3RlLf2ADAQKpNlrurS8HnT4xdhTk=)**

name: Karl VonZabern
subject: Eric Jones for Congress - Demand a Debate
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Eric Jones for Congress
body:
Happy Friday Everyone,

Now that November is a race between two Democrats, we keep hearing the same fair question at doors and town halls: what actually separates Eric Jones from Congressman Mike Thompson? Sign a debate petition to lay these differences bare.

[Debate Petition — Eric Jones for Congress](https://www.ericjones.us/debate-petition "https://www.ericjones.us/debate-petition")

**Here are some of the major differences between candidates: **
**
**
1\. The Power for the People Act — who pays for the data center boom

Electricity bills in this district keep climbing, and a growing share of new demand on the grid is coming from AI data centers. The Power for the People Act (H.R. 8241) would fix who pays for that: it directs federal regulators to make data centers cover the transmission upgrades they require, rather than spreading those costs across every household on the system.

Sixteen House Democrats have cosponsored it, including our neighbor John Garamendi. Congressman Thompson has not.

Eric supports this bill, and he'd go further: he's called for a moratorium on new data centers in California until our water and electricity systems can handle them. In Congress, that means securing and appropriating funding for water and electricity infrastructure rather than capitulating to big tech. We need to update our water and power infrastructure, not overload it with projects nobody asked for.

2\. ICE — reform inside DHS, or move it out entirely

Both Eric and Congressman Thompson have criticized how ICE is operating. The disagreement is over the fix.

Congressman Thompson's approach works within the current structure: he's introduced legislation to bar ICE agents from wearing masks and to require body cameras. Eric supports those guardrails — but doesn't think they go far enough.

Eric would move ICE out of the Department of Homeland Security and into the Department of Justice. That would end the roughly $70 billion in supplemental funding Trump pushed through last year, and hold agents to the same training and legal standards as every other federal law enforcement officer. If ICE's job is bringing violent criminals to justice, it can do that from DOJ — under real accountability, not a blank check.

Body cameras are a guardrail. Restructuring is a solution.

3\. The Massie Amendment — a vote, or a shrug

On July 15, the House was forced for the first time to vote directly on whether to keep sending military aid to Israel. The amendment would have stripped $3.3 billion in military financing. Democrats split down the middle: 103 voted yes, 98 voted no.

Congressman Thompson was one of ten Democrats who voted "present." He said the amendment was too broadly drafted and that his vote was a protest against Netanyahu's conduct in Gaza.

Eric would have voted yes.

He has been consistent that he will not vote to fund unnecessary foreign wars, and he doesn't believe a vote that consequential is one you sit out. Reasonable people can disagree about that amendment. What voters in this district deserve is an answer.

**Why this matters**

This district was redrawn last year. Nearly half of it is new. Almost a million people have never had the chance to hear directly from the person who represents them in Congress — and in the June primary, a majority of voters chose someone other than the incumbent.

That's why Eric has challenged Congressman Thompson to nine debates, one in every county in the district. Voters should be able to hear both men answer for their own records, in their own words.

If you want that conversation to happen, help us make it impossible to ignore:

Get involved at ericjones.us/volunteer

Thank you for being part of this fight,
**Karl VonZabern, PhD**
**
**
**Regional Field Director**
**Eric Jones For Congress**
**Karl@ericjones.us**
**
**
Paid for by Eric Jones for Congress.

Pete Serrano was sworn in today as the Interim United States Attorney for the Eastern District of Washington. United States Attorney Serrano was appointed to the position by Attorney General Pam Bondi on August 6, 2025. As Interim United States Attorney, Mr. Serrano supervises the prosecution of all federal crimes and the litigation of all civil matters in the Eastern District of Washington in which the United States has an interest. He leads a staff of approximately 79 prosecutors, civil litigators, and support personnel across Eastern Washington.
Prior to his appointment as Interim U.S. Attorney, Mr. Serrano was Mayor of the City of Pasco, Washington. In 2021, Mr. Serrano co-founded the Silent Majority Foundation, a nonprofit organization to fight for civil liberties. Mr. Serrano was Director and the General Counsel for the Foundation. For more about Pete visit him at

As Interim United States Attorney, Mr. Serrano supervises the prosecution of all federal crimes and the litigation of all civil matters in the Eastern District of Washington in which the United States has an interest. He leads a staff of approximately 79 prosecutors, civil litigators, and support personnel across Eastern Washington. Prior to his appointment as Interim U.S. Attorney, Mr. Serrano was Mayor of the City of Pasco, Washington. Let me be honest with you about something.
I'm not supposed to be in this race.
The grandson of a sharecropper? Not supposed to be a viable Senate candidate in Louisiana.
A Black farmer from rural Tensas Parish? Not supposed to compete statewide in the Deep South.
Someone without billionaire backers or a Rolodex full of Washington insiders? Not supposed to have a shot at flipping a Senate seat.
But here we are.
**And MAGA is absolutely shocked.**
They thought Louisiana was locked up. They thought they could focus on defending seats in swing states while the South stayed safely red. They thought a race like ours — a real populist challenge to their grip on power — wasn't possible here.
They were wrong.
Look at what's happening: Democrats flipping Trump districts across the South. MAGA candidates tearing each other apart in primaries. Republican retirements at levels not seen since the Great Depression. Trump's approval cratering over his failed Iran war.
This is a once-in-a-lifetime opening. The kind of moment that doesn't come around often in Louisiana politics.
**_And I believe — deep in my bones — that this is the campaign to meet this moment._**
Not because I'm the most polished politician. Not because I've been planning a Senate run my whole career. But because I understand what working Louisianans need because I've lived their struggles.
I know what it's like to watch costs rise while your income stays flat. I know what it's like to compete against corporations that rig the system against family operations. I know what it's like to worry about whether there will be anything left for the next generation.
That's the authentic economic populism that can win here. Not the fake MAGA version that delivers nothing but culture wars — the real thing that actually fights for working people.
And if we capitalize on this moment — if we show the political world that Louisiana is genuinely winnable — everything changes.
Not just for this race. For the entire map. For what's possible in the South.
But only if we have the resources to compete. And that counts on good folks like you stepping up.

clean_body: MAGA is shocked we're competitive. A Black farmer from rural Louisiana isn't supposed to threaten their Senate seat. But here we are. | | | = Let me be honest with you about something. I'm not supposed to be in this race. The grandson of a sharecropper? Not supposed to be a viable Senate candidate in Louisiana. A Black farmer from rural Tensas Parish? Not supposed to compete statewide in the Deep South. Someone without billionaire backers or a Rolodex full of Washington insiders? Not supposed to have a shot at flipping a Senate seat. But here we are. And MAGA is absolutely shocked. They thought Louisiana was locked up. They thought they could focus on defending seats in swing states while the South stayed safely red. They thought a race like ours — a real populist challenge to their grip on power — wasn't possible here. They were wrong. Look at what's happening: Democrats flipping Trump districts across the South. MAGA candidates tearing each other apart in primaries. Republican retirements at levels not seen since the Great Depression. Trump's approval cratering over his failed Iran war. This is a once-in-a-lifetime opening. The kind of moment that doesn't come around often in Louisiana politics. And I believe — deep in my bones — that this is the campaign to meet this moment. Not because I'm the most polished politician. Not because I've been planning a Senate run my whole career. But because I understand what working Louisianans need because I've lived their struggles. I know what it's like to watch costs rise while your income stays flat. I know what it's like to compete against corporations that rig the system against family operations. I know what it's like to worry about whether there will be anything left for the next generation. That's the authentic economic populism that can win here. Not the fake MAGA version that delivers nothing but culture wars — the real thing that actually fights for working people. And if we capitalize on this moment — if we show the political world that Louisiana is genuinely winnable — everything changes. Not just for this race. For the entire map. For what's possible in the South. But only if we have the resources to compete. And that counts on good folks like you stepping up. = | | = We have the opportunity to pull off something historic in Louisiana that will do a whole lot of good for people here. I couldn’t be more grateful to have you fighting alongside me. **Darline Graham is extraordinary.** She has dedicated nearly 30 years of her life to serving the people of South Carolina — fighting for those with disabilities, building workforce programs, and giving a voice to those who are too often overlooked. She is warm, tough, principled, and ready.

clean_body: Annie Andrews raised $11M and attacked Darline the moment she won. | - Peter, I had the honor of serving alongside Lindsey Graham in the United States Senate. He was a fighter, a patriot, and one of the most dedicated public servants I have ever known. His beloved sister, Darline Graham, won the Republican nomination to carry on his legacy. Before the results were even final, Democrats attacked her. Annie Andrews — the Democrat nominee — sent out a fundraising text to South Carolinians the moment Darline clinched the nomination. Her message? "The Senate isn't the place for on the job training." They couldn't even wait. I know what Democrats did to Lindsey for years — the attacks, the smears, the millions they poured in to try to take his seat. They never broke him. And now they are coming after his sister with the same playbook. Darline Graham is extraordinary. She has dedicated nearly 30 years of her life to serving the people of South Carolina — fighting for those with disabilities, building workforce programs, and giving a voice to those who are too often overlooked. She is warm, tough, principled, and ready. President Trump saw it too. He personally asked Darline to run, **gave her his "Complete and Total Endorsement," and said there would be "nobody better to honor the legacy of her beloved brother, Lindsey." I could not agree more. Darline has and will continue to bring Lindsey's fighting spirit to the Senate and stand with President Trump every single day. She will be a voice for South Carolina values, a defender of our borders, and an unwavering ally in the fight to keep our country great. But Annie Andrews has already raised nearly $11 million. Our national debt just hit **$40 TRILLION** — with a T.

The federal government now spends more than **$1 TRILLION A YEAR** just on interest. Not defense. Not the border. Not a single thing you'll ever see or use. Just for interest. And it's set to double again within the next decade. That's your tax dollars, gone, before Washington spends a cent on anything that matters.

Senator Rick Scott (R-FL) said what conservatives have been saying for decades: **Congress needs to STOP SPENDING and BALANCE THE BUDGET!** He's right, and he's one of the only people in Washington with the guts to say it out loud.

**Here's the part nobody wants to admit: the Fed didn't do this to us._Congress did._ Politicians want to pass the blame to someone else when it's their fault. You cannot print, borrow, and spend $40 trillion and then blame the guys who have to finance it. **

And don't buy the line that we'll "grow our way out of it." That's not a plan. That's Washington-speak to keep spending and hope for the best. It won't work because it can't. This is a spending problem, plain and simple, and they only get fixed one way — by tightening your belt.

Voting for anyone with an R next to their name won't get the job done. Most of these Senators never saw a spending bill they wouldn't vote for. The earmarks keep flowing. The omnibus bills keep passing at 2:00 a.m. What really matters is the kind of Republicans we send to Washington.

This is why **Senate Conservatives Action** exists — to change Washington by changing the people we send there.

We don't back candidates just because they wear a Republican jersey. We back real leaders with the backbone to make the hard decisions, to fight for the policies we desperately need to save this country. **We only back candidates who will say NO to out-of-control spending — NO on the earmarks, NO on the late-night omnibus bills, and NO on business as usual.**
